the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. mr president, the committee on the environment, public health and food safety has adopted a position on the constitution, which highlights the following main points: it is good that the implementation of the three pillars of sustainable development is included among the objectives of the union and that environmental integration and a high level of human protection are recognised. it is a pity that the third part on the policies and functioning of the union is not in line with the principle of sustainable development, particularly in the fields of agriculture, cohesion, transport and trade policies. certain environmental measures, such as those of a fiscal nature and those relating to land use planning, quantitative water management and land use, could be subject to the ordinary legislative procedure but continue to be adopted by the council by unanimity. the adoption of measures to achieve high standards for the quality and safety of medicinal products and medical devices is welcome. measures relating to surveillance, early warning and combating serious crossborder threats to health are also positive and are part of the shared competences of the union and therefore subject to the ordinary legislative procedure. the introduction of a chapter on the democratic life of the union and the principle that these positions should be taken in the most transparent and closest to the citizens are welcome. the importance of the responsibility of the community institutions towards citizens and the possibility of access to the courts for these and their organisations, particularly in the field of the environment, should be emphasized. personally, mr president, i think that what remains to be seen is how the citizens of the union will accept the new constitutional arrangement, how this constitution, which is in some way made from the top down, will be accepted and lived from the bottom up, how the principle of equality of the states and the community method will be strictly enforced in practice. but that answer can only be given by history.
in writing. i congratulate mr nicholson on his excellent work on the recommendation on the extension of the peace programme. the peace programme, launched in 1995, is designed to strengthen peace and reconciliation in northern ireland and the border areas of the republic of ireland. following the success of the peace i programme and in order to continue the projects developed, the berlin council decided in 1999 to extend the programme for a further five years. i support the rapporteur's position that in this region of europe, which has suffered more than thirty years of violence, all efforts to maintain social integration, economic development, employment, urban and rural regeneration and crossborder cooperation should be encouraged. it is therefore essential to extend the implementation of the peace programme for a further 2 years, until the end of 2006, thus coinciding with the programming period of the structural funds and with a proposal to extend the annual community contribution to the international fund for ireland for the same period. the wider objective is to enable the actions financed by these two instruments for ireland to be aligned with the interventions carried out in the region under the eu cohesion fund.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr james nicholson's report on the northern ireland peace programme because i consider it of great importance that the european union should show solidarity with the irish peace process. our solidarity should be expressed by seeking to benefit the wide range of sectors, areas, groups and communities that have been particularly affected by violence, and by encouraging inter-community projects. the management of funding through local-based partnership structures and sector-specific non-governmental organisations will contribute to strengthening the bonds of peace and reconciliation that are fundamental to the stabilisation of northern ireland. i also consider the objective of financial coherence, which is the aim of extending the implementation of the peace programme for another two years, to be essential, since it is aimed at aligning the actions financed by this instrument and the international fund for ireland with the interventions carried out in the region under the eu cohesion fund.
in writing. in a europe which is able to build peace within its borders, phenomena such as those in northern ireland and the basque country are fortunately becoming more and more sporadic. however, given the seriousness of these cases of violence as an attempt to resolve political issues, they should continue to be condemned by the european union in the strongest and most unconditional terms. in the face of the ceasefire initiatives and the initiation of negotiations between the parties to the conflict in northern ireland, i believe that equal commitment should be required when it comes to supporting any initiatives which aim to contribute to the establishment of a lasting peace in those territories. in this context, i consider it advisable to maintain the financial support available to both northern ireland and the contiguous area under the sovereignty of the republic of ireland, and to extend the peace ii programme for two additional years.
mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, the new treaty is a positive step forward from the institutional point of view, as everyone has stressed. the new treaty will make the union stronger, more effective, more democratic and closer to the citizens. but a constitution is first and foremost a com munity of values and a political project. the commission has already started with the constitutionalization of the charter of fundamental rights, aiming at a society which sees itself as a social market economy and where full employment is aimed at. they're not just words. these are the new objectives of the union, enshrined in article 3 of part one of the treaty, which must guide all its actions and policies. for example, article 185 of part iii on monetary policy expressly states that, without prejudice to the objective of price stability, the european system of central banks shall support the general economic policies of the union in order to contribute to the achievement of its objectives as defined in article 3 of part i. the horizontal clauses which frame the union's actions and policies provided for in part iii of the treaty are of particular importance. in articles 115 to 122 of part iii, the different union policies must take account of the promotion of equality between men and women, the protection of the environment and consumers, social rights, in particular employment, and the conditions necessary for public services or services of general economic interest to fulfil their missions. these examples illustrate how the new treaty strengthens the european social model, not by making any retreat from the past but by making new and important advances. it is therefore good news for the reaffirmation of the will that we must live in a society with high social protection and high environmental values.
mr president, among the various reasons for our opposition to this new treaty i would highlight the strengthening of centralism, federalism and the european bureaucracy, the insistence on policies which are becoming unique to all the member states of the union, regardless of their concrete situations, the deepening of neoliberalism and the militarisation of europe. the blind imposition of the stability pact, the european central bank and the single monetary and exchange rate policies in the euro area countries, regardless of the situation in each country, has resulted in the worsening of the social situation, the increase in inequalities resulting from the privatisation of strategic sectors and public services, accompanied by serious attacks on the rights of those who work. we also know the practice of these neoliberal policies in agriculture, fisheries and foreign trade policy, with economic setbacks, unemployment and the destruction of production in ever larger sectors of the countries with the weakest economies. but we cannot equally agree to a campaign to promote the new treaty, which is neither democratic nor pluralistic, based on the arguments of those who support it, forgetting the reasons of those who are against it, because they are fighting for a more democratic social europe, based on the principle of sovereign and equal states and committed to peace.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the real world in which we live is still far from being just and therefore requires a change in the traditional political models. what is new and fascinating about the european constitution is the link between the recognition of a common system of values, democratic values and human rights, and the recognition of a common system of authority; it is this remarkable link between a project of justice and a method of political sharing in the precise sense already indicated by the great philosopher immanuel kant. that is why the european constitution is both an act of political transformation and an act of moral transformation. because it is not satisfied with the common recognition of fundamental values but decides to share them in practice, because it gives way to the norm rather than to permanent negotiation, because it affirms the sovereignty of rights and the sublime dignity of man as the reason and end of european policies, because it articulates a programme of global justice that transcends nationalisms and complements the effectiveness of the internal constitutions of the states, because it brings together the modern european political identity in a system of universal values that welcomes all other identities, because it represents the feeling of belonging to a cosmopolitan and anthropocentric world, because it is the starting signal for a league of peoples in a more rational and more balanced world order, because it is the constitutional homeland in which all countries in europe recognize each other, in the sense of a new europe. i am writing today to the president of the european parliament and to the commissioner for institutional relations to set up a tv channel to broadcast parliament's proceedings and the future public proceedings of the european council to all the countries of the european union on a full-time basis. finally, my tribute to the rapporteurs from vigo and corbett.
mr president, by approving the corbett/mendez de vigo report, the european parliament will be making its last major contribution to the adoption of a constitutional text for europe. the existence of a european constitutional text marks the historic transition from a community of peoples and countries progressively united by ever closer economic ties to a genuine political community united by the desire for a common destiny. fifty years of a policy of prudent small steps have opened the way to a new reality based on common values, values of civilization which express a common european identity based on peace, democracy, human rights and economic and social progress. europe is not being built against the secular reality of the nations of our continent. europe is born of the free and enlightened desire not to allow the past to repeat itself and to ensure that its peoples are able to remain united in their own destiny in a future fraught with challenges. those sovereigntists who blame europe for the erosion of national sovereignty and see in this constitution the materialization of their superstate nightmare are making a profound error of analysis. economic, financial and technological globalisation, the emergence, now or in the future, of new global political and economic powers, are forcing europe to seek solutions that no longer exist at national level in order to defend, deepen and export the humanist project launched in the last century by the post-war social state of law. in a world marked by uncertainty, disorder and deregulation, europe's voice and leadership are increasingly needed by us and by others who follow our example and expect us to intervene on the major issues on the international agenda. but the opponents of this treaty are not the only sovereignty-loving people. others have to denounce it with a stern tone, denouncing its insufficiency and modesty of results or lack of ambition. they are the ones who refuse to recognise the important progress made because they insist on the futile exercise of comparing the constitutional text before us with the idealised versions of their dreams instead of comparing it with the existing treaties and with the nice process in particular.

in writing. the proposal aims to update the minimum amounts of compulsory insurance in the framework of community harmonization in this field in the so-called motor insurance directive. the main difficulty with this proposal is to strike a balance between the need to improve the cover of protection for victims - cover for personal and property damage - in the event of a car accident (which is at a relatively low value) and the reflection of this improvement in risk cover in the increase in insurance premiums, when the 'prices' charged by insurers are not controlled. the general problem of harmonization is also apparent here, where there are different economic realities in each country, which must be taken into account, particularly in the southern countries, such as portugal, which have always had reservations on this matter. portugal has had a transitional period to adapt its national legislation. the common position provides for a new transitional period of five years, which seems more balanced. however, the proposals to increase the minimum amounts to eur 1 million per victim and eur 5 million per claim, irrespective of the number of victims, especially in the second case, are excessive.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report recommendation for second reading manuel medina ortega (a6-0073/2004) - civil liability arising from the use of motor vehicles. the development of the internal market and the growth of community traffic have for years called for an update of the rules in force. the protection of victims of motor vehicle accidents by compulsory insurance had therefore to be updated and strengthened, and greater convergence in the interpretation and application of the directive by the member states had to be ensured. the fifth directive will make it easier to obtain effective and valid motor insurance outside the country of residence and to sell or buy a vehicle in another member state. the text also increases the legal protection of accident victims. i also think it is essential to stress parliament's proposal for a transitional period of up to five years to allow member states to adapt to the minimum coverage amounts.
in writing. motor vehicle liability insurance is of particular importance to european citizens, both as policyholders and as victims of an accident. by updating and improving the protection of victims of road accidents through compulsory insurance; by filling in the gaps and clarifying provisions of the directives in order to ensure greater convergence in their interpretation and application by the member states; and by providing solutions to the problems which frequently arise in order to ensure a more efficient internal market in the field of motor insurance - the draft legislative resolution contributes to the modernisation and updating of european insurance law while at the same time safeguarding the interests of consumers who are now covered by higher cover. the legislative resolution thus reflects the spirit of strengthening the protection of victims of road accidents by making it easier for the injured party to obtain the compensation due. i hope, however, that some final flexibility will prevent a sharp and abrupt increase in insurance premiums. i also think it is of the utmost importance to develop legislative efforts to avoid the use of delaying practices to avoid assuming the liability guaranteed in a risk transfer contract. my vote is in accordance with the consensus reached yesterday at the trialogue.
in writing. this report gives a positive and balanced favourable opinion of the treaty, but it is regrettable that it excludes the opinion of the committee on fisheries of this parliament, the only european forum with specific competence in fisheries which has discussed the amendments introduced to the conservation of marine biological resources. as the committee on fisheries concluded, 'the inclusion of the conservation of marine biological resources in the context of the other exclusive competences of the eu specified in the draft constitution is anomalous and unjustified'. unlike other matters where this treaty has made profound changes, marine biological resources are not an institutional domain reserved for politicians. they concern the maritime communities, fishermen, scientists, environmentalists, who should never have been ignored. i would remind you that a poll of portuguese public opinion found that only 4% of citizens favoured this solution, compared with 86% in favour of a shared or national competence. the conservation of marine biological resources cannot be the exclusive responsibility of anyone. it is a duty of citizenship for all, and first of all for those who have these resources as a way of life, which cannot be ignored by the european institutions and the representatives of the states. i hope that this "unjustified anomaly" will be corrected shortly.
in writing. i welcome the quality of the report on the treaty establishing a constitution for europe. while i regret that the constitution has fallen short of the ambitions of the european parliament and has enshrined controversial issues such as the issue, particularly for madeira and the azores, of the union's exclusive competence in the field of the conservation of marine biological resources, against which various opinions have been expressed in the european convention, as well as the committee on fisheries in its opinion on the constitution, i recognise that it represents a positive commitment and an improvement on the existing treaties, as advocated by the co-rapporteurs, and constitutes an important step towards the realisation of the european project, both from the perspective of the states and european citizens. the treatment accorded by the constitution to the status of the outermost regions is also noteworthy: the possibility of modulating the application of all european policies to the outermost regions is not only maintained and reinforced, but it is also confirmed that this article constitutes a valid and sufficient legal basis for the development of a genuine policy for the outermost regions. i am voting in favour of the adoption of the constitution and calling for its ratification, and i am expressing my commitment to the campaign for its implementation.

in writing. the free world as we know it would be nothing more than a distant mirage if it had not been for the close and cooperative relationship between europe and the united states, which liberated our continent from the totalitarian yoke of nazism and communism. more than a mere historical curiosity, this relationship is today unavoidable and indispensable in the face of the common challenges and opportunities that confront us. i therefore deplore with particular vehemence those who try to turn allies into antagonists or competitors. i believe that the very history that records our common victory today would be a poor judgment of allies who, having defeated their most visible enemies, bet on facing off when the threat becomes diffuse, almost invisible. the fact that we do not always agree should be an incentive to promote dialogue and not to encourage sterile and counterproductive tensions, which only benefit those who have always wanted to see us divided. i am pleased that the same european parliament which has just been swayed by anti-american rhetoric is now showing its responsibility by declaring its willingness to cooperate in solving global problems and to welcome president bush on his next visit to the community institutions. by walking together, we will go further.
in writing. the external debt of developing countries is a mechanism to exploit them and subordinate them to the creditor countries and international financial institutions and the economic interests they represent. it is illegitimate and immoral, because it is a serious obstacle to development, it diverts vast sums from the basic needs of these countries and their peoples, most of whom devote more resources to debt repayment than to the total expenditure on health and education, preventing them from dealing with diseases such as aids and tuberculosis or with problems such as illiteracy, among many others. the debt maintenance is unacceptable. it is noted that the indebted countries have already paid more than seven times what they owed in 1982 and have nevertheless seen their debt increase fourfold. they still have, for the most part, a history of colonial exploitation which makes them creditors rather than debtors to the industrialized countries. the persistence of this situation is all the more incomprehensible after the cancellation of 80% of iraq's debt, imposed by the occupying military power, the usa, and according to calculations of participation in the exploitation of the country's wealth and the lucrative "business" of reconstruction. the cancellation of the external debt of developing countries is therefore essential if a fairer world is to be built.
in writing. the reduction of the debt burden of developing countries is a worthwhile option, which shows - and should show - a genuine desire on the part of the international bodies and the richer countries to contribute actively to the economic growth and development of those countries, and also to a more balanced sharing of the costs of this process. in addition, in contrast to those who advocate the unrestricted opening of frontiers to all immigration, the most correct, effective and just policy is to seek to promote development in the countries most in need, rather than promoting the desertification of their most capable human resources. in this context, it should also be recognised that, as regards the past, in many cases this debt has its origins in reprehensible policy choices; the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this field, including the establishment of a european centre for the development of vocational training (ecvet) and the establishment of a european centre for vocational training (ecvet). i therefore support procedures such as the one in question, which reduce the debt burden of developing countries. but this must be accompanied by the fact that the resources thus freed up will be spent on sustainable development policies, and not on policies which cannot and should not be supported.
in writing. community cooperation policy must promote the economic and social growth of developing countries and their progressive integration into the world economy. it should be borne in mind that the countries to be assisted must receive increased attention, both in terms of improving the processes of democratic consolidation and in terms of progress in respect for human rights. economic growth in developing countries must be people-centred. only in this way will we be able to eradicate poverty and ensure the growth of their economies, in order to reduce their external debt requirements and to meet their obligations. we should welcome the nepad initiative and the measures announced at the g8 summit, because, in addition to being a considerable effort for the economic progress of the developing countries, they are aimed at the promotion and consolidation of democracy, good economic management, the promotion of peace and security in the developing countries. within the framework of the conditions mentioned, i believe that the process of reducing the burden of public debt must be accelerated and deepened, allowing developing countries to allocate resources to basic services and thus achieve the millennium development goals.

the rapporteur. mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the construction of the area of freedom, security and justice is one of the most pressing challenges facing the european union today, and in particular the need to ensure, as we set out in the hague programme, high standards of quality in justice throughout the union, without prejudice to the plurality of legal systems existing in the 25 member states. in accordance with the hague programme, as in tampere, the cornerstone of the construction of the area of freedom, security and justice is mutual recognition, as commissioner frattini reminded us here just a moment ago. but for mutual recognition to exist, it is essential that there be mutual trust. and as our colleague mr di pietro has just pointed out, mutual trust is not a matter of faith. mutual trust requires building and requires its actual existence. the truth is that we have to recognize that among our 25 member states, among the judicial authorities of our 25 member states, that mutual trust does not exist to a sufficient degree. this mutual trust needs to be strengthened. that is why i am starting this own-initiative report by proposing a mechanism for mutual evaluation between the different member states. of course, a mechanism that respects the independence of the judiciary. but a mechanism that involves national parliaments and that involves the judiciary's own management bodies so that we can have a rich assessment of the different views on the quality of criminal justice in each of these member states. secondly, i think it is essential that this assessment be an objective one and in order to be objective i propose the creation of a charter on the quality of criminal justice. a charter of quality which must be constructed on the basis of the interpretation of the right to a judge in the european declaration of human rights, the charter of fundamental rights and in accordance with the case law of the european court of human rights, the court of justice of the european communities, but also the recommendations of the united nations and the council of europe. this quality charter should be an objective reference framework for assessing the different criminal justice systems in the different member states so that we can disseminate good practice, benchmark and have high quality standards for all european citizens anywhere in the union. however, we all know that, in addition to mutual recognition, we cannot do without a minimum degree of harmonization. the council defined the criteria for the harmonization of substantive criminal law. in our report we propose that we should support the council's proposal. the council invited the commission to prepare for harmonization as soon as possible in respect of all the crimes provided for in the constitutional treaty so that, by the time the constitutional treaty enters into force, the preparatory work will have been completed and the council, together with parliament, will be able to adopt rapidly the harmonization rules required by the new treaty. as regards procedural law, we believe that we should be selective, but we should also be ambitious in the scope of our intervention. we therefore propose four key areas. firstly, a matter on which the commission has already announced that it is working, the harmonization of the rules on the establishment and evaluation of the basic evidence. secondly, harmonization to facilitate the enforcement of penalties, but also of the preventive measures to be applied. thirdly, the existence of common minimum rights for prisoners in all member states and, finally, consideration of international recidivism for crimes which have already been harmonised. in this report, parliament calls on the council and the commission to speed up their work so that we can all work together to build an area of freedom, security and justice with a higher quality of criminal justice in europe.
mr president, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, we have a common task to perform in order to improve the standards of quality and efficiency of justice, without forgetting that the cornerstone of our european themes is the independence of the judiciary and the protection of the fundamental rights of citizens, both at the substantive and procedural level. in the event of doubt, if i may do so again, i would like to congratulate mr antónio costa on the excellent report he has presented to us, which argues that the right to justice must be guaranteed to european citizens, either by the union, ensuring that they have comparable treatment regardless of the member state in which they are, or by the member states, in accordance with their respective competences, seeking to avoid the differences between the various judicial systems being an obstacle to achieving a high level of justice and protection in the area of freedom, security and justice. i agree with the rapporteur that it is essential to strengthen mutual trust so as to enable mutual recognition of judicial decisions, contributing to the progressive development of a european judicial culture. i support the idea of adopting a european charter of criminal justice, which should be the basis for assessing the functioning of the judicial systems of the union and for creating a mechanism for mutual evaluation of the quality of justice, objective and impartial, with a statistical and comparable database which should be put into operation as soon as possible and should involve not only the european parliament but also the national parliaments. i also thank mr antonio di pietro for his report and his proposals on shortening the time limits and conditions for access to personal data. the existing system for exchanging criminal records information is not effective. it is essential that a computerised system for the exchange of information between member states be set up, which will allow rapid access to this kind of information throughout the union, and i welcome the new developments made by mr frattini on this subject.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the issue of the quality of criminal justice and the harmonization of criminal legislation is a core issue in the european union's overall justice project. it is in criminal justice that the debate on human rights, their interrelationship, their conflicts, their foundation on an essential principle of dignity, is most dramatically expressed. the criminal question thus appeals to the moral foundations of european political culture and makes it urgent to pursue an active policy of improving the quality of criminal justice and harmonizing the laws of the member states. the emergence of a european constitution, incorporating a binding charter of fundamental rights and constituting a system of values marked by unity and integration, calls for better justice and the harmonization of criminal legislation. it is that criminal law is truly constitutional material law, it summons all the fundamental constitutional values. the absence of harmonization in this area will mean that the principle of equality between citizens is not being respected, and that the constitution is not being respected. that is why the harmonization of the penal system must not be merely a minimum, it must not be merely the basis for mutual recognition of judicial decisions, it must be an end in itself. a concerted policy does not call into question the member states' decisionmaking power in this area just because it is a concerted policy. the system of values of the european constitution also implies that the harmonization of legislation must be transversal to the whole criminal law system. it should not only consider the aspects of the procedure and the execution of sentences, but also the substantive rules, the policy for defining crimes and the criteria for shaping sentences. it must be concerned not only with security but also with the humanization of criminal law. if europe does not embrace this design, its constitutional justice system will eventually be, as kafka ironically put it, a system of open doors into which one never enters.

the stability pact is finally called into question, although belatedly, and only when france and germany have failed to comply with it, as is the case in most of the countries of the european union, because of the deterioration of the economic and social situation. but better late than never. unfortunately, the prospects for the ecofin council on 8 march, when they come to fruition, will mean more of the same. the flexibility in the application of the stability pact would depend on whether a state is more or less able to challenge its public social security and pension systems, its public health systems or, as some point out, the reform of its public administration, i.e. the more a state implements policies and achieves objectives which we consider to be very serious in the lisbon strategy, the more flexibility it would have in the application of the stability pact, which would be unacceptable.
mr president, mr commissioner, at a historical moment when it is becoming increasingly important for europeans to know each other in their human and cultural diversity, the european capitals of culture programme is a very effective instrument for achieving this objective. the new european dimension following the last enlargement fully justifies the designation of two european capitals of culture per year. it is necessary, however, as the european people's party has already had occasion to stress, that community funding be sufficient and appropriate. the european capital of culture is a very prestigious designation, but a city in these conditions is not expected to use the specific community funding to be european capital of culture in urban redevelopment infrastructure works or other similar. the specific funding of the programme is expected to help to highlight its role as a european city and a centre of cultural influence. nor is a european capital of culture expected to become just another international festival, however important it may be. it is expected to provide visitors with a vivid, accurate and evocative picture of the face of the city which receives the title and which thereby makes itself known. and this must be an image enriched by its contributions to european culture and its contributions to europe's relationship with the world, an image which allows us to understand its specific values, its history, its spiritual and material heritage, its traditions and customs, the peculiar way of being of its inhabitants, in a word, its human dimension. i support the prets report and the general views expressed by my predecessors, and i would suggest that the commission should take these points into account in the reforms it will be making in 2005.
in writing. i agree with the report by mr antonio di pietro, which supports and aims to strengthen the commission's initiative to introduce technical improvements in the legislation on the exchange of information extracted from the criminal record, proposing practical solutions to fill the gaps in the existing system (based on the council of europe convention of 1959). this is certainly a necessary and urgent measure, since it has been demonstrated on several occasions that the existing system is not effective. it is therefore essential to set up a computerised system for the exchange of information between member states, which will allow quick access to such information throughout the union. this is another step towards achieving a truly effective, independent and transparent criminal justice system. i also support your proposals on shortening the time limits (as the effectiveness of the proposal will depend on speed, both in terms of access and in terms of updating this data) and the need to impose conditions for access to personal data (as there should always be a balance between the need for speed in this exchange of information and the safeguarding and protection of personal data).
in writing. in a europe of free movement, of free trade, shared security is a necessity. without prejudice to the full exercise of the sovereignty of the different member states, it is now widely recognised that the different countries must cooperate in the fight against crime. it is that, in addition to traditional crime, there is today a crime that does not respect borders, that operates where it sees fit and that by breaking the law of one it jeopardizes the safety of all. i understand that this is the case and i agree with the substance of this report, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. justice is, rightly, one of the elements which the member states have traditionally reserved for the sphere of sovereignty. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. similarly, states are cautious in the way they allow their nationals - even simply their residents - to be judged by other states. on the other hand, there is now a global crime which is transnational in nature - such as terrorism, drug trafficking, smuggling, sexual exploitation or pornography - which requires cooperation to ensure effective crime prevention and harmonization to prevent some countries from becoming crime hotspots. these different aspects lead to the need for cooperation, recognition of judicial decisions and some harmonisation, without, however, losing sight of the fact that legal systems have to respond to the realities of different societies, so that a single european legal system is undesirable. as for a european standard of justice, in full respect of the very nature of the judicial system, this is desirable. i therefore believe that the vote in favour of this report is justified.
in writing. the defence of an economic model based on capitalism, which encourages effort, rewards merit and recognises efficiency, obliges us to defend an effective and efficient system of enforcement of the competition rules. without competition there is no market, without market there is no capitalist model and without capitalist model there is no economic success and development, as history well demonstrates. the community's role in competition supervision is therefore of great importance. without prejudice to the need to safeguard certain activities in the short term or in a certain geographical or sectoral context, competition policy is generally concerned first and foremost with the interests of consumers, who are not usually represented by trade unions, employers' associations or other movements. for this reason, i believe that the effort to protect competition deserves our applause and our agreement, even if we may disagree with some of the decisions taken by the commission. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. on the basis of the principle that it is only the identification of seafarers when they are embarked that is at issue, we agree with the essential point, namely that the seafarer's identification document should be considered a sufficient document and should dispense with any entry visas, particularly in cases of arrivals and stopovers, and also in the cases of transit, transfer or repatriation. moreover, the portuguese seafarer's registration card, in accordance with article 9 of annex i to decree-law no 280/2001 of 23 october 2001, 'may constitute a seafarer's identification document for the purposes of ilo convention no 108', leaving therefore only the question of 'visas', which in our view should not be required. we are therefore generally in favour of the proposals contained in the report. there is, however, one question that needs to be examined. the commission proposal is to propose to the council that the member states be authorized to ratify an ilo convention, thus once again putting national sovereignty at risk, which is something we are opposed to. it should be stressed that france has already ratified this convention, effectively exercising its sovereignty as an independent state, and of course without asking the eu whether it could do so or not.
in writing. since only member states can accede to convention no 185 of the international labour organisation (ilo), the european commission took part in the negotiations as an observer, proposing to the council to authorise member states bound by community rules in this field (council regulation (ec) no 539/2001 of 15 march 2001) to ratify the convention in the interest of the community. although there are some technical reservations (in particular as regards the operability of control by means of biometric data) raised by the rapporteur, i also share his view that, by proposing this council decision, the authorization is being given a symbolic value. by allowing simultaneous ratification by all member states, the importance which the union attaches to this convention is thus confirmed to the rest of the world. i voted yes.

in writing. i voted in favour of the mathieu grosch report on driving licences. protection against fraud, the free movement of drivers and road safety are fundamental to the defence of freedom of movement in the european union. this good idea should not be undermined by excessive regulation, which creates more burdens and difficulties for the motorists for whom it is intended. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods are applied in the member states. it is necessary to avoid that a beneficial and fully justified measure increases regulatory and bureaucratic constraints, creates additional limitations for applicants to drive motorcycles or sets more restrictive conditions for the validity or renewal of driving licences. although none of the amendments i have supported has received the support of the majority of the house, i consider the balance of the text acceptable and therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the multiplicity of types and forms of driving licence which entitle a national of a member state to drive a motor vehicle is a circumstance which, in a community in which freedom of movement is the rule, may affect the supervisory capacity of the authorities of the respective states in a worrying manner, with inevitable costs for legal certainty and road safety. the european network of information on driving licences and the mutual recognition of penalties could be valuable contributions to tackling this situation. the fight against fraud, the free movement of drivers and road safety are the main issues in this area and the aim should be to achieve a convergence of criteria which will make it possible to achieve the same level of reliability from lisbon to nicosia. in my view, such convergence should take account of the principles of subsidiarity, appropriateness and proportionality, avoiding duplication of bureaucracy and creating obstacles to the free movement of persons and goods. i believe that the idea of progressiveness or phased access to certain types of vehicles, particularly motorcycles, can have a positive effect on reducing road accidents among young people and that it is worth considering whether it can be implemented. after all, i voted yes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the renate sommer report because it considers inland navigation to be one of the key elements of intermodality in transport. the eu has a dense network of natural canals and rivers which is not yet fully exploited and which should be exploited given the safe and environmentally friendly nature of this means of transport. the proposal aims to create a european framework for the introduction of inland navigation information services and could contribute to a better and more efficient management of traffic and transport on inland waterways. it is time to ensure the interoperability of these services and to lay the foundations for modern transport chain management. in this way, real-time information clearly increases the competitiveness of the sector. this proposal does not restrict the action of the member states too much and also provides for a considerable reduction in estimation errors and the number of accidents. the new technologies mentioned here can boost the sector and influence the distribution of modes of transport in the economy. the positive role that inland navigation can and should play in intermodal traffic systems, which are a cornerstone of future transport, should therefore be taken into account.
in writing. the commission's proposal is a major effort to reduce road congestion, particularly in the transport of heavy goods in europe, which i have been constantly stressing for a long time. inland navigation is a safe and environmentally friendly means of transport, but unfortunately it represents only about 7% of the goods traffic of the 'old' 15 member states. like inland navigation, cabotage should also be monitored and promoted more closely. more than just sectors to be taken into account, as the commission has defined, both are valid solutions to be promoted and developed. the proposal also sets out a european framework for the introduction of inland navigation information services using modernised information and communication services to improve traffic and transport management on inland waterways. the intermodality projected in european transport policy and the ambition to achieve high levels of environmental protection and quality can only be realised if sectors of activity that embody these same aspirations are given a boost. i hope that this proposal for a directive will be another step towards a genuine long-distance maritime and inland waterway transport strategy, which will be preferred to road transport.

in writing. the implementation of control and inspection measures relating to the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp) in their respective exclusive economic zones is a matter for the member states. we are sceptical about the merits of setting up a community fisheries control agency and think that centralisation at this level clashes with the competences of the member states. it is not by chance that this regulation comes before the publication of the results of a feasibility study by the agency. we therefore vote against the report. this does not invalidate our position that we consider it important to strengthen the coordination of member states in the field of control activities to ensure a more uniform application of the cfp and to combat illegal fishing. or that the community budget should be more closely involved in the investments required to ensure control activities. without prejudice to matters of principle, we cannot but express our disagreement with the representativeness of the management board, its operating model and the excessive weight the european commission assumes in it, particularly in the voting system. as we believe, in the name of the principle of co-management, that the participation of the different representatives of the fisheries sector should be guaranteed.

the textile and clothing industry, although it has lost some weight in recent years at the general level of the european union, continues to be of enormous importance in some countries of the union, and is even the structuring activity of the economy of several regions. as has already been said, since last january the quantitative restrictions on international trade in these products have disappeared. this change, although expected, has a major impact on markets, mainly due to the influence of china, which, ignoring social or environmental concerns, allows its companies to practice exceptionally low prices. two main consequences follow: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of the use of pesticides in the food industry. despite the commitments made by the chinese authorities in recent months to limit their own exports from their country, the fact is that the indicators we have are of the greatest concern to us, and it is therefore appropriate at this stage to ask the following questions: first, how are the commission and the council monitoring developments in this matter, using what instruments to make a permanent assessment of the development of this situation, and secondly, how is the commission prepared to act on the specific safeguard mechanisms, even considering that there is at least the fear that the united states will do so very soon.
the european garment industry is facing a serious crisis. in addition, the crisis is concentrated in some regions which are already disadvantaged and which will now be much more vulnerable. the restructuring of the sector in recent years has led to massive relocations of production and mass redundancies, the overwhelming majority of which are low-skilled women. the balance sheet is known and leaves no room for doubt. in about ten years, a loss of 20 to 25% of industrial units and jobs. the recent opening of the market to china aggravates the situation. i would suggest that the commission should take three types of measures: first, to monitor scrupulously all imports on the community market, without fear of acting through the safeguard clauses. the monitoring system must work and it must work quickly. i do not want to appeal to any kind of protectionism. it would be to go against the winds of history. europe must get used to competing with countries where labour is cheap, but europe cannot accept competition with companies that do not pay for energy, that use slave labour and children and that do not respect intellectual property. secondly, we must monitor the phenomenon of the relocation of textile companies, as well as cases of fraud and of companies which received aid before they closed down. thirdly (a recommendation to the commission), the european textile sector should focus on those points in the value chain where europe has real competitive advantages. this requires the development of a policy which takes account, among other things, of logistics infrastructure, geographical proximity to major markets, the ability to respond to orders within short deadlines, design, quality control, innovation, the use of new materials and new technologies, relations with the major distribution networks, continuing vocational training and support for smes, which remain the majority of companies in the sector. i call on the commission to take note of the fact that this is the way the future of the textile industry in europe will go.
from 1 january to the present, authorised imports of textiles from china have reached, for several textile categories, volumes up to 7 times higher in quantity than the corresponding imports made in 2004. for several items, import licences in these two months have already exceeded the total imports of these same items during the whole of 2004. for almost all products, prices have fallen sharply, some by less than half. in view of the possibility that the commission may lift the safeguard measures provided for in the chinese accession process, i would ask you, commissioner, to clarify: first, what are the consequences of the commission not having yet begun to produce customs data on textile imports; on the other hand, the consequences of the guidelines still to be defined which the commission should have prepared and made available as early as 2004; finally, what assurance can european producers have that the commission is technically and politically capable of acting before it is too late?

mr president, it has been two months since the tsunami tragedy. these two months have certainly been the worst of all time for the many thousands of human beings who have not only lost their families, their homes and their communities, but have been, and sadly continue to be, deprived of their only means of livelihood, especially those who depended on fishing. the commission's proposal is therefore welcome and should be approved by the european parliament after incorporating the proposals for improvement put forward by the pse and other parliamentary groups. the proposal must, however, be assessed realistically and in accordance with its exact size, i.e. it must be seen as a limited, short-term and little more than symbolic response, given that thousands of boats have been destroyed and that this action will hardly replace more than a few dozen, and that there are doubts as to the suitability of the boats for the reality for which they are intended, and that the operationalization of the proposal is becoming very difficult and expensive, especially as regards the transport of the boats. the initiative has the merit of demonstrating that the european union is not indifferent to this aspect of the tragedy. however, solidarity will only be effective if we go further, that is, if adequate support is obtained for the construction and reconstruction of vessels on the spot, in particular small craft boats and gear appropriate to the types of fisheries being fished, by, inter alia, withdrawing a share of the fifg from the appropriations allocated to each member state to ensure their financing. in short, the commission proposal should not be demagogically criticized for being insufficient. first, we must do everything to complete it.
in writing. the report is concerned above all with the effectiveness with which the european union is dealing with its international obligations, in particular those which result from the fact that its member states are all members of the united nations. in this sense, and in view of the legal architecture of the union, this proposal for a council regulation makes perfect sense. on the other hand, the application of sanctions is at issue here, which are intended - and the necessary rigour is expected - to act against those who may represent a threat to the peace and national reconciliation process in côte d'ivoire. the process of peace and national reconciliation is fragile and needs all the international protection that can be given it. moreover, the sanctions provided for here do not affect or are intended to affect the population, but only certain persons, so that their usefulness and fairness must be recognized. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the tsunami disaster has had a huge impact on the fisheries sector in india, indonesia, myanmar, maldives, somalia, sri lanka and thailand. data indicate that thousands of fishermen have died, 110,000 vessels have been destroyed, and the cost to the sector has risen to some eur 400 million, requiring the repair of port infrastructure to cost more than eur 450 million. the scale of the disaster requires serious efforts by the international community to support the reconstruction of this key sector. unfortunately, the proposal to transfer to these countries vessels intended for slaughter in the various member states is a hypocritical example of apparent aid which is not feasible and does not meet local needs. this leads to the unusual situation of no requests from the countries concerned. data show that at the cost of sending these vessels, some 9600 new ones adapted to the fishing situation in these countries could be built. we therefore supported the amendments which aimed to turn this commission proposal into humanitarian aid and the development of the fisheries sector in the countries concerned, providing technical and financial assistance. maintaining the possibility of transfer of vessels if requested and complying with fao criteria. we voted yes to correct a mistake.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, i think that this report is relatively consensual, but that cannot prevent us from looking at some fundamental questions which go beyond the report itself, beyond the eib's own activity. the excellent cooperation between the european parliament and the eib over the past five years has already been mentioned. the eib, as we know, and it is mentioned in the report, is an institution which has been in existence for a long time - since the founding of the communities - but which has only been working in collaboration with the european parliament for five years and this cooperation has resulted, as the rapporteur has said, in fruitful activity and some very important developments. i would therefore say that this relative success story is significant and noteworthy, in that the eib is one of the major financial institutions in europe, set up by the member states with the mission of financing directly or by leveraging private resources the investments and policies needed to achieve the main objectives set out in the treaties. the report under consideration takes note of this, of course, but it mainly sets out the bank's activities in a dynamic perspective, recognising that the effectiveness of its actions and the improvement of the transparency of its operation must gradually improve in parallel with the debate in parliament. it must be acknowledged that the bank's activities have been progressively adapted to the concrete circumstances and the european economic environment and that this adaptation has been made by the institution without prejudice to the full and respectful fulfilment of its real mandate. it is therefore easy to identify a set of principles and rules, or if you will, suggestions, which the bank should follow to strengthen its activity and which will help to understand its action better and will certainly help to build better intervention in the future. the first is that this institution can and must play an increasing role in the development of the european economy, particularly in times of recession, by directing its resources and policies towards economic growth and cohesion. the second principle is that the eib has a major multiplier effect in mobilising private or quasi-public resources, by encouraging the participation of all economic operators on acceptable risk terms, either through risk capital operations or through the granting of guarantees. the third idea is that it is also the bank's responsibility to assess the effective contribution of its policy to the lisbon strategy, which means that the bank should take care to measure the results of its actions from this perspective and immediately make them known to public opinion. the fourth principle is that the bank's activities must have a concrete and measurable effect on job creation and a positive and favourable impact on the economic environment which also limits and conditions the full development of small and mediumsized enterprises. the fifth idea is that, as the bank is responsible for supporting the european economy as a whole, it should give particular importance to supporting scientific research and high-technology sectors. the sixth principle is that all this is not incompatible, but on the contrary, with the eib's constant commitment to transparency and accountability of its action, which is demanded by public opinion and has been built up in dialogue with the european parliament. mr president, mr lipietz has put forward a very sensible initial proposal and it has made it possible to draw up a final report of a high quality and a broad consensus which i believe deserves the support of this house.
