mr president, women continue to be the main victims of discrimination, unemployment, violence, poverty and social exclusion and are excluded from representative participation in decision-making and power. that is why the celebration of 8 march, international women's day, a day of struggle for the human rights of women, who are an integral, inalienable and indivisible part of universal human rights, still disturbs many politicians and many governments, as happened in turkey, with police violence against a demonstration of women and even more unacceptable, because it is a country that wants to join the european union. it is unacceptable that unemployment continues to rise in the member states because of increasingly neoliberal policies, that precarious work is rampant in the name of labour flexibility and competitiveness, that wage discrimination persists, that human trafficking and prostitution persist, that violence is the daily reality of millions of women in the european union without adequate measures being taken to change the situation. it is also unacceptable that sexual and reproductive health and rights, guaranteed in the beijing platform for action, continue to be called into question, as in portugal, where women accused of illegal abortion have been subjected to the vexation of trials in court and threats of imprisonment of up to three years for upholding an unjust and unjust law, which is a real attack on women's dignity. let this debate therefore contribute to further progress in the solidarity struggle for women's rights.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the social situation is known to be worsening and is already very worrying, with almost 20 million unemployed and some 70 million people living below the poverty line, particularly women, the elderly and children. as for unemployment, with an average rate of around 9%, although it reaches 10% for women and over 18% for young people, the situation is particularly serious in poland, with almost 19% unemployment, followed by slovakia, lithuania and spain. but in other countries, such as portugal, there are regions where the unemployment rate is very high due to increasing deindustrialization, the relocation of multinationals, the privatization of public sectors and services. however, existing employment is becoming more precarious and women are the main victims of precariousness. on average in the european union, only one in three full-time and permanent jobs is held by women, who also continue to be victims of direct and indirect wage discrimination, with pay differences ranging on average from 16% to 30%, and in some countries even higher. this situation shows that the strategies defined for the growth of quality employment with rights are not enough, because in the name of competitiveness the dogmas of neoliberalism, the priorities of the european central bank, the irrational application of the nominal convergence criteria of the stability pact, the acceleration of liberalization and privatization, flexibility and labour deregulation have been insisted on. the stability pact must therefore be repealed and replaced by a genuine development and employment pact that gives priority to the growth of quality jobs with rights, that focuses on the thorough revision of the lisbon strategy, eliminating liberalisation and labour deregulation, giving full priority to employment with rights and social inclusion. it is noted that some 22 million new jobs with entitlements are needed to achieve the 70% target for overall employment set in lisbon in 2010. otherwise, instead of moving towards economic, social and territorial cohesion, we have a worsening of inequalities, whether between countries or within population strata. we already have several member states with average per capita incomes below 51% of the community average and 10 countries, however, with values above 100% of the european union average. on the other hand, the top 20% of the population receive five times as much as the bottom 20%, although this indicator varies between 3% in denmark and 6.5% in portugal and has worsened in recent years. these inequalities cannot continue when 15% of the population of the european union is at risk of poverty and in some countries this situation reaches 20% or more, as in portugal, greece and ireland. only social protection and social security benefits prevent this situation from worsening. without social transfers, including pensions and other support, the risk of poverty would on average reach 30% of the population in finland, 37% in portugal, 40% in france and the united kingdom and 42% in italy. with the increase in unemployment in recent times and the decline in social support in some member states, the situation of poverty and social exclusion is probably even more serious than the statistics show, which raises the question of the priority to be given to social inclusion in the various community policies, and in particular in monetary and internal market policy, in order to defend quality public services. the commission must therefore withdraw its proposal for a directive on the creation of the internal market in services and not insist on new regulations on the organization of working time. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a welcome step towards the creation of a european company registering as a member of the european union. the new social policy agenda cannot be a mere collection of words and statements without practical content. i hope that there will be a debate on these issues. i thank all those who contributed to the preparation of this report and i hope that it will be adopted, without the amendments envisaged in some of the proposals put forward by members of the epp and the liberals, because we need more employment, more social inclusion so that this european union can talk about economic and social cohesion without just listing empty words, but that it can move towards a reality of better well-being for all.
the commission has already made a number of proposals. the report we are given on the social situation in europe is a blatant distortion of reality. i therefore think that this is an unbalanced report. the text emphasizes all the negative aspects, which we recognize still exist in terms of social exclusion, unemployment and the existence of poverty spots, but at the same time it deliberately ignores all the aspects mentioned by the commission. where it highlights the positive aspects, one can also identify a development in the social situation in europe. i'll mention five missions that i consider serious; first, it is omitted that during the last decade most of the 25 member states have made progress in employment, output growth and cohesion. secondly, the commission's statement that the totalitarian regimes in eight of the new ten member states are the main cause of the social problems is deliberately omitted. thirdly, there is not a single word about the opportunities that will open up for the new member states with accession to the european union. fourthly, the report ignores all the complexity that results from the phenomenon of globalisation. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we believe the opposite, that economic dynamism, price stability and cost reduction are not enemies but allies of the development of the european social model. in short, the text of the report under consideration gives a very reductive view of the european social reality, with the intention of some demagogy. moreover, symptomatic of the ideological influence of the report is the fact that at no point is the proven superiority of the social market economy over planned economy models recognised.
on behalf of the pse group. i would like to begin by greeting commissioner mandelson. the generalized system of preferences has been an important instrument in supporting developing countries by stimulating their participation in world trade. this openness stems from the responsibility of the european union as the world's leading trading bloc and is inconsistent with the positions taken in the world trade organisation and the dahoa process. since last january, within the framework of the wto, imports from china in particular have been entering the european area without barriers. perhaps too aggressively. i say perhaps because i must take this opportunity to regret that neither the guidelines nor the actual import measurement systems are available, although they are a commission commitment for 2004. in the meantime, i welcome the european union's rapid response to the dramatic consequences of the tsunami. the amendment of the rules of origin which is now under way will also strengthen the opening up of the european market to textile exports from developing countries. subjecting the world's poorest countries to the combined and simultaneous effect of the liberalisation of textile imports from china and to a not sufficiently selective treatment that would welcome major world textile powers such as india under preferential treatment would probably mean the break-up and the final disaggregation of these economies and regions. i am sorry to hear that commissioner mandelson is not sensitive to this problem. the perverse effect of the stronger countries crushing the weaker ones once and for all, under the instrument which was intended precisely to support their development, must be considered and analysed, but it is also essential in europe that the opening up of low-cost countries to textile imports be accompanied by reciprocity on the part of the beneficiary countries and the gradual adoption of fairer trade rules in social, environmental and intellectual property terms, as proposed by the high level textile group. let us be clear: while it is true that rapid adaptation of the european textile regions is indispensable, it is necessary to prevent this adaptation from turning into a sudden breakdown of the economic and social structure in the european textile regions, with very serious consequences, particularly in terms of unemployment.
i would like to say that there are some translation problems in some language versions and i would therefore ask the bureau to take into account the french version of paragraph 5 and the portuguese version of paragraph 8 and recital m.
in writing. an open economy requires clear regulation, which is enforceable and designed to be verifiable and enforceable. in the matter at hand - the conditions of access to the natural gas transmission networks - it is important to ensure non-discrimination in order to ensure that the internal market functions properly. in view of these concerns, i should like to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. the internal market in natural gas can only function effectively if network access conditions across the single market meet certain minimum standards with regard to the fundamental aspects of third party access. these rules are essential to ensure fair and balanced conditions and to enable new market entrants, and in particular small enterprises, to exploit business opportunities. conditions for access to the network should not discriminate between network users of different scale, as this could lead to distortion of competition and in any event would prevent gas consumers from benefiting equitably from the internal market in natural gas. the measures now adopted provide users requesting access to the network with a sufficient level of transparency to enable them to conduct their business, otherwise business opportunities arising from market developments in the short and long term could not be exploited. the amendments to the regulation are aimed at promoting non-discrimination and competition by clarifying basic principles, which is why i voted in favour of the compromise amendments (block 1) and i am glad that this can lead to the adoption of the regulation.
in writing. the european union cannot be just an area of free movement of capital, goods and services. europe must also offer the possibility of residing, working and moving freely without prejudice to the rights of its citizens. regulation 1408/71 plays an important role in achieving this objective. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation for second reading on the common position adopted by the council. regulation 1408/71, which came into force more than three decades ago, sets out the basis on which citizens moving between two member states may receive social benefits. the revision of the current regulation contains several new provisions to strengthen social security rights and allows for the determination of whether a citizen retains his right to specific benefits established by the home member state and which are exportable or whether he will have access to an equivalent benefit in his new member state of residence. however, i regret that the council did not agree to the inclusion of five benefits for disabled people and their families. these should be taken into account in the next revision of the regulation.
in writing. although this is a second reading and therefore there will be no final vote, i think it is useful to explain why i voted against the proposal to reject the common position. as portugal has argued, and in view of the position of the european court of justice, it is essential that the content of annex ii a to regulation 1408/71 be deleted in order to ensure the exportability of certain benefits which are of the greatest relevance to the interests of portuguese emigrants, since if these special non-contributory benefits were included there, they could not be exported, thus causing serious damage to our emigrants.
in writing. the freedom of movement of workers within the union is somewhat limited by the fact that the member states advocate different interpretations and formulae of social security schemes, which is natural in a community which is plural and not centralised. i do, however, recognise the need to establish a basis which will enable a citizen of one member state to move and reside in another without thereby being completely deprived of the social guarantees and benefits to which he was previously entitled. unfortunately, the 'exportability' of five non-contributory benefits (childcare allowance, invalidity allowance and allowance for the care of a disabled child, maintenance allowance for a disabled person, for permanent care and for assistance provided to a dependent person) remains controversial, a hypothesis regrettably denied by some countries (finland, sweden and the united kingdom), in contravention of the principle of the extra-territorial payment of benefits (article 42 of the treaty) and prejudicing workers returning to their countries of origin. it may be for the court of justice to decide on this matter, as the commission may so declare. in line with the portuguese government's position, i voted against amendment no 2, which would mean the rejection of the common position, and in favour of amendment no 1, which takes note of the statement made by the commission on the possible clarifying appeal to the court of justice.
in writing. in the light of the european parliament's proposed amendments to the european commission's proposal, it will be important to highlight, among other aspects, and following the opinions expressed by industry professionals:- the criticism of the intention to add to the responsibilities of an air traffic controller competences that go beyond his functions, such as those linked to 'unexpected crisis situations (e.g. aircraft diversion, bomb threats).' - criticism of the opening up of the possibility for controllers 'who operate under the responsibility of air navigation service providers' (asps) not to be their employees. do you have a fragile bond? are they employees of one company working for another? under what conditions? can a controller work without being an employee of the air navigation service provider? with what consequences? finally, the consideration that, even if more or less clearly stated, in some of the european parliament's proposals there is still an implicit openness to previous and current projects linked to the 'single european sky', i.e. to the liberalisation and subsequent privatisation of air traffic management.
in writing. the report in question, which i voted in favour of, is part of the amendment to which i am a supporter and which seeks to ensure that the rights acquired by the current air traffic controllers - rights acquired under valid, demanding legislation with obviously positive results - are respected, without in any way calling into question the highest value of air transport safety. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. the proposal for a directive, which follows the legislative package on the single european sky, aims to harmonise the member states' legal provisions on the training and exercise of the profession of air traffic controller, which is particularly relevant and prominent today. the adoption of common standards of competence and training, based on international criteria, could benefit the circulation of these professionals on the european market, increase the recruitment base available to each employer and contribute to achieving an identical level of safety throughout the european union. the vote in favour of the report in committee shows that the proposal is highly technical and that the majority of the committee supports it. i voted yes.
in writing. the european investment bank is, and should be, one of the instruments of the european union's development policy. the work it does, the credit it provides and the terms on which it does it, the technical support it provides, all these elements are part and parcel of a type of development intervention which deserves our agreement. the commission's work is also of a political nature and is geared to the development objectives of the programme, which justifies its presentation to the european parliament. for both reasons, and without this vote being a commitment to all the eib's actions, i believe that the report deserves a vote in favour.
in writing. the european investment bank is a privileged instrument of the european union and its economy. the own investments it has developed and the individuals it has empowered give it a key status in the objective of making europe the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world. the dynamism of the european investment bank's activities, particularly in the private sector, has enabled it to mobilise new sources of finance, in particular through risk capital instruments and the granting of guarantees. this gives us the necessary assurance that the european investment bank will continue to play a crucial role in the union's institutional framework in financing small and medium-sized enterprises, thus contributing to the creation of a sound economy that creates more and better jobs and fosters sustainable growth. the eib should therefore give priority to strengthening its lending to small businesses, setting precise rules for the evaluation of their projects, improving access to risk capital for smes and facilitating access to its activities by local and regional financial partners. i voted yes.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague, mrs ilda figueiredo, on her report on the social situation in the european union. it makes a critical diagnosis of this, supported by statistical data which illustrate well the social inequalities that persist in the eu, exacerbated by the recent enlargement. i agree with the call for: - giving the utmost priority to tackling the problems of unemployment, poverty and social exclusion and to creating sustainable, quality and entitled employment; - taking this reality into account in the definition of the broad economic policy guidelines, and in particular in the reform of the stability pact and the revision of the lisbon strategy, as well as in the decision on the financial perspectives and the structural funds for 2007-2013; and - supporting the structural development of the most disadvantaged regions, in particular the outermost regions. among the measures proposed, i would like to highlight those which promote equality and combat discrimination in the area of women's rights, given that today is international women's day. the commission has also proposed a number of measures to combat poverty, such as the 'minimum income' which is vital to the fight against poverty, since portugal had a pioneering experience in this respect under the previous socialist government, with recognised positive results, with the so-called 'minimum guaranteed income'.
in writing. we regret that this report has been rejected by the right-wing majority of the european parliament, which is disturbed by the fact that social problems are being discussed, that it is not acceptable to denounce the causes and that it rejects any attempt to change the policies of neoliberalism. the epp, accompanied on several points by the liberals, has therefore tried to tamper with the report in its key points from the outset. the commission has not been able to do so in the committee on employment and social affairs, but it has been able to do so in the plenary, in particular in the following respects: - withdrawing criticism of the lisbon strategy as regards its contribution to accelerating liberalization/privatisation, labour flexibility and job insecurity; - insisting on the importance of the lisbon strategy for the future, without any revision, despite the current problems of unemployment and social exclusion; - removing references to the need for a review of current economic and financial policies, in particular the stability pact, the lisbon strategy, the internal market and competition policy, and giving priority to the pursuit of a high employment rate, sustainable, quality and rights-based employment; - rejecting, as the ps did, our request to the commission to withdraw the proposal for a directive on the creation of an internal market for services... in writing. neither the fact that the author is portuguese nor the fact that she is speaking on the social situation in europe is sufficient to make me vote in favour of this report. in fact, more than a national or a social brand, the report in question registers a heavy ideological brand which, with all due respect, i have considered for several years to be deeply wrong. on the one hand there are those who believe more in the effectiveness of the state as a creator of social equality, and on the other there are those who believe that freedom regulated by a less intrusive state but more rigorous in ensuring the application of the law is the model to follow. i'm part of the seconds. the main issue here is the economy. and i argue that a productive economy creates more wealth, creates more jobs, creates more opportunities and allows for better distribution. the idea that a country full of subsidies and public jobs is sustainable is an illusion and the right path to greater social injustice.
in writing. the objective of making europe the most competitive and dynamic economy cannot be divorced from social concerns, and growth must be supported by policies that promote greater social cohesion. i therefore support measures to support the family, to reduce inequalities between countries, to tackle the birth rate problem, to examine the consequences of the services directive on the labour market, to encourage vocational training and to create small and mediumsized enterprises. unlike the rapporteur, i do not believe that the european social problems can be solved without taking account of price stability, cost reduction and the budget deficit. i do not believe that the key to combating poverty and social exclusion lies solely in the social economy, but rather that the incentives for private enterprise should be the driving force behind any economy and the solutions to its social problems. finally, i believe that the solution to europe's demographic problem should be found, preferably, through policies to encourage births rather than emigration. unfortunately, the maximalism of the positions of the rapporteur and her group led to the rejection of this report. it is a pity, because this is a serious problem which merited the adoption of appropriate recommendations, but more realistic, objective and balanced ones.
nuclear weapons are illegal and immoral. five years ago the world rejoiced at the historic consensus reached on the nuclear non-proliferation treaty. a significant milestone for world peace, as kofi annan said. five years later, on the eve of the next treaty review conference, the picture is frighteningly different. the united states has changed its position on the commitments it has made and the present administration is even announcing the development of new nuclear weapons technologies involving astronomical sums. the united states and other nuclear-weapon states party to the treaty have not since respected the commitments to disarmament, nor have they shown any sign of wanting to reduce their nuclear arsenals. the united states still has 480 nuclear weapons stationed in europe and has not ratified the ctbt. and the result is that other states parties do not feel like they are also bound by the commitments under the npt after the invasion of iraq, under the false pretext of the existence of weapons of mass destruction. possessing or making believe that one possesses nuclear weapons has come to be regarded, if not perceived, as a factor of deterrence and self-protection. states such as israel, india and pakistan, also possessing nuclear weapons, remain outside the treaty and thus see no incentive or even feel pressured to become a party. more worryingly, north korea is trying to withdraw from the treaty and blackmail the international community. we have even seen this status invoked in the argument for permanent members of the security council. according to the united nations high-level panel on threats, hazards and challenges, we are now at the point where the erosion of the non-proliferation regime may become irreversible and result in cascading proliferation. we know that there is, on top of that, a high risk of nuclear materials falling into the hands of terrorists, in many cases not even controlled by states. cascade proliferation can only be prevented if the international community joins forces in effective multilateral solutions. and the next npt review is an opportunity that cannot be missed. the european union can and must play a decisive role in making the treaty operational with a permanent bureau and for this it must go through coordination with the countries in the european union which have nuclear weapons, so that there can be real coordinated action under the terms of the cfsp and the esdp. given the situation of real emergency of absolute priority, the european parliament should send a mission to accompany the european intervention at the conference, thereby assuming a role of monitoring the action of the member states and promoting the effort of the treaty in line with ... mr president, this debate is taking place at a particularly difficult time in the social situation in the european union. we are a long way from the economic growth and employment of the late 1990s, which were the result of the restrictive economic and financial policies, the stability pact, the liberalisation and accelerated privatisation envisaged by the lisbon strategy. today, with growing social and territorial inequalities, unemployment reaching almost 20 million workers, increasing precariousness in employment and some 70 million people living in poverty, inclusion and social cohesion must be a priority, a central concern of this mid-term review of the lisbon strategy, which implies not only the creation of jobs with rights, but also a fairer sharing of the wealth created, with social policies focused on ensuring human rights, better pensions and reforms, quality public services in health, education, research and vocational training, social protection and security, housing and family support facilities, with particular attention to promoting equal rights for women and taking into account appropriate environmental policies. instead, the president of the commission, mr barroso, came here to say that the lisbon strategy is at the heart of economic policies, following the conclusions of the wim kok report, which places particular emphasis on madam president, mr president of the commission, the text of the recommendation reiterates a rhetoric of general principles already acquired exactly where an articulated outline of concrete measures to be taken would be desirable. it would seem that everyone agrees on the objectives, but few know what to do to achieve them. a knowledge-based economy presupposes, as the text says, a highly qualified education, but there is no reference to the fact that a highly qualified education must be based on a school course of high quality, from the first years of schooling. since various deficiencies are known in primary and secondary education in most countries, it is regrettable that the recommendation does not invite the member states to examine this aspect and to urgently seek a solution to it. this document points to the future and the future cannot be without this solution. on the other hand, the need to mobilise european public opinion to persuade it of the advantages of the lisbon strategy and to get it to join them is emphasised, but not a single word is said about cultural policies, either at european or national level. we are talking about a culture of dialogue, but we are not even talking about a dialogue of cultures. the internalization by each european citizen of the need for and benefits of the lisbon strategy must be above all a cultural attitude. culture is not only an essential dimension of democracy, it is also the framework that will allow us to measure the distance from failure to success in a strategy such as the lisbon strategy, especially if we want to preserve the european social model. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster is a good one, but it is not enough to say that the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the directive is implemented. without them, the lisbon strategy will remain little more than a sympathetic cast of good intentions.
in writing. the relationship that has developed between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific countries deserves our recognition and our applause. for reasons both of history and of a simple sense of international responsibility, these countries have a special significance and importance for a large majority of the member states in particular and for the european union as a whole. the importance and usefulness of this relationship, which is reflected in the activities of the joint parliamentary assembly, require that it be true to and consistent with the principles which the european union has defended and regularly called for. good relations between the two parties are more than desirable, they are imperative, but they are only possible - and useful - if they are based on a logic of defending the values in which we believe and if, consequently, the european union does not hesitate to criticise and to take the necessary consequences in cases where the countries in question do not comply with their international obligations or with those of their own nationals. in general, this has been the case, despite the disagreement we have had the opportunity to express in cases such as cuba and angola. still, my vote is in favor.
in writing. the unanimous vote on this report in the special committee illustrates the growing importance which this parliament, from right to left, has been attaching to relations with the parliaments of the acp countries and their members, which are fundamental in a europe which wants to be open to the world and is committed to strengthening dialogue with its strategic partners, in line with historical ties. i welcome the significant progress made in the internal organisation, external action and institutional influence of the joint parliamentary assembly during the past year and wish it to continue and strengthen itself. i welcome the recognition of the need to address the issue of post-conflict situations together and i am grateful for the trust placed in me as co-rapporteur on this matter. despite the reasons for satisfaction mentioned, i cannot help but criticize, once again, the fact that, in the sessions of the joint parliamentary assembly, the use of portuguese and the provision of interpretation in this language - which, it should be recalled, is the third european language of universal communication - are repeatedly neglected in relation to other languages (ultra-minority languages in the acp context), preventing portuguese-speaking members of parliament from being on an equal footing with the other members of the assembly. i voted yes.
in writing. the current generalized system of preferences (gsp) is based on a logic that contains a contradiction: that it is through the liberalization of international trade - an export-promoting model, regulated at world level, with a 'centre' and a 'periphery' - that development is promoted. a logic which denies fair international relations and aid to the development of the endogenous factors of the economically less developed countries, without which - between the theft of external debt and the imposition of the interests of the large multinationals of the usa, the eu and japan - they will continue to have a peripheral and subordinate status. trade is a component of development, but it is by far not the most important. the gsp guarantees preferential access to products from some 178 countries. the current proposal anticipates its entry into force date and opens the gsp to products of particular sensitivity for portugal (tuna canned, tomato concentrate, textiles and clothing). textiles and clothing are particularly affected, in particular by the existence of a high graduation threshold for the sector. this and other negative aspects need to be changed, otherwise there will be serious consequences for the national productive sector, with the social and economic consequences that follow.
in writing. the gsp should be understood as both a trade policy instrument and a development support instrument, while international trade is certainly one of the most powerful engines of development and growth in any economy. in this sense, and as the rapporteur expressly states in his explanatory statement, 'the gsp should therefore be consistent with the objectives of development policy and compatible with the doha programme'. the doha round is indeed an important step forward towards a more open, fairer world economy and this understanding should, as the report proposes, be present in the gsp. finally, i understand that the speed with which the gsp was changed to respond to the aftermath of the tsunami should be applauded.
in writing. the graduation mechanism introduced allows the gsp to be withdrawn from countries which are competitive on the community market and which no longer need the preferential system to promote their exports. the mechanism also plays a key role in regulating trade flows in textiles and clothing, which is of the utmost importance for the defence of the european textile industry, given the abolition of tariff quotas on 31 december 2004. i also believe that one of the areas of promoting sustainable development is the improvement of the economic situation of developing countries, particularly those countries which are least integrated into the international trading system. the most vulnerable developing countries, therefore, which bear special burdens and responsibilities due to the ratification and implementation of the basic conventions on human and workers' rights, will benefit from additional tariff preferences under the gsp, which i welcome. finally, the simplification achieved by reducing the number of schemes from five to three, with a general scheme, a special scheme to encourage sustainable development and good governance and a special scheme for the least developed countries (everything but arms) should be noted. i voted yes.

in writing. good democracy is based on full and maximum respect for the rights of citizens, respect which historically has included the right of citizens to petition parliamentary assemblies. this practice, which may at times seem of little use, is above all a sign of democratic humility and a willingness to listen to the citizens, which are the most important characteristics of a democratic society. the existence of the committee on petitions in the european parliament and the work it has done deserve our public's recognition.
in writing. the most common criticism of the current state of the european integration process is that of the divorce between decision-makers and citizens, the so-called democratic deficit. in parliamentary terms, the committee on petitions is a fruitful way of intensifying contact with the population, and its involvement should be enhanced and popular participation in european affairs encouraged. i think that this will have the solidarity merit of, on the one hand, giving an account of the real concerns and aspirations of the people, and, on the other, allowing parliamentarians to present what their work has been to those who seek them and to demonstrate their willingness to work for the real needs of their fellow citizens. in this connection, i regret that the petition calling for the inclusion of the reference to the legacy of christianity in the preamble to the constitutional treaty, in clear contradiction to the expressed wish of more than one million people who had mobilized to sign it throughout europe, was not given due consideration. finally, i believe that the committee on petitions would benefit from increased resources and effective and balanced support not only from the european commission but also from the council.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, as did the pse group and the large majority of the ep, because it sets out guidelines and measures which will make it possible to revitalize the lisbon strategy, improve its implementation and achieve the objectives set in 2000. as i have always advocated, it provides for greater involvement in the decision-making and implementation process not only of the european parliament (a genuine culture of dialogue with parliament should be established), alongside the commission (with which a 'strong partnership' would be established) and the council (tripartite meetings between the three institutions are proposed), but also of the national parliaments (a 'strong partnership' would also be established between them and the ep), as well as the enhanced involvement of regional and local authorities. e- calls for budgetary resources at national and community level to be adequate to the objectives to be achieved under the lisbon agenda, and this should be reflected in the financial perspectives for 2007-13 and the structural funds as they have been reformed in the context of the reform of cohesion policy. in addition, the revised lisbon strategy will be an instrument for bringing about the desirable change in the economic and social development model hitherto followed in the madeira region.
in writing. between the illusion that it is enough to declare a goal to achieve it, and the reality that shows that the european economy has not been able to cope with the current moment of world crisis, we find a european union with different economic and social realities that brings together a set of good declarative intentions, but which has been little effective in solving its problems. that said, it is important to recognise that europe is the best continent in the world to live on. so if europe is to become the most competitive economy in the world, we must make adjustments to the path we have been following, without losing what is best and most essential, and respecting the historical, cultural and developmental diversity of the different european countries. i therefore believe that the general meaning of the resolution in question is correct: sustainable growth and employment must be the eu's most urgent objectives and they will be the ones that will promote environmental and social progress. there is no european social model without a european economy, but there is no point in a competitive economy that does not serve the interests of the citizens.
in writing. the mid-term review presented here is marked by the conclusions of the last european council in brussels in the spring, which concluded that the results achieved were modest in relation to the objectives set. the stagnation of the european economy since 2000 has not helped. the proposed text, moreover, - apart from calling for greater determination on the part of the commission's leadership - merely reiterates principles embodied in the original strategy. sustainable development, social cohesion, improvement of working conditions and increased employment, continuing or dynamic training and the competitiveness of the economy are as relevant today as they were then. as, unfortunately, the alienation of many states and citizens continues to weigh on the other side. in this connection, i regret that the last ecofin meeting was another opportunity to combine financial discipline and budgetary rigor with the necessary consideration of the nature and quality of public expenditure. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. finally, i think that a much more realistic approach is needed, one that does not simply deplore failures and justify everything repeatedly by the absence of motivation and implementation by the states. it calls for creativity, leadership and determination, which is the most salient aspect of this resolution and which leads me to vote in favour.
in writing. based on the realistic scenario outlined in the wim kok interim report, the european commission has decided to revise its copy and present a reform of the lisbon strategy objectives. the priorities set in 2000 have been redefined on the basis of the current concerns of european citizens: growth and jobs. on the basis of this new reality, the people responsible for each measure are identified, concrete deadlines are set and progress is assessed. implementation now involves a single national programme and the appointment of a 'lord of lisbon' in each member state, responsible for monitoring the actions of the lisbon strategy and for simplifying the evaluation methods. as an intergovernmental area, the lisbon strategy depends almost exclusively on the capacity and commitment of member states to carry out deep structural reforms. with the revision of the strategy, the setting of clearer priorities and the urgency of the timetable, the necessary preconditions are created for member states to make the lisbon strategy a success story. today, for most european citizens, the lisbon strategy may seem a bit utopian. the history of the eu is rich in examples of this. in the 1980s, no one believed in the success of the single market and the single currency. i wish the lisbon strategy the same success.

in writing. i voted in favour of the marie-hélène aubert report on the european action plan for organic food and farming because i believe that it raises fundamental questions for the very future of organic farming. we must be aware that this agriculture now represents an important part of the food and agricultural production market in the european union. the action plan proposes to act on three main priorities - developing the organic food market based on information and raising consumer awareness, making public aid to organic farming more effective and improving and strengthening community standards for organic farming and import and inspection requirements. these priorities should therefore above all seek to address effectively the difficulties inherent in the specific features of organic farming, which run from production to distribution. a european action plan for organic farming should be ambitious, since organic farming is not limited to the production of food, but plays a wider role in environmental and social matters.
in writing. biological issues are of great importance today. since 1985 we have seen a significant increase in the number of farms and hectares of land used for organic farming. however, this growth has slowed down considerably in recent years due to difficulties in the production, processing and distribution of these products. this report advocates more and better measures to remove these obstacles. the main objective is to make everyone, in general, and not just some urban minorities, aware of the environmental benefits of organic products. improving community standards, including the cap, and increasing public aid are key to making organic farming a more dynamic aspect of sustainable agriculture. at a time when the environment must be a priority, this issue must be at the forefront. while i am sure that the high price of 'organic' products is the major obstacle to consumption, i am convinced that the development of support for organic farming will result in lower prices and, consequently, in increased consumption by the general public. i voted yes.

in writing. this report addresses a very important issue for the future of research, knowledge and innovation in the various member states of the european union, which should be summarised in three aspects: - to achieve more research, increased funding is needed and the budget of the sixth framework programme represents only 5.4% of total public expenditure on research in europe, making the creation of any european research area impossible. the financing of the future programme is essential, but the final amount of the financial perspective is not known. the rapporteur is asking for at least a doubling, which seems logical. - i know . the future programme will, however, undergo a number of changes compared with the present one. but not exactly the ones proposed in the report. research must support innovation, but it must not be all about increasing competitiveness, as is the case with the commission's guidance following the wim kok report. - greater attention must be paid to the working conditions of all those engaged in research. the rapporteur states that in order to achieve the objective of investing 3% of gdp in r & d, the european union needs 700 000 new researchers by 2010. now, this means that we need to invest in human resources to get more researchers.
in writing. research is a crucial area for the success of innovation and the long-term competitiveness of the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this report on the guidelines for the future policy of the european union in support of research. the creation of the european research area will only be possible with increased eu research funding, with a view to better coordination between european, national and regional research policies. i therefore give my full support to the proposal to double the budget for the 7th framework programme. the eu needs 700,000 new, appropriately qualified researchers by 2010 if it is to meet the target of investing 3% of gdp in research and technological development. to achieve this, it is essential to make europe more attractive to researchers and scientists, to generate a new enthusiasm for science among young people, to encourage the participation of women, and to promote scientific careers and the mobility of researchers. finally, i would like to stress that member states eligible for the structural funds should use a significant part of these resources to eliminate their disadvantaged situations in the field of research.
in writing. i voted in favour of the pia elda locatelli report (a6-0046/2005) - guidelines for the union's research policy on 'science and technology' because i am an advocate of strong and effective research policies for and in europe. fully aware of the difficulty of achieving the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy, i remain a supporter of a union research and development (r & d) policy as one of the main instruments for promoting europe's growth and competitiveness. the completion of the european research area (era) and the continuity of the planning of research programmes are essential. the objective of making europe more competitive requires financial resources for research. new strategies for the creation of enterprises cooperating with regional institutions as well as universities are therefore aspects to be developed for the future. it seems to me important that universities should take on an entrepreneurial side, capable of interacting between research and industry. finally, i support the proposals that the structural funds should support regional r & d actions and a 'european label of excellence'.
in writing. i welcome the courage of the rapporteur who has given the following title to her explanatory statement: 'europe deserves better: no more 'lisbon lament'. as i said yesterday, the 'objectives of lisbon' are as consensual as the recognition that a new, strong and courageous attitude is urgently needed. i'll add that to your list: creative. the kok report on the lisbon strategy stated that europe needed to be made more attractive to researchers and scientists. indeed, numerous sources and statistics indicate that europe has been suffering a veritable bloodletting of its best scientists and researchers. we need to stop it. the objective of the 'european research area' should be pursued through concrete actions, including: increased technology transfer, especially for smes; full and efficient use of the structural funds to support r & d at regional level; special emphasis on interdisciplinarity in training; strengthening the role of universities in the europe of knowledge by empowering them; encouraging the mobility of researchers by promoting and facilitating family reunification; achieving the 3% target for r & d; establishing and disseminating innovation hubs, such as the proposed european institute of technology; equipping primary and secondary schools with technological tools to encourage research; promoting 'success stories' campaigns. in a word, leave the regrets. i voted yes.
in writing. the preservation of biodiversity and the reversal of desertification are key to ensuring sustainable development. healthy ecosystems provide important social and economic resources. the natura 2000 network, based on sites protected under the birds and habitats directives, contributes to this objective. in its proposal for the financial framework for 2007-13, the european commission intends to finance the costs of running this network - €6.1 billion per year - from existing funds. although the aim is to reverse biodiversity loss: - the causes are not addressed: the change in the production model based on profit maximisation, as exemplified by the release of gmos into the environment. - i know . and the necessary funding is not secured, putting this objective in 'competition' with other economic and social objectives. we therefore believe that the appropriations for rural development (to compensate for the additional costs for farmers) and the structural funds should be increased proportionately if the costs of natura 200 management are charged to these funds. it is also essential to increase the appropriations for the life programme and/or to create a dedicated programme for this network to ensure that the objectives are met.
in writing. in an increasingly urbanised society, where rural areas are becoming desertified and where industrialisation and construction take up the traditional 'natural' space, the european union's concern to ensure the maintenance of biodiversity is justified and useful. a society that abandons its fields, its forests, its rural space not only reduces biodiversity but also its capacity to exploit natural resources, encourages urban concentration, the macrocephaly of the major cities and reduces the quality of life in general. more than the defence of biodiversity as an end, our main objective must be to protect a model of development which ensures the possibility of full enjoyment of a quality life, only possible when the 'natural' space is preserved and maintained.
in writing. the environment deserves to be a priority worldwide. the growth of recent decades and the negative impacts on the world have made this a priority and a necessity for sustainable development. in this particular case, what is at stake is the world's biological diversity, which has been declining steadily over the last few decades. the natura 2000 network, which aims to protect nature, in particular by preserving animal life and its habitats, presents a unique opportunity to combat this depletion of biological diversity in our area. it's our share of direct responsibility. i think it is important that there are adequate levels of funding and that the support and benefits are increased if the main objective is to be achieved. it is worth recalling that the eu is committed to the principle of environmental integration in line with the cardiff process and the community's own sustainable development strategy. this report advocates joint responsibility for the member states and the community. the european union funds should therefore cover sites included in the network and their management activities. moreover, this strategy, because of the activities associated with it, could contribute to the improvement of the rural economy and the quality of life of citizens. i voted yes.
in writing. we know that the present sugar regime has been accused of causing market distortions, high consumer prices and having a negative effect on the world market, particularly in developing countries. it was on the basis of these arguments that the commission put forward in july 2004 a proposal for the reform of the common organisation of the market in sugar, focusing on price reductions (guarantee price (37%), institutional price (33%) in two stages over three years; the abolition of the intervention price (currently three times the world market price) and the abolition of public intervention, which will be replaced by a private storage system and the substitution of the intervention price by the reference price, plus the reduction of sugar production quotas and the reduction of subsidised exports. the only support provided is the introduction of income aid in the form of a differentiated payment to sugar beet growers to compensate them partially (60%) for the loss of income resulting from the price reduction and the introduction of the possibility of transferring quotas between operators in different member states. these are positions which we cannot accept, and that is why we have tabled several amendments, but unfortunately not all of them have been adopted.
in writing. the resolution in question, concerning the common organization of the market in sugar, was ultimately the result of a compromise which ultimately guarantees the essential interests of the country, particularly in view of the reduced beet market which is beginning to develop in portugal, and which is all the more serious since, if this were not the case, the damage would be in an ultraperipheral region such as the azores, which is already exposed to various constraints on its economic development.
in writing. the main reservation i have about the sugar reform is that it is a major reduction in the beet production quotas announced in the commission proposal. i share the view of the producers' associations and some european governments that this measure is leading to the concentration of beet production in only a few member states. i believe that it must be maintained throughout the community, not only for environmental and economic reasons, but also because otherwise there is a risk of losing thousands of jobs, which are hardly replaceable, and inevitably social costs. i am sure that the reform of the common organization of the market in sugar must ensure a price level which ensures that both community producers and suppliers from developing countries are adequately remunerated, and that the temptation to upset the balance in the sugar sector is avoided. otherwise, i believe, it will cause serious damage not only to community producers, who will suffer a sharp fall in income, but also to community consumers, who, as in previous reforms, will not even benefit from a reduction in the price of sugar, and will lose everything in the market. i voted yes.

the european parliament has been asked to make a statement on the situation in the region. we cannot hold the new commission directly responsible for the progress or delays that have occurred. in fact, 2004 was the year in which the prodi commission ceased to function and the barroso commission took office, i.e. vitorino replaced fratini. but 2004 was a historic year, mainly for three reasons: first, because the european union has grown in size, now with a population of over 450 million, and has become more politically, geographically and economically powerful; second, because beyond the economic dimension and the internal market, we have become more shared in responsibility for threats to stability and security that are not confined to borders, as is the case with terrorism. we must remember the tragic events of 11 march in madrid. and thirdly, as mr cavada and mr ruhr have already mentioned, the major change in the area of justice and home affairs, with the introduction of a new institutional framework for visas, asylum and immigration, the introduction of codecision with the european parliament and qualified majority voting in the council. the questions we have put to the commission and the council here highlight the concerns to which we want answers. we want to know what initiatives are being taken and this parliament wants to follow up on these initiatives. we do not want to play a mere decorative role, we want our views to be taken into account in order to ensure that all citizens of the union can live freely in a world of security, combating all forms of calamity and guaranteeing our freedoms. in this respect, commissioner fratini, i congratulate you on your assurances that greater security must not compromise freedom, and on the initiative you have taken within the council of europe for a european day against the death penalty. the european parliament has also called for the introduction of a european citizenship system, which would allow citizens to have the right to vote in local elections. and thirdly and lastly, that judicial review be improved by extending the jurisdiction of the court of justice.
european public order is based on a system of universal values, which finds its ultimate expression in the charter of fundamental rights and the emerging constitution. the system of competences of the european union of the member states and of the european institutions is therefore not morally neutral. the area of freedom, security and justice is the place where the challenge to public policy posed by the question of basic human dignity is most clearly seen. asylum, immigration, the penal system, the balance between freedom and security require consensus for justice and often harmonization of legislation. on this basis, there are dramatic areas to which i would like to draw the attention of the council and the commission. how can we tackle, for example, the issue of illegal immigration? is there any recognition here of the urgency of a common policy or is each state left to its own policy, including the policy of criminalisation? how do the council and the commission intend to tackle the question of prison reform? do you accept that this too is a matter for individual states alone or do you see the need for a common, urgent policy that is transversal to the whole criminal justice system, that is to say, covering the period of serving sentences and the modulation of sentences themselves? europe is not really fulfilled only if it is an obsessive security space. europe is only a reality if, along with the concern for a security area, it is also a real area of justice.

in writing. the aim, in view of the latest enlargement of the european union, is to amend regulation no 1059/2003 of the european parliament and of the council on the establishment of nuts, i.e. the nomenclature of territorial units for statistics, which aims to provide for a uniform system of allocation of territorial units for the compilation of regional statistics in the european union. the opportunity created by the enlargement of the european union has facilitated the introduction of changes necessary for the greater effectiveness of the system, among which i would highlight the redefinition of the framework of the existing administrative units and the provision of a category of smaller administrative units. this last amendment eliminates the lack of homogeneity which has hitherto characterized the nuts classification and which led to the whole of sweden and the brussels region being listed at the same level. i support the rapporteur when he considers it appropriate to reflect certain elements better, in particular when he considers that it is not appropriate at this stage to amend the legal basis of the proposal for a regulation under consideration and in the request to the commission to draw up a communication on the subject.
in writing. the counterfeiting of the euro has been increasing alarmingly, and it is one of the main targets of criminal organisations, which, with a high degree of sophistication, end up benefiting from the absence of internal borders in the eu and the lack of technical and operational resources in some member states. joint, homogeneous and effective responses are needed, which should involve close cooperation with europol. the proposal put forward by six member states to designate europol as the eu's central counterfeiting unit is not realistic, however, given the limitations it has to be able to fulfil these functions. despite the good intentions, the proposal does not solve the fundamental problems raised by the structure of europol. europol should be community-oriented, have community funding, a legal basis that can be changed more easily, use the rule of qualified majority and codecision, and be subject to the democratic control of the ep and the court of justice. i support this report, because in the present situation there can be adequate protection of the euro only if the powers of the current national central services for the protection of the euro are maintained and a mechanism for close cooperation and exchange of information between them and europol is established.
in writing. given its value, the borderless territory it covers and the importance it is acquiring as a reference currency in non-eu economies, the euro is today one of the most coveted currencies by counterfeiters. these use increasingly sophisticated techniques and methods which are often beyond the detection capability of the authorities in each member state. it is therefore clear that there is a need to continuously study the best ways of protecting the euro and of establishing an effective fight against counterfeiting at european level. in this respect, i believe that europol can play an important role in the centralisation and dissemination of information, contributing to the effectiveness of national services dedicated to the fight against this type of crime. however, to be able to take on this role, its interaction capacity will have to be streamlined and made more operational. without these amendments, and in view of the limitations which the rapporteur has also noted in budgetary and legal terms, there is legitimate doubt as to its ability to fulfil such a task. i voted yes.
in writing. police cooperation is essential if a high level of security is to be provided for european citizens within the area of freedom, security and justice. it is important that there is continuous development of police services and that a whole range of common quality standards and methodologies are adopted at european level. the balance sheet for the first three years of cepol's operation was frankly positive, with considerable progress despite the difficulties caused by the absence of a legal personality, a seat and a budget financed by member states' contributions. decisions on the seat and legal personality were adopted in 2004. the proposal aims to convert cepol into a union body with its own legal personality and statute; to give it increased powers; to provide it with community funding; to provide it with its own seat, bodies and staff (subject to the eu statute); to replace unanimity voting with simple majority voting; and to introduce provisions on the use of all official languages and access to documents. i support the demetriou report and the amendments introduced by the rapporteur, which seek to minimise the risk of centralisation of the system, and i cannot but stress that the training provided by cepol will be complementary to the national training and that it is important to maintain a networking of national institutes.
