in writing. among the many aspects covered in the resolution, as regards members' allowances, the majority of the european parliament once again insists on the creation of a single salary for meps, arguing that there should be no difference in the remuneration paid to them. what is not mentioned is that the creation of an equal salary - in the order of 8,500 euros (about 1,700 accounts) per month - for all members, regardless of the countries they represent, would create situations of immorality when compared with the wage reality of workers (and other elected officials and holders of public institutions) in most countries - this is the correct and fair reference - particularly in portugal. the salary of a member of the european parliament should be based on the salary of the members of the national parliaments of the country where he or she is elected. meps are elected in national circles and are, and should remain, bound by them. the measures of transparency and rigour in the use of the financial resources made available to members for the development of their activities should continue to be applied. that's why i'm voting against it.
in writing. when the clearance of accounts is voted on, it is clear that the distinction between what is agreement with the political decisions which affect financial management and the recognition of the validity of the accounts presented is complex because if i may have objections to raise in respect of the first, the same will not necessarily be true in respect of the second. the report itself leaves a number of notes and recommendations which fully justify my vote in favour. i therefore express my support for the need for a single statute for members of the european parliament, which would put an end to the unjustified inequality of those elected by equal citizens. i also agree with the aim of making brussels the single and permanent seat of the european parliament for reasons of efficiency in the management of human and financial resources, since this duplication of costs with the two european parliament premises is pointless, useless or unreasonable, and is costly. finally, i agree with the need to increase the funds available to guarantee interpretation. knowledge of foreign languages may not be a condition for the exercise of the office of member.
in writing. i welcome the good results in the implementation of the 2003 financial year, the first in which the directors-general drew up annual activity reports, which were subsequently transmitted by the secretary-general to the president and the committee on budgetary control with a declaration giving reasonable assurance that the parliamentary budget had been implemented in accordance with the principles of sound financial management and that the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions had been ensured. a very high level of budget implementation was also achieved. i regret that this report has been an opportunity for another closed-door attack on strasbourg as the seat of the european parliament. it is true that duplicating the locations of operations generates high and unnecessary costs and great inconvenience. but opting for brussels is not the only answer, which could only be defended by sectarianism and myopia. the answer to the problem is to concentrate on strasbourg, which would also strengthen the day-to-day practical and functional independence of parliament vis-à-vis the council, the commission and their bureaucracies. that's the way i see it going. only a decision by the latter to establish a permanent seat in strasbourg and to end the itinerant system would also require the french and strasbourg authorities to make the necessary investments and justify the long-term adaptation of the transport system.
in writing. the broad support for each of the 14 discharge procedures for the decentralised agencies leads to the conclusion that there is a peaceful and useful effect of their action, which is projected to improve the overall effectiveness of the european union's action. from the time the first agencies were set up in the 1970s until the most recent (the european network and information security agency, set up in march 2004), it became apparent that specific tasks of a technical, scientific or management nature were being carried out, which was the objective behind their creation. the accumulation of experience makes it possible to identify new ways and improvements both in terms of the coordination and transparency of the action and in strengthening the complementarity of the action, better organising the necessary resources and their efficient allocation for the production of results and designing a communication strategy for the dissemination of these results. these are some of the suggestions made in the report, together with regular scrutiny of the actual conduct of their projects and the real relevance, effectiveness and efficiency of each agency's model in implementing or contributing to community policies.
in writing. as i have said and written on numerous occasions, i consider the external dimension of the union, and in particular development aid, to be one of the most important aspects of the european project. i therefore support in particular the opinion of the committee on development: the main objective should be to eradicate poverty by strengthening social, educational and health infrastructure, increasing the productive capacity of the most deprived populations and providing support to countries in need so that they can develop local growth and potential. in this connection, as i have said elsewhere, i consider it a priority that 20% of the european union's development cooperation expenditure should be allocated to basic education and health in developing countries. the edf is a key instrument for the implementation of this policy in the acp countries and the commission should, as proposed in this report, promote a policy of speeding up the disbursement of edf resources in order to avoid the (worrying) level of unused resources that has been observed. the desired faster implementation will necessarily have to be accompanied by improved transparency, as well as accountability and respect for the principles of sound financial management. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. although the report makes an assessment of the situation, pointing out, for example, that the number of people living in extreme poverty is constantly increasing or that the fight against poverty requires above all a radical change in policies to combat its structural causes, such as the unsustainable payment of the external debt by the developing countries or inequality in the distribution of wealth, it does highlight its 'limits' by not proposing measures to combat the causes it points to effectively, by accepting the liberalization of world trade or by not calling for the unconditional debt cancellation of all developing countries, as proposed in the amendment we tabled and which was rejected. it does, however, incorporate many positive points, such as the need for public control of water as a principle, and moreover the adoption of our amendment which reaffirms that water is a common good of mankind and that access to water is a fundamental human right which must be promoted and safeguarded.
in writing. the european union has enormous obligations - and advantages, let us admit - in terms of its contribution to development. the permanent discourse in defence of a model of values, a model of growth, a way of being in international relations must have a real correspondence. however, this policy, which should be a priority and which should serve to widen the space for economic development and democracy and respect for human rights, cannot be confused with an export policy that is part of the political agenda of some groups, movements or parties. there is a heritage in the western and developed world that we are part of that is sufficiently common and rooted, and it is this heritage that should be part of our development support effort. this must be the focus of our policies in the run-up to the millennium development goals.
in writing. the fight against poverty in all its forms deserves a global commitment involving the international community and with particular responsibility for the most developed countries. the reduction by half of the number of people living in extreme poverty, the containment of the spread of hiv/aids and the universality of primary education in the world, among other things, are objectives which deserve universal support and to which the european union cannot remain indifferent. in view of this, i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that the millennium development goals are goals which the european union, as a defender and promoter of human rights, should support and encourage. if they are achieved, they will mean remarkable global progress and be a sign of true, active and effective humanism. however, i cannot but note and deplore the attempt to manipulate concepts and language that has been used in the shadows of parliament's reflection on these objectives. the use of euphemisms to mean only globalization and the encouragement of abortion is the strongest evidence of this. i voted against that part. the adoption of such practices, which are real defeats of humanity, can hardly be called a victory over poverty.
author. the existence of a consistent community regional policy - and therefore adequately funded - is a prerequisite for the european union to promote the effective reduction of the regional disparities which successive enlargements have accentuated, as well as real convergence between the different countries. regional policy should be a necessary and fair redistributive instrument which minimises the negative consequences of the internal market for economically less developed regions and countries. if it is clear that the economically most developed countries in particular will be the ones to derive important economic benefits from enlargement, while cohesion countries such as portugal and greece will be the most affected at the macroeconomic level and will also face a real threat of reducing the structural funds in the context of budgetary constraints and the so-called statistical effect, i ask the commission: do you not think that much higher financial amounts than those proposed for regional policy in your proposal for the financial framework for 2007 and 2013 should be required to meet the needs of enlargement and to ensure an effective cohesion policy? what measures does it intend to take for the countries most affected by enlargement, such as portugal and greece? will it set up specific and adapted programmes for the development and modernisation of its economies in the context of an enlarged european union, as it has done in the past? are you prepared to advocate full compensation for the so-called statistical effect, i.e. to ensure that the regions affected by the statistical effect have the support they would have if the eligibility reference point were a european union of 15, since no region should feel disadvantaged by enlargement?
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the recent enlargement is probably the greatest challenge ever faced by the european union. vision, leadership and a community spirit are required if we are to respond in the best way to the needs and impact of enlargement. it was a strong response of this kind to the challenges of completing the single market and economic and monetary union, when the amounts allocated to the structural funds were doubled. the challenge of a viable enlarged europe requires that regional development policy once again play a crucial role. strengthening and reinvigorating economic and social cohesion policy is therefore crucial, not only to combat the huge regional imbalances resulting from the entry of many impoverished regions from the new member states, but also to continue to address the backlogs still existing in several regions of the old member states. the latter aspect cannot be underestimated, not least because regional asymmetries may increase within the framework of the former european union of 15 countries as a result of the dynamics induced by enlargement, particularly in periphery-centre relations. this is why we must not forget that the european union is a political union, a political union of the people, a political union of the people. in fact, taking into account the former european union of 15, it is estimated that the richest and most central countries are the ones who benefit most from enlargement, with countries like portugal, spain and greece probably the ones who benefit least or even lose out. in view of this, i return to the questions raised in the oral question because i do not consider that they have been sufficiently answered by the commission. has the european commission established the cost-benefit ratio of enlargement for each country of the european union? if so, and in situations where the cost clearly outweighs the benefit, does the european commission not think that ways should be found to compensate such countries?
mr president, regional policy has played a fundamental and very well defined role since the very first and weakest steps of the european union. the principle of solidarity was already there as a fundamental point of difference between our antagonistic points and other worldviews. the aim has always been to leave no region behind in the name of a simplistic vision, which is inevitable. this is why all member states and regions have always been committed to developing themselves and making their development models sustainable. today, we all want more, and besides wanting more, we are more. is it reasonable or even rational that after so much effort to achieve european cohesion we should think that just because we are more we are also richer? as european citizens we do not want to look at the make-up, we want to look at the substance, at the structure, and this means that we do not abandon all those regions which have not yet reached the process of real convergence and which, because of a financial and simplistic view, seem to want to get rich overnight. it also requires us to bear in mind the necessary link between regional policy and the lisbon strategy. strong links between these two objectives are crucial to their effectiveness. measuring growth only in financial terms is artificial and unsustainable. sustainable development must therefore be about convergence and competitiveness. to give priority to competitiveness, leaving behind those who are only now beginning to think about how to walk on their own, means that they will fall again and will not have the strength to recover on their own. for us, for all the citizens of this europe of solidarity, competitiveness cannot replace convergence. competitiveness cannot replace regional policy, the most visible policy, and therefore solidarity is needed with regions such as the algarve, the highlands, asturias and madeira, as well as with many other regions outside europe that have theoretically become rich overnight.
the recent downward revision of the growth forecasts published by the commission, and the slowdown in growth forecasts, compared with the already low growth in 2004, show that restrictive fiscal and monetary policies at european level and in the member states have limited domestic demand, public investment and economic recovery. its negative impact on unemployment, poverty and social exclusion, as well as on the worsening of social and territorial inequalities, is visible in the 20 million unemployed and the nearly 70 million people living in poverty, despite the fact that the operating results of large enterprises in the european union increased by 78% in 2004 and that profits as a percentage of gdp in the euro area are now close to the highest level for at least 25 years. in this situation, how can we accept the current relaunch of the lisbon strategy, based on competitiveness and the creation of a more attractive framework for businesses, insisting on deepening the policies of liberalization, particularly in the area of services, increasing the flexibility of the markets, reducing workers' rights, extending the sectors where low wage levels are in force, insisting on maintaining the proposals for directives on the organization of working time and the creation of an internal market in services? we won't take it. how can we accept that the council's conclusions only mention social inclusion in a brief sentence and refer to children in poverty, without taking a multidisciplinary and integrated approach to combating poverty and social exclusion? how can it be accepted that, despite the announced revision of the stability pact, we continue to insist on meeting restrictive, albeit somewhat flexible, targets, but giving priority to the dismantling of public and universal social security, when we know that public investment and the maintenance of public social security systems are essential to combating poverty and social exclusion? for all these reasons, we insist on the need to withdraw the proposals for directives on working time and the internal market in services, to repeal and replace the stability pact with a growth and employment pact, to give priority to the creation by 2010 of 22 million quality jobs with rights, to achieve the targets set by the lisbon council and to halve poverty and social exclusion as agreed in the lisbon strategy in 2000. we believe that the fight against income inequalities and the promotion of equal rights and opportunities and real convergence must be at the top of the economic and social agenda of the european union.
in writing. to their despair, the european council of 22 and 23 march was marked by an item which was not on its agenda but was imposed on it. the recent polls indicating a possible victory for the 'no' vote on the so-called 'european constitution' in the referendum to be held in france on 29 may have sounded the bells. the right wing and the social democrats, sisters, are mobilizing, encouraging all the more or less brazen interference in the campaign that is taking place in france. the european parliament is unacceptably using 8 million euros for propaganda in favour of the 'yes'. the pilgrimage of heads of state and government and all those who think they can influence the decision of the french people is increasing, trying to convince them of the hypothetical and non-existent 'advantages' (?) of the so-called 'european constitution'. the big employers and the trade union leaderships dominated by the social democrats or the right wing - with the european trade union confederation at the head - all strive to defend this project which undermines the sovereignty of the peoples and is fighting for neoliberal capitalism and militarism. the european commission and the european parliament are postponing decision-making in an attempt to avoid giving even more and fair arguments to the no. despite contradictions, the no in france will be the best answer!
in writing. my vote in favour of the proposed calendar, which keeps the plenary sessions in line with the demands of high-quality parliamentary work required of an institution such as the european parliament, does not undermine my conviction, and the defence i have made of the need to rationalise parliamentary work and the costs associated with it, in particular by adopting a single permanent seat in brussels.
in writing. the enlargement process to bulgaria and romania must, as in the past, be accompanied by a realistic assessment of its financial implications, otherwise enlargement will become a process of subtracting the conditions for the prosperity and development of the member states of the union. a correct assessment of the financial implications is not a selfish gesture on the part of those who have already joined, but rather an imposition of an institution's sense of responsibility.
in writing. the enlargement process to bulgaria, which must be subject to an individual assessment, is at present proceeding as expected and as required, since it is only late in the year for bulgaria to be able to start the application process. as you would expect, we are still far from being able to say that bulgaria fulfils the necessary conditions for membership of the european union. there are reforms to be made, habits that take time to acquire and a whole process of adaptation, which is not just legislative, that must be carried out so that neither the union is disfigured nor bulgaria is left in a situation of inability to meet its future new obligations. that said, the truth is that everything indicates that the conditions will be met in due time, and we should therefore welcome this further step in the enlargement of the european union.
in writing. in view of the insufficient progress made compared with the 15 enlargement states on 1 may 2004, bulgaria's intention to join the european union on that date was postponed. however, it is now clear that bulgaria has made significant efforts to meet the community criteria and to move closer to the community politically, economically and socially. the progress made in political and budgetary terms is noteworthy, providing a stable basis for bulgaria's remaining path towards european standards - a path that will be neither short nor easy. the european council of 17 december 2004 therefore endorsed the accession of bulgaria on 1 january 2007. the european commission, which had been issuing regular reports on the progress of the accession process, did so on 22 february 2005. parliament must follow in their footsteps. it is clear that for the union, the accession of a country like bulgaria will necessarily involve costs, which are desirably borne by an increasingly effective effort at internal cohesion, but above all an enrichment of its own capacity to relate to and understand the world. an increase in diversity. i voted yes.
in writing. the right wing and the social democrats in the european parliament - and not only here - continue to try to impose neoliberal capitalism on the applicant countries. the example of bulgaria speaks for itself. the ep welcomes the so-called 'structural reforms' in the framework of the capitalist 'market' and 'competition' which it considers to have taken place in the country. it shows its "satisfaction" with "the expansion of the private sector" and "the progress made in liberalizing vital industries" moreover, it 'encourages' the introduction of 'greater flexibility in the labour market' and 'encourages' the pace of privatisation to be maintained. more words for what? the whole accession process has been characterized by other impositions which we consider unacceptable, such as discrimination in the movement of workers, equal access to community funding, or the existence of unilateral safeguard clauses which can be used against the interests of these countries, and only of these countries. enlargement is taking place within a political and financial framework which takes no account of the interests of portugal or the needs of the new applicant countries. in front of the criticism of the way in which enlargement is being implemented, we are not opposed to the accession of new member states, provided that this is the will of their people and that portuguese interests are safeguarded.
in writing. it seems clear that bulgaria will be in a position to join the european union on 1 january 2007, as is accepted by the other community institutions. i therefore believe that the european parliament should add its own opinion to those already produced and publicly express its support for the enlargement of the union to that country. despite this principled position, there are still some gaps, particularly in judicial and police terms, which need to be effectively filled in order to allow for greater effectiveness in the fight against crime and to promote greater transparency and procedural guarantees, which are essential in a state governed by the rule of law. at this preparatory stage, it is also important to pay particular attention to the rights of ethnic minorities and the need to ensure their identity, as well as to protect children and the elderly, the most fragile and vulnerable parts of society, particularly in a changing society. i voted in favour, hoping that bulgaria could soon join the 25 in an ever larger and more diverse europe.
in writing. we have also abstained here, as we did in the last enlargement of the european union, except in the case of cyprus, where we voted in favour also in protest against the unacceptable occupation by turkey of a part of the north of the island. in principle, we are not opposed to the accession of new member states, provided that this is the will of their people and does not compromise portuguese interests. the truth is that, although the will of the romanian people is not well known, the truth is that there are expectations created by accession, after immense demands and impositions that we consider unacceptable, in particular the structural reforms that justified privatisations, and which had a negative impact on the life of the population. new demands, as several members have tried, seemed to us to be excessive and unacceptable. but the fact is that there are already impositions, such as the derogations on the free movement of workers and the limited financial resources, particularly for agriculture, which also deserve our condemnation. finally, we also disagree with the proposals under negotiation for the new financial perspective, which take no account of countries in difficulty such as portugal or the needs of the new applicant countries.
in writing. the assessment of whether or not the conditions for the accession of a new member state are met must be made on an individual basis, even if the accession may take place at the same time as that of another member state. but this possibility should not be conditional on the most important thing for accession to take place: that the assessment of the necessary conditions be realistic. only in this way will it be ensured that both the union, with all its member states, and the applicant country can derive all the benefits of accession. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. what i have just said implies that i regard the possibility of postponing accession as a positive one if there is a need to do so. but it doesn't mean i want it. for reasons of internal policy romania has started its reform process later than would be in its own interest. however, the pace of reforms is giving rise to confidence and hope that the adjustment capacity will be in line with the timetable desired by both parties.
in writing. the process of romania's accession to the european union has been dragging on since 1995. the negotiations and efforts made by the romanian authorities have brought about significant changes in the situation in the country in recent times. as such, the european council decided in december 2004 to conclude the accession negotiations with a view to accession in 2007. however, i recall the concerns raised in the nicholson of whinterbourne report (a5-0103/2004) about a year ago. at that time i highlighted serious problems, namely the lack of a rule of law, the high level of corruption, the lack of freedom of the press, and the lack of independence of the judiciary, which prevented accession from taking place alongside the other former eastern european countries, which did so as early as 2004. the motion for a resolution deserves my support because it contains, among other things, those which are also my main concerns for this country. romania will have the doors of the european union open, but it must realise the urgency of finding rapid, concrete and effective solutions to its most serious problems. i voted yes.
in writing. the european parliament always monitors the situation of countries which formally express an interest in joining the european union. it has obviously done so with regard to romania. it should be noted that this monitoring has been carried out with particular care in view of the delicate situation in the country and the delay in the accession negotiations. romania has made significant efforts and measures in recent years and it is expected that more solutions will be implemented in pursuit of romania's national objective of joining the european union. the various reports of the committee on external affairs, and in particular the most recent report, also by mr moscovici (a6-0077/2005) have documented this. the new romanian government, which emerged from the last elections, also deserves words and clear signs of encouragement. after successive delays and having missed the chance to join the ten countries that joined last year, i have no doubt that if the other recommendations are met, romania, along with bulgaria, will be one of the next states to join the eu. i voted yes.

in writing. the council, in its common position, rejected in general the amendments previously proposed by the european parliament and also departed from the original proposal of the european commission. the community seems unanimous in its aims of improving working conditions, preventing market distortions due to different working conditions in different countries and improving road safety, for which the controls of working hours, which are realistic and feasible, are justified. the council considered that there were considerable practical difficulties preventing the compulsory road checks on compliance with the directive on the organisation of working time from being carried out exhaustively, or at least to the extent desired by the european commission. the commission has been recording a steady increase in the number of infringements in its biannual reports on the application of regulation (eec) no 3820/85 and the adoption of practical and realistic control mechanisms is being sought. the rapporteur has tried to meet the council's common position by seeking to reconcile positions, and in a line which also deserves my agreement.
in writing. we voted in favour of this second reading, despite some differences of opinion on certain aspects of the new directive which lays down ecodesign requirements for products consuming electricity. we believe that it is necessary to focus on maximising energy efficiency and consumer information, but at the same time to ensure that the new legislation does not place a burden on small businesses. the directive covers objects we use every day, such as hair dryers, washing machines, computers, etc., which will be responsible for about 40% of the carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere. only cars are excluded, because they have special legislation. there are important proposals in the report to safeguard micro- and small businesses and consumers. we'll see what the council's position is.

in writing. the aim is to define ecodesign requirements for energy-using products throughout their life cycle, with the main objective of reducing the negative impact of such products on the environment. it is a sensitive matter and, in this respect, parliament has tabled an important set of amendments at first reading, including those relating to conformity assessment of products, ecodesign requirements they must meet, the establishment of a credible and effective market surveillance system, support for smes and consumer information. in the common position, the commission and the council adopted some of the amendments suggested by parliament, but left out important concerns in this area. i support the rapporteur's proposal, which i consider realistic and quite favourable because of the compromise it makes possible. the clarification of concepts such as importer and manufacturer, the suggested increased rigorousness of supervision, mitigated by concerns about smes, the design of a margin for adapting standards to the specificities of the member states are examples of this. i voted in favour of the new amendments, which restore parliament's previous positions in a balanced way.

in writing. the rapporteur's proposal is in line with parliament's original position at first reading. in fact, according to the amendments proposed by parliament, and taking the year 2000 as a benchmark, sulphur emissions from seagoing vessels would be reduced by around 80%, whereas the council's position provides for only a 10% reduction. in the context of the proposals made, i would like to stress the rapporteur's concern about the desirability of making progress within the international maritime organisation (imo) and, in particular, about the role that the eu could play in this respect. both the united states of america and canada and mexico have made important signals to tighten up the imo and eu agreements, and even the recent environmental accidents which have occurred in the united states can and should have a say in this matter. the rapporteur's idea of promoting the development of an environmental technology by creating and fostering a market for it is also interesting. the suggestions made in this context constitute a more effective solution for the protection of human health and the environment.

in writing. this report recalls the danger to public health of the use of certain substances, either as raw materials or as intermediate materials. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not distorted by the use of toxic chemicals. the commission proposal, which the rapporteur, by introducing only one amendment, calls for support, seeks to restrict the use not only of toluene and trichlorobenzene but also of preparations containing them. the european union has always been concerned with these issues of the utmost importance to the lives of its citizens, in line with article 93 tec. the benefit of adopting the proposal in terms of protecting the health of european citizens is clear, so i voted in favour.
in writing. the 2006 budget is strategic in the objective of a growing europe. not only because it is the last of the current financial perspectives and the strategic framework within which parliament will decide its priorities for the period 2007-13, but also because 2006 will be a key year for achieving the objective of a europe of dynamic and sustainable growth, creating more and better jobs. the year 2006 will present enormous challenges for europe. in addition to meeting the financial needs of a union of 25, it is essential to ensure that the institutional and political changes resulting from the new constitutional treaty are carried out in the best possible way. it is therefore essential that europe be able to meet these challenges with coherent, well-coordinated and sufficiently funded actions, and that the 2006 budget be able to provide the appropriate response. but the european challenges for 2005/2006 do not end with the consolidation of enlargement and the new treaty, and decisions on various ongoing enlargement processes, the strengthening of the eu on the international scene and the launching of new measures to revive the lisbon strategy must be added to the list of challenges, and the resources needed to implement and sustain them must also be available. i voted yes.

in writing. i welcome the expected final adoption of the proposed regulation which, by repealing it, will clarify, simplify and update the provisions of the existing regulation (regulation (eec) no 3820/85). individual interpretations, which have previously given rise to legal disputes, will be avoided and the obligations of employers and workers will also be clarified, with the overall aim of improving the application of the regulation. the rapporteur has once again shown that he is working towards the council's common position and thereby speeding up the adoption of this relevant legislation. important changes will come about in terms of compulsory daily rest, the limit of weekly driving hours or the adoption of a legal framework allowing member states to impose penalties for serious infringements. the main objective of improving road safety is expected to be better achieved. i also hope that a fair competition environment will be promoted and at the same time that the social interests of those involved in road transport will be safeguarded. in the amendments i voted in favour of balanced proposals which take account of the special needs and interests of the most peripheral countries, such as portugal.
in writing. we voted against the joint resolution on the spring european council because they did not accept the positions we took, nor the proposals we put forward, of which i would stress: - notes the agreement of the european council on the reform of the stability and growth pact; considers that this constitutes an implicit acknowledgement that the 1997 stability and growth pact had negative consequences for employment, public investment and real convergence and prolongs the stagnation of the european economy; considers it essential, therefore, to repeal the stability and growth pact; - strongly criticises the fact that 'structural reforms' can be taken into account in budgetary assessments, as this will lead to perverse anti-social incentives which will lead member states to dismantle social security and the welfare state in order to avoid penalties under the excessive deficit procedure; - stresses the council's statement on the current wording of the proposal for a directive on services in the internal market, stating that it 'does not fully meet the requirements' of preserving the european social model, but regrets that the council did not take the opportunity to reject this proposal in its entirety. - believes that the fight against income inequalities and the promotion of real convergence should be at the top of the eu's economic and social agenda.
in writing. the vote in favour of this resolution does not prevent me from expressing some disillusionment with the outcome of the european council of 22 and 23 march 2005. both the revision of the lisbon strategy and the reform of the stability and growth pact have been lacking in ambition. public finances require more restraint, rationality and efficiency in investment, not more indebtedness. on the other hand, the lisbon strategy needed a revision that was more realistic and more geared to a genuine commitment to competitiveness. jobs are not created by decree, they are created by a healthy economy, and it cannot be said that the union has clearly gone that way.
in writing. the european council in brussels will, in the first instance, be inexorably linked to the review of the criteria of the stability and growth pact, which have been amended there after successive cases of non-compliance. these changes, while not being linked to the excessive rigidity of the previous model, need to be separated from the lack of clarity which, if not avoided, could have a negative impact on the international credibility of the euro and the stability of the public accounts of the member states. another relevant aspect that drew the council's attention was the relaunch of the lisbon strategy, which had failed at this intermediate stage of implementation. i think that the strategy has been a victim of its own ambition and the vague, almost proclaiming nature of some of the proposed targets, without a corresponding concrete and properly marked itinerary. while maintaining ambition, one wishes for more realism. despite some reservations about parts of the services directive, mainly because of the enunciation and defence of the so-called 'country of origin principle', i believe that it contains largely positive aspects which deserve to be exploited and put into practice at european level. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by the ppe/de group, considering that it clearly and critically identifies the main concerns of the european council.
the european security strategy challenges us to reflect on the union's role in world governance. the reports by mr brok and mr kuhne make excellent contributions to the challenge. to be effective and coherent, european foreign and security and defence policies must put the citizen at the centre, promoting human rights, international and humanitarian law and multilateralism in international relations, that is to say, they must be based on the concept of human security, as the kuhne report - in line with the important barcelona report on the doctrine of human security - underlines. this vice-president of the commission. mr president, let me begin by dealing with the specific case at issue. the commission is aware of the plans for the closure and possible relocation of the innovia films plant in bridgwater and we have asked the services to examine whether the measures taken by the state of kansas constitute a breach of wto rules. we will also explore, in cooperation with the member states concerned, whether any other remedy is available under international law in this situation. i wish to add that my own political judgement with regard to this case is absolutely the same as that expressed by honourable members in the debate. if us state aid rules apply in kansas, that is certainly a practice that is not allowed here. however, fortunately or unfortunately, the state of kansas is not part of the european union. in particular this involves looking at the possibilities offered by the complaint procedure in the context of the oecd guidelines for multinational enterprises, which state that oecd enterprises should refrain from seeking or accepting exemptions not contemplated in the statutory or regulatory framework related to environmental, health, safety, labour, taxation, financial incentives or other issues. it should be noted, however, that these guidelines and the recommendations that may result from the complaint procedure are not legally binding. as regards the wto, the commission is evaluating the compatibility of the measures taken in kansas with the wto agreement on subsidies and countervailing measures. these rules, while in principle allowing wto members to decide on their own fiscal regime, prohibit tax exemptions when they directly promote exports. that is the case that we have to examine: whether the measures in kansas directly promote exports. if so, they run against wto rules. i wish to add a few general remarks on the role of the wto in the area of environmental policy. let me first stress that wto members have explicitly recognised the importance of working towards sustainable development and making international trade and environmental policies mutually supportive. the european union plays a particularly active role in this respect, but the work is not complete. wto members are free to choose their own environmental policy at national, regional and, in the case of multilateral environmental agreements, global level. this also implies that any action against illegal breaches of existing regional, national or international environmental legislation should be taken at those levels. the appropriate answer to ‘environmental dumping’ at global level is, therefore, to enhance environmental governance by means of legally binding instruments such as multilateral environmental agreements, and the commission is very active in that field. as regards the other question raised, about harmful tax competition in the european union, all eu member states are committed to the code of conduct on business taxation. the code aims at combating specific tax measures that affect, or may affect, the location of business within the community. almost all the harmful tax measures identified following a peer review process have been or are in the process of being removed. more generally, the commission’s tax policy aims at promoting the principles of the code towards third countries in order to tackle harmful tax competition on as wide a geographical basis as possible. in this respect, the commission has already included a reference to the principles of the code in several international agreements with third countries and aims at including this reference in future agreements. furthermore, the commission supports the oecd efforts to remove harmful tax practices.

for the gue/ngl group mr president, mrs murko said in her speech that cultural diversity is intended to defend and protect minorities. it happens that today all cultures in the globalized world are minority cultures, minority cultures, but that is not the reality that is translated by the markets. this is where the problem lies. it is ignorance that is against cultural diversity, but there are also those who consider culture as a mere commodity, there are also those who maintain that the current global media are mere platforms for the "production of content". this trend is now dominating the stage of international trade negotiations and is manifested in the european union itself, in various governments and, for example, in the proposal for a directive on the liberalization of services. that's why this debate is so important right now. because what is being argued here, and what the committee on culture has been arguing, is that we need another way, a way that commits this parliament, the european institutions and each member state to other priorities, other policies, other instruments. the resolution is very clear. states have an obligation to protect cultural diversity. the states have an obligation to protect media pluralism, the states have an obligation to intervene, to invest in the creation, production and distribution of cultural goods. in short, the states have an obligation not to resign. and that is what we are discussing here today again when we call for a common, swift and firm position from the european union in this negotiation.

for the gue/ngl group we believe that the state of fish and shellfish resources warrants recovery measures. these imply the need to restrict fishing, which will inevitably have social and economic consequences. it should therefore be borne in mind that any loss of income for fishermen as a result of temporary stops or fishing restrictions due to a recovery plan must always provide for financial compensation for fishermen whose objective is to offset the resulting losses. moreover, compensation is also an incentive for the commitment and involvement of fishermen in the implementation of the recovery plan, as the main objective of these plans is to ensure the sustainability of fisheries resources as a way of securing the future of fisheries. recovery plans should therefore not necessarily lead to definitive measures to reduce fishing, either by promoting the killing of vessels or by lack of economic viability, given the absence of socioeconomic compensatory measures for the closure of the fleet. the cuts mean the permanent destruction of the means of production and, consequently, permanent unemployment for the fishermen. it is therefore necessary to enter socio-economic measures in this regulation, with their correspondence at the level of the community budget. that is the sense of our amendments which we think are fair. we hope that this will merit your support.

since the beginning of the year we have been alerting the european commission and the european parliament to the serious situation in portugal, as a result of one of the most severe periods of drought in our country, the social, economic and environmental effects of which will tend to be more acute as summer approaches. with the question put to the european commission in january and with the intervention at the plenary session of the european parliament in february, we raised the need for urgent measures to respond to the difficult situation in agriculture and also to ensure that the water supply in several regions will not be interrupted in the future. the situation in agriculture is worrying. autumn/winter crops have been lost and spring/summer crops are also at risk, such as tomatoes, maize, rice, fruit and vegetables or animal feed and the normal development of autumn crops such as citrus and wine. some reforestation after the fires of 2003 and 2004 is being lost forever due to lack of moisture in the soil. this situation puts thousands of small and mediumsized farmers in serious financial difficulties, so concrete measures to support portuguese farmers are urgently needed, such as those provided for in the resolution or, as we have proposed, the creation of a public agricultural insurance funded by community funds, which will guarantee a minimum income to farmers in the event of calamities such as drought and fires, and a financial support line that will minimise the increase in costs and the decrease in agricultural production, as well as the temporary exemption from social security contributions, without loss of rights, for full-time farmers with an income of less than 12 edu and the extension of the campaign credit for two years without interest. on the other hand, short- and long-term measures should also be considered to ensure that water - the creation of a single market for financial services has been a decisive factor in the construction of the internal market and, consequently, in the further economic and social development of europe. in this context, the financial services action plan, adopted in 1999 and reinforced at the lisbon and stockholm european councils, is an indispensable instrument. it is now widely recognised that the financial services action plan is a great success, with 39 of the 42 legislative measures adopted having been enacted; it is however premature to give a definitive judgment because many of these legislative measures are not yet in force. the effort that must be made at this stage is therefore precisely to ensure that the necessary implementing measures are transposed into national law and, above all, that their operation is monitored in a transparent and effective manner over a period of time. the monitoring of the fsap, which allows the impact of legislation on the proper functioning of european financial markets to be measured and the development of promotional, supervisory and anti-discrimination measures to be developed, should be the priority objective of the commission and the member states in this area. among the various aspects which the report refers to in order to provide guidance, i would like to highlight, because of its enormous importance, the call to the member states to implement the directive on vocational rehabilitation institutions quickly and with full effectiveness, which will make it possible to increase the possibilities and alternatives of savers and offer them a maximum return on their investments. however, the main message of this report is that member states need to adopt the 'better regulation principles' adopted by the commission in due course and that national supervisory practices need to be more closely aligned with the measures included in the financial services action plan. it is also very important to conclude that any future legislative measures aimed at correcting market failures should take into account the cost/benefit of their implementation in relation to the economic balance of their absence. mrs van den burg's report deals with all these problems of financial services in a very sensible, coherent and intelligent way and should therefore deserve the support of this parliament.
mr president, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, we are in favour of reciprocity as a fundamental principle of visa policy and we believe that a common european policy on visas should always be based on the principle of solidarity. a mechanism is needed to ensure that european citizens are not required to obtain a visa to travel to third countries whose nationals do not require a visa to enter the territory of the union. however, several third countries require visas for citizens of the union on a non-reciprocal basis. the existing mechanism has never been applied since its creation in 2001. mr frattini has already acknowledged that this mechanism is too rigid and lacks functionality, and he is quite right. in addition to being triggered only at the request of the member state which is the victim, the almost automatic nature of the reintroduction of the visa requirement is ultimately a deterrent, since it entails excessive risks of provoking external crises in relations with third countries, as well as internal crises due to lack of solidarity in the event of a possible blockage in the council. as a consequence, the member states which have been victims of this situation, such as my own - portugal - have always refrained from using it. with the latest enlargement of the union, the situation has worsened. it has already been mentioned that, for example, the united states requires visas for nine of the ten new member states and canada for seven of them. we therefore agree that a more flexible mechanism should be created to ensure greater operability and more effective implementation, to reinforce the principle of solidarity between member states, while at the same time giving the commission a crucial role based on its competence in visa matters. i therefore support this proposal and the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, mr henrik lax, whom i congratulate on his excellent work.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, world public opinion is slowly waking up to the new problems of the day. environmental quality is not a luxury, it must be a political priority as a condition for sustainable development. rulers, some more than others, are coming to realize that the world has changed and that policies must change too. everyone is becoming increasingly aware that the destruction of the environment threatens the future of present and future generations and irreversibly degrades people's quality of life. environmental and health concerns are relevant and timely. ignorance of the past and laxity of the present have high costs - environmental costs, financial costs and costs in human lives. it is therefore necessary to remedy this, but it is above all urgent to prevent it. over a thousand different compounds are now produced by the chemical industry. some of these compounds are persistent, that is, very resistant to degradation in the environment. some of these compounds are bioaccumulative, that is, they accumulate in the tissues of living organisms and are also toxic. among these toxic compounds, persistent organic pollutants, or pops, are prominent, and they are associated with a number of health problems, including cancer, endometriosis, cognitive and learning disorders. pops are also responsible for reproductive defects and hormonal dysfunctions. because they are resistant, pops are passed from generation to generation and contaminate the food we eat, the air we breathe and the water we drink. because pops are bioaccumulative, they accumulate in the environment and in the bodies of living organisms. because of these characteristics, pops spread everywhere and can be found as far away as antarctica in penguins, and in the arctic region in polar bears. it is no use, for example, for brazil to stop producing mirex if argentina does not, and it is no use for the european union to ban ddt if china continues to produce and use it. i would therefore urge that concerted efforts be made at world level. it is important to remember that many of these substances did not exist fifty years ago. negotiations to control the use, production and release of pops were launched in 1995. twelve pollutants have been identified. the stockholm convention, which was concluded in 2001, sets out a set of objectives and measures aimed at better managing pops, but also at their elimination and the promotion of cleaner technologies. in view of the decisions of the stockholm convention, which took place, as i have already said, in 2001, and the objectives and agenda of this first meeting of the conference of the parties, to be held in uruguay from 2 to 6 may, it is appropriate to ask the commission in writing. the regulation establishing the european foundation for the improvement of living and working conditions in 1975 is being reviewed on the basis of the results of an external audit. the foundation's main objective is to develop thinking on improving living and working conditions in the medium to long term and to identify factors for change. the main changes are aimed at an internal reorganisation of its management bodies, greater involvement of independent experts and an increased role for the social partners and representatives of national governments. this strategic and operational review will enable the foundation to pursue its responsibilities more effectively and transparently. by providing information and analysis on living and working conditions, the foundation has made a significant contribution to the development of community social policy. i therefore vote in favour of these amendments.
in writing. all efforts to improve safety and health at work - as long as they are effective - deserve our applause. europe, although having a standard of safety and health at work which is, in relative terms, remarkable, has, however, still much to do to improve these results. the european union is still faced with a clear lack of assurance and compliance with health and safety rules, which is why serious accidents at work continue to occur. to avoid these cases, it is necessary to create adequate legislation, to ensure that it is complied with, and to promote good practice. that's what i hope this agency knows and can do.
in writing. on the basis of an external audit carried out to assess the functioning of the european agency for safety and health at work (bilbao), the commission proposed a number of amendments to its constituent regulation. i voted in favour of this report because the amendments seek to clarify the objectives and responsibilities of the agency, improve its operation, strengthen the role of the social partners and increase cooperation with other bodies active in the social field. the agency plays a key role in disseminating information and promoting exchanges of experience on health and safety at the workplace. this task is essential in the face of the real tragedy of workplace accidents, which have incalculable human and financial costs. the agency also participates in the decision-making process by providing the european institutions with information relevant to the adoption of legislation in the social field, in particular as regards the impact of this legislation on smes. in addition to this role of collecting and disseminating information, the agency will now analyse data on occupational safety and health. any amendment that makes this agency more transparent and efficient deserves my unequivocal support.
in writing. in international affairs the eu must bear in mind that different member states deal with third countries in different ways, and legislation must therefore ensure that each member state is able to act and react to its own situation in the world. the flexibility of a mechanism which, although necessary, was not put into practice because it was essentially difficult to use, seems to me to be fully justified. i would also add that the fact that the door is open to the possibility of using other types of action besides the reciprocity mechanism itself seems to me to be useful and potentially effective. i therefore believe that the solution we have found deserves our support.

in writing. the financial services action plan was born almost a year before the lisbon strategy, but it is one of its fundamental pillars. the objective of creating an internal market for financial services and integrating capital markets is not only to further liberalize investment and capital movements, to give large multinational companies the means to restructure and raise capital at lower cost, to speed up the process of acquisitions and mergers of companies at european level, but above all to manage the enormous financial flows released by the progressive privatisation of national pension systems. it is ironic, although the rapporteur is not satisfied, that 39 of the 42 legislative measures in this plan have already been adopted, that is to say that the objectives of this plan are those that are best implemented, especially in the face of the timid social objectives included in the 'lisbon strategy'. and all this is done in technical jargon, with almost no prudential rules, leaving self-regulation to the discretion of the sector's agents. more jobs and economic growth are promised, but the consequences of this progressive 'financialisation' of the economy are clearly visible in the high number of regional and global financial crises and the flight of investment from the productive sphere to areas of capitalisation and speculation.

the cinematography of the member states of the european union as a historical, cultural and civilizational heritage must not only be preserved and enhanced by all means, but also made widely available for research purposes and also for cultural training and enjoyment, a principle which obviously applies to all other forms of manifestation of european cultural heritage. it is through such concrete policies and lines of action, which involve the preservation of memory and its maintenance in a fertile and multifunctional state, that the plurality of cultures of the member states of the european union and the extraordinary spiritual and material wealth that corresponds to them are defended. it is also in this way that the essential european added value which should be a feature of cultural projects supported by the union's institutions can be achieved and stimulated. european culture can assert itself vis-à-vis the cultures of third countries only by strengthening its own value, which takes all citizens who identify with it to ever higher levels of qualitative demand, both in their cultural creations and in their cultural consumption. europe does not have to defend itself against cultural products of cultural quality from other sources. if they do, they reflect the dignity of the human spirit and europe needs them too. but it's worth competing with them, at least on the same quality level. and against the spurious products from which it can be invaded, that is also what europe's defence is about and not in conventions to be secured in the instances of political correctness ostensibly proclaimed for the protection of cultural diversity, but in fact prepared to set up barriers in the name of more or less corporate and more or less parochial interests. i shall therefore vote in favour of this recommendation, even though i have some doubts about its legal validity, since even if it is called a recommendation, it is aimed at a harmonization which the treaty excludes.
the proposal before this house is balanced and sensible. that's why it's a good proposition. it is in line with the lisbon strategy and protects small and medium-sized enterprises. this proposal also includes significant elements of labour market flexibility. however, there are points of controversy. first, the opt-out. the possibility of maintaining the opt-out practice would mean that the european union would adopt a directive on sensitive aspects of minimum standards for health and safety at work, only to say in the same directive that whoever wants to comply with these minimum standards, does not comply with them. the continuation of this practice cannot therefore be seen as an element of flexibility. it would mean deregulation in a sensitive area such as health and safety at work. the european economy needs more flexibility in the labour market, but not at the expense of the absence of rules. there are other more effective ways of ensuring labour market flexibility, such as the one included in this proposal, which relates to the extension of the reference period. it is guided by the principle of subsidiarity, which leaves the member states free to choose the reference period between 4 and 12 months in accordance with their national realities and not the european union to unilaterally impose a fixed duration. finally, on working time and rest time, there is no reason why the european parliament should not comply with the case law of the court of justice. the principle of subsidiarity is once again put into practice in this proposal, which allows the member states to define the methods of calculation which they consider most appropriate for the purposes of wages and the calculation of working time. it should be made clear that the proposal presented has no other impacts than those i have just mentioned.
this proposal for a directive on working time is one of the most dangerous marks of the attack on workers' rights, calling into question the gains of a struggle of more than a hundred years, affecting millions of workers and their families. we therefore insist on the need to withdraw this proposal from the european commission and to draw up a new one completely abolishing the opt-out, refusing to classify idle time, respecting the case law established by the court of justice, facilitating the reconciliation of work and private life and protecting the health and safety of workers. we also insist on the need to reduce the working day to 42 hours and not to increase it from 48 to 65 or more. what europe needs is to set an example in defending more rights, not to approach asian standards in the name of flexibility and competition.

in writing. we voted in favour of the report approving the agreement between the ec and switzerland on the participation of that country in the eea and the european environment information and observation network. the aim of the agreement and of swiss participation is to provide objective, reliable and comparable information on the environment. switzerland will retain observer status without voting rights in the european environment agency, will benefit from equal treatment with regard to the provision of data, information and analysis in the field of the environment, and will create an infrastructure capable of providing standardised data and information on the state of the environment on its own territory. the agreement will make it easier and more accurate to provide reliable and comparable information on the state of the environment in europe and will also allow for better integration of the assessments and data provided on ecosystems shared by switzerland and neighbouring countries.

in writing. the undersigned voted against amendment no 27 to the maaten report on bathing water quality because epidemiological studies have shown that there are differences between the two types of water: coastal and inland waters. in particular, according to these studies, the fecal contamination hazards for children (who are the group at greatest risk) are caused by a variety of bacteria, so it makes perfect sense to maintain the distinction between coastal and inland waters, as was proposed by the council. the undersigned also voted against amendments nos 5, 7, 8, 12 and 32 because they consider the existence of the 'sufficient' category for bathing water classification to be a positive factor. this classification would allow a gradual evolution of a bathing water body which, in compliance with the directive, would be in a conditional situation awaiting its evolution to the good and excellent classifications.
in writing. the amendments proposed by the rapporteur to the proposal for a directive on the management of bathing water quality are generally positive, although we disagree with the abolition of the distinction between coastal and inland waters, insofar as in portugal it would mean that certain bathing areas, in particular river beaches, would be classified as unsuitable, despite having the conditions for their use without public health problems, since epidemiological studies have shown that there are in fact differences between these two types of water. so here, as in other matters, it is essential to follow the recommendations of the world health organization. as regards sufficient classification, this would only be acceptable if it was understood as the minimum quality and to be improved within a specified short time, which was not the case. the advance of the date for classification also raises problems, taking into account the water framework directive itself. as regards information for the population and possible emergency plans for areas where flooding is common, i think this is a positive step and we have therefore supported these proposals.
in writing. the european parliament's committee on the environment adopted on 21 april 34 amendments to the council's common position on bathing water quality management. as regards amendment no 27, which seeks to remove the distinction between 'coastal waters' and 'inland waters' in annex i, i must express my total disagreement. portugal has advocated a clear distinction between these waters, since epidemiological studies have shown differences in quality indicators and levels of bacteriological activity in one and other media. it is concluded that if the bacterial indicators are different and act differently, then the two types of water deserve different criteria with regard to their epidemiological assessment. since the recommendations of the world health organisation and the scientific studies supporting them have so far been to differentiate between 'coastal and inland waters', i see no reason to take decisions to the contrary, especially since they would mean that in portugal some 21% of bathing areas currently comply with the classification. i therefore consider that this proposal from the ep should not deserve my support.
in writing. this bathing water quality report is very important for my country. the portuguese coast stretches for many kilometres, where bathing in the sea is a popular recreational activity. the same is true of some inland bathing areas. the requirements for safe use of designated bathing areas are not only linked to access to, infrastructure and safety of beaches, but increasingly to the quality of the water found there. the quality of bathing water is thus not only a factor in health, but also an important indicator of environmental quality and tourist development. however, in this report i cannot agree with the proposal to remove the distinction between coastal and inland waters, as there are differences between these two types of waters, or to remove the 'sufficient' classification which gives member states more leeway in terms of managing bathing water compliance. acceptance of these two amendments would have serious implications for portugal, given that the costs involved would be disproportionate to the benefits obtained.
in writing. the increasingly demanding protection of the environment is undoubtedly both necessary and desirable. but since there is no need for such a policy to be incompatible with economic growth and development, it is necessary that the measures taken in this context should not, by appearing to be an uncompromising defence of the environment and public health, result in actual damage to the economy, in particular to the tourism sector which is so important for portugal. but in this report, and more specifically in some of the amendments proposed to it, that balance was not guaranteed, quite the contrary, and some of them did not even have the necessary scientific support. i therefore voted in favour of the report, but i voted against the amendments which, in my view, were prejudicial to the reasonable and justified national interests, in particular by providing for the non-inclusion of the sufficient category in the assessment of water quality and by failing to make the necessary and justified distinction between coastal and inland waters.

for the record, mr. deputy. i would like to make the same announcement as i have already made: i consider question time closed. (the sitting was suspended at 6.20 p.m. and resumed at 9.05 p.m.)
the challenge of constitutionalising europe lies in the area of its external action, which is perhaps the most complex, controversial and fascinating. through its external action, europe is teaching the world the lessons of a new style of governance based on the active sharing of democratic values and the affirmation of human rights. that is why the european external action service is not just a means of administrative and financial rationalisation, of organizational will. the service shows that the european union's foreign policy is now marked by a project of common life, a model of consensus on the great horizon of humanity that europe is drawing for itself and for its relations with the world. all this requires concerted action across the board by the institutions and the democratic underpinning of foreign policy decisions. the emerging constitution shows that the common foreign policy is now decided on a basis which is not exclusively intergovernmental, that it is transversal to the european institutions which process the political decision and that the intervention of the commission itself immediately sets in motion a link with parliament. a coherent europe with a clearly defined strategic vision along the lines of multilateralism and a new system of international law requires an adaptation of the relationship between its institutions, the synergy of its actors and permanent internal consensus. this is the spirit of the new european external action service. the service thus raises the following questions: what is its organisational structure? how will you manage your immense multidisciplinarity? how will you establish your chains of authority? how will you prevent a possible field of tension between the council and the commission, if not even tendencies towards feudalism in relations between the council and the commission? and finally, how will you define the links of responsibility, including here the links of democratic responsibility?
we do not want to join the boat of those who, in seeking to evade their deep responsibility for the objectives and the conduct of the wto negotiations by promoting and trying to impose a blind and violent liberalisation of world trade with very serious economic and social consequences, are now trying to shake the waters off the coat by trying to blame china for all the evils. it is a discourse which also seeks to mystify the fact that the real beneficiaries of the current liberalization of world trade are the large economic and financial groups. they are the ones who off-load their production in search of maximum profit, they are the ones who dominate distribution and get the lion's share. the textile and clothing sector is an example of this alarming reality. it is not china that is responsible for the way the textile and clothing negotiations in the wto have been conducted, but the european commission and the council. china is not responsible for an overvalued euro which accentuates the difficulties and competitiveness of textiles and clothing produced in the countries of the european union. it is not china, but the european commission and the council, which have not yet triggered the safeguard clause despite the serious situation facing the textile and clothing sector in the european union, particularly in countries such as portugal, and which are instead protecting this urgent decision. so i ask: when will the safeguard clauses be triggered? when will the mandate of the european commission for the wto negotiations be reviewed? what is required is the suspension and reversal of the current policies of trade liberalization. what is needed is the creation of a system of fair and equitable trade, geared to the real development of the potentialities of each country in a sustained way, without relations of domination and dependence, and thus to the urgent improvement of the living conditions of the peoples of the world and the guarantee of their rights.
i believe that mr chiesa has put his finger on the problem. and the finger on the wound is the huge divorce that exists between the european institutions, their leaders and the citizens. this is solved first and foremost by good policies and not just, or primarily, by good techniques. and where i strongly share the commissioner's view is that when we talk about communication we are talking about two and when we talk about two we are not talking about one who gives the information and another who receives it. this is a pre-modern conception which continues to prevail in the opinions of european leaders. i would like to make three comments on the report, which makes a great effort to reach consensus or convergence. the first concerns the boundaries between culture and communication. all culture is communication but the reverse is not true. and that is why we are against the european union, against the institutions being able to finance fiction, films, cultural creations to spread and promote european ideals. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the end of the year. the second objection is about the boundaries between information and propaganda. we may want to involve the institutions in the referendum campaigns, but the essential thing is - because it is a question of communication - to guarantee the contradictory, the right to contradict, and that is not in the proposal we have to discuss. and thirdly, the problem of intelligence in the use of public means and money. the idea of a parliamentary channel is bureaucratic, old-fashioned, time-stopped. this is a terrible idea. on the contrary, the bet on euronews, the bet on information with the safeguarding of editorial independence, that is the way, it is the way in which people can see news of what they do not like.
