in writing. the resolution adopted today by the european parliament welcomes the decision to hold a seminar of government experts to discuss the european union's role in combating climate change, supporting sustainable energy r & d and limiting emissions from road, air and sea transport, which we support, while underlining the need for effective measures and political will for the commission and the member states to be part of this effort, by presenting proposals for a future strategy based on the kyoto protocol, technological innovation and development of environmental technologies. as stated in the resolution, we also regret that several countries have not yet ratified the kyoto protocol, including the united states of america, which is responsible for a large proportion of emissions. finally, it should be noted that there is a need for greater financial support for adaptation measures in developing and least developed countries, although it is true that developing countries do not have to repeat the same polluting practices of industrialized countries. but all countries have the right to development, and so they need to be guaranteed the support they need for proper development.
in writing. the kyoto protocol is rightly considered to be an instrument of the utmost importance in the field of climate change. it is important, however, that the proclamation of principles and the public assumption of obligations of various kinds, which have been repeatedly reaffirmed, be followed by concrete action. in environmental matters, as in most other matters, good intentions are seldom followed by consequences. and calling upon them is not the same as following them. i therefore believe that the serious and distant study of political - and geopolitical - struggle is a path that should be encouraged.

in writing. we all share the general aversion to the horror of world war ii, and we feel the importance of remembering what humanity, peoples and each individual was capable of. we therefore sincerely share the feeling that this occasion should serve above all to say: never again. this is the basis on which the eu was created. but there are the other memories. for the countries of eastern europe, particularly the baltic states, the celebration of the end of the war is not exactly the celebration of liberation, since the liberators were the soviet military who only left in 1989 onwards. for this reason, what may seem to be a misplaced idea - to confuse the soviet empire with the end of the war - is not so from the perspective of this part of europe, because one thing is inseparable from the other. how can anyone be asked to celebrate liberation if liberation is not followed by occupation? we can't. we have to. if we want peace, we need the truth. let us celebrate the end of world war ii, but let us not think that the horrors ended there. the memory of others must also be part of our own memory.

in writing. the european union's information and communication strategy must always be objective and respect pluralism, cultural diversity and human rights. the practice we see, particularly now with regard to the draft european constitution, is that there is no objectivity or pluralism. there is a major propaganda campaign which does not respect pluralism and the different opinions of members nor does it take account of the different public opinions. this report is a clear example of the manipulation of the european union's information and communication strategy. the european parliament has a duty to support the ratification of the european constitution, and it is not the council's responsibility to support the ratification of the european constitution. it also ignores contrary opinions. unfortunately, however, in the vote in plenary, several proposals which would have improved the report were rejected, so we had no choice but to vote against it.
in writing. political institutions can only have one communication strategy: truth and transparency. to which must be added a readiness to listen as much as to be heard. if it is true that the vast majority of europe's citizens feel close to the essence of the spirit of the european union, it is no less true that there is a distance between what they experience on a daily basis and even the content of some of its fundamental texts. it is therefore our task, in full transparency and truth, in full respect for pluralism, to make the union visible and to pay attention to the feelings of the citizens. all communication is bi-unicode, and that is one of its most democratic features. we understand you, yes.

first of all, i would like to apologize to the spanish member of my confederal group of the european united left - nordic green left, willy meyer, who, because of the problems of air transport to which the president has already referred, cannot take part in this debate. in any case, the drought problem in spain is also a problem in portugal. the whole of the iberian peninsula is suffering from the consequences of the drought which has been going on for many months and which, together with frost, is causing a serious crisis, whether in the crops of vegetables, flowers, herbs and fruit trees, or in the great losses it is causing to livestock and to some sectors of the processing industry. but in many municipalities, particularly in portugal, there is a real threat of water shortages to supply the population, and i would therefore like to stress here that water is an irreplaceable public good, a universal human right which must be protected and which must not under any circumstances be treated as a commodity. but in addition to our solidarity with spanish and portuguese farmers and livestock producers, we also express our solidarity with the municipalities and the people who are affected by this tragedy, which may have serious consequences in the near future. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the situation in the community is not worsened by the introduction of new measures. we are also concerned about the risk of forest fires, which are already starting to occur in many regions, and we therefore insist on the need for effective and urgent measures. an effective protection system at community level is needed to protect european farmers from the risks and crises resulting from the situation in portugal and spain. it must be borne in mind that the reform of the cap requires farmers to take responsibility for managing the risks that were previously absorbed by market and price support policies. as a result of trade liberalisation, farming now remains much more vulnerable to specific risks and crises beyond the farmer's control. it is not enough to say that the study of the pilot project agreed in the 2005 budgetary procedure for the establishment of a community insurance scheme will soon begin. we need to move quickly towards the creation of a compensation mechanism such as public agricultural insurance financed by community funds to compensate for the effects of natural disasters such as drought and forest fires and to provide a minimum income for farmers. we also insist on greater openness and flexibility so that the solidarity fund can be used to repair damage to the productive capacity of large regions, to help the most serious cases in portugal and spain in order to guarantee the living conditions and economic stability of many regions and areas. we also insist on a financial support line that minimises the increase in costs and the decrease in agricultural production and farmers' incomes, and on the temporary exemption of full-time farmers with low incomes from social security contributions without loss of entitlement, and of course the extension of campaign credits for two years without interest. we also consider it important to consider the possibility of establishing a european drought observatory and measures to promote more rational use of and, of course, from the european parliament. this time, and in continuation of last month's debate, we want to reiterate our full solidarity with spain and spanish farmers. compensation should be given to farmers, forestry and livestock producers for the significant losses they have proven to have suffered and will continue to suffer. the effects of drought on agricultural, forestry and livestock workers who have lost (or are seriously threatened with) their jobs need to be reduced. in spain and portugal, exceptional measures are urgently needed to promote employment in the affected areas. in my country, the agriculture, food and forestry union estimates that 50 000 jobs have already been lost or are in danger of disappearing, a situation which is likely to be aggravated by the depletion of reservoirs of buffers and groundwater and the lack of operational conditions for irrigation canals. in both portugal and spain, the montado is the species most at risk of disappearing. thousands of cork oaks and maple trees, on the other hand, are dying in the antechamber of death. there are important regions in the iberian peninsula on the verge of desertification. we're not making the situation any more dramatic. the description given is based only on objective criteria and realistic parameters. exceptional situations merit and require exceptional measures. the european institutions have not been blind to this disaster. the commission, for example, has been working to help with its resolution - i would like to begin by congratulating mr nassauer on the excellent report he has presented to us, which has won the support of the ppe. it is necessary to protect the union, its member states and its citizens by strengthening the defenses against money laundering. the perpetrators of this crime must not be able to take advantage of the free movement of capital and the free provision of financial services. we must also cover the financing of terrorism. we know that we are dealing with two types of crime with different natures. in the case of money laundering, we are dealing with the concealment of illicitly obtained capital, and this activity is at the heart of organised crime. to combat it effectively is to weaken transnational organised crime networks drastically. terrorist financing may also involve the use of legally acquired assets to finance terrorism, i.e. it does not presuppose that a crime has been committed but that financing itself constitutes the crime. the aim is also to extend the scope of the directive to other categories of professional persons, whilst always taking into account the need to respect proportionality in the adoption of measures. i welcome the fact that the compromise reached in the second directive has been maintained, preserving the lawyer-client relationship of trust. an effective defence can only take place where there is a guarantee of the principle of confidentiality. finally, i would like to stress three essential points. first, coordination and cooperation between financial intelligence units, without forgetting to provide them with the necessary means to be able to carry out these functions; secondly, it is essential that member states which have not yet transposed the second anti-money laundering directive do so as soon as possible; thirdly and lastly, it is urgent to evaluate the current anti-money laundering legislation in terms of its relevance and its practical impact.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we wanted to talk about employment. jobs cannot be created without enterprises, and enterprises cannot be created without entrepreneurial agents who are enterprising and risk-taking. the ability to take initiative depends on a number of factors. first of all, macroeconomic stability, good governance practices and, above all, the promotion of a widespread entrepreneurial culture, which presupposes trust in policies and institutions. but trust is not something you decree. in the age of the knowledge society, only those who participate in the large decision-making networks can acquire high levels of trust. the large groups and companies will certainly do so, but small and mediumsized enterprises, which account for more than 90% of all european enterprises and employ two thirds of the workforce, are at a clear disadvantage and will only be able to do so if they are able to scale up. this will depend on how they are encouraged to join universities, centres of excellence, in a logic of active cooperation. it is the regions, by asserting themselves as policy-making centres, that can play a very important role in this respect: it is precisely the promotion of this type of cooperation and, through it, the generalization of confidence that is the most decisive ingredient for increasing investment and creating jobs. that is why i say that the creation of more jobs in europe will depend very much on what happens in the regions. those who do not want to understand that the future of europe is at the hands of the regions and small and mediumsized enterprises are precisely the same people who advocate reducing the resources for cohesion policies. i am also referring to the signatories of the famous letter which talks about a maximum of 1% of the proceeds as a contribution by the member states to the financial perspective. let there be no doubt: if we go along with this, there will be no more economic growth or more jobs in europe.
i am pleased to note that the commission has taken the initiative in this area, and that it has also taken the initiative in the other areas. unfortunately, the vague nature of the broad guidelines for the economic and employment policies of the member states and the community and the restrictive proposals in the social agenda are far from providing the response needed to restart economic growth, create the more than 22 million new jobs with rights that are needed to achieve the targets set in the lisbon strategy and promote the social inclusion of the approximately 70 million people living in poverty. when a social agenda truly committed to social inclusion was needed, what the council did at the spring summit was the opposite - the commission has restricted the objectives of social inclusion and the fight against poverty to children, claiming that the situation of children cannot be improved without changing the situation of families. it has also forgotten about concrete measures to promote and assess progress in the area of equality between men and women, whether in access to employment with rights or in wages, where discrimination persists and in some cases is aggravated. political guidelines insist on pointing in directions that are already known to be wrong. the answer should not be more of the same. it is now clear, and in some ways the reports under discussion acknowledge it, that the results of the path we have followed are negative. but the necessary checks are not made and the same policies and measures are insisted on, always subordinated to the obsession with price stability and the adaptability and flexibility of the labour market. the liberalization of the internal and external markets is being pursued, with particular emphasis on services, the privatization of social security and, above all, pensions. the obsession with the deficit and the stability pact continues, when the problem we face is economic, not financial. the aim, of course, is to facilitate wage moderation and to ensure that productivity gains are transferred to the big economic and financial groups, avoiding the real scandal we already have in the distribution of income with profits reaching their highest level in the last twenty-five years. that is why, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a serious change of policy and direction is needed at the level of the european union.
in writing. the good performance of the economy requires as precise a knowledge as is possible today - with respect for privacy, of course - of the various economic indicators. the report meets some of these needs exactly, and i therefore approve it.
in writing. the multiannual programme (mp) for enterprise and entrepreneurship, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), was originally planned to run from 1 january 2001 to 31 december 2005. this programme is the key element of community policy to promote entrepreneurship and support innovation in european smes, so i voted in favour of this report which supports the extension of the pp until 31 december 2006, and which underlines the need to increase its annual allocation to € 91 million. these measures will allow for better coordination between the pp and its successor - the 'framework programme for innovation and competitiveness' (fpic) - but also with the 7th research framework programme. it is important to maintain and extend support to entrepreneurs and smes in europe because they are the backbone of the european economy and their continued growth is a condition for achieving the lisbon objectives. the financial instruments of the existing programme, which largely cover the needs of the new member states, should also be maintained. reducing funds will prevent the integration of these countries into the european economy.
in writing. in view of the results of the programme in question and in view of the general agreement on the proposed increase in the budget, my vote is in favour and is accompanied by the sincere expectation that this programme will have a positive impact in terms of increasing competitiveness and business innovation.
in writing. under the financial perspectives (2007-2013), the eu has established a 'framework programme for innovation and competitiveness' (fpic) to support business, entrepreneurship and, in particular, innovation in smes. to make a transition between the current programmes ending in 2005 and this new framework programme, the ep increased its support to €91 million for 2006. this initiative deserved my support, since smes are the key element of the european economy and the unavoidable lever to achieve the lisbon objectives. a more competitive, economically growing and job-creating eu inevitably depends on the entrepreneurial skills of smes. to realise its full potential, the eu must take initiatives to make entrepreneurship more attractive. this package of measures includes a culture of entrepreneurship, the alleviation of fear of taking risks and the creation of a simple and fast-track administrative framework. although the evaluations of sme support programmes show that the intended objectives are being achieved, it is appropriate to strengthen the coordination between the future ipa and the structural funds in a context of regional development, achieved through partnerships between local, regional and cross-border actors.

in writing. although money laundering is not confined to the financing of terrorism, the fact is that this 'crime of criminals' is of particular importance in the financing of terrorist activities. europe must remember that terrorism is a real and permanent threat which we must face today. and this is as true for the 'new terrorism' which has acquired its own dimension and relevance after 9/11, as it is for combating the forms of terrorism which have been around for a longer time and which are still active in europe today, such as eta. this fight therefore requires constant and determined attention and the consequent adaptation of legislation, but this must be done with full respect for the defence of freedoms, whether individual or collective, and this is as true for freedom of expression as for economic freedoms. on the other hand, it is necessary to know what are fair, reasonable and effective requirements to be made, particularly to economic operators, and what are those which go beyond the realm of feasibility, effectiveness or simply reasonableness. in this balance lies the guarantee of defending freedom for security, without exchanging one for the other.

in writing. we regret that in voting on this report an important article concerning restrictions on the use of nutrition and health claims has been removed. in the article concerned, the commission should set out the specific nutritional profiles that foods must meet in order to make nutrition and health claims and which would be set out with reference to the amounts of fat, saturated fatty acids, sugars and salt/sodium present in the nutrients. we also regret that the situations in which health claims are permitted have been relaxed. in the original proposal, these health claims would have to be authorised, i.e. proven, and in the amendment now approved, the competent authorities will only be informed about the use of health claims and only subject to examination in case of doubt. this process is justified as being less costly, but the truth is that it is the consumers who are the ones who are harmed. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is informed and protected, and this right should not be subordinated to the economic and financial interests of those who give priority to reducing the costs of litigation, even to the detriment of consumers.

in writing. we voted against the report because it continues to obsess over the deficit and the stability pact, when the problem we are facing is economic, not financial. we forget that the problem we have is one of demand, which requires increased purchasing power and therefore higher wages. we forget that we have a real economic problem and that we therefore need more support for the manufacturing sector, and that we need to use safeguard clauses for the textile sector as soon as possible to prevent thousands of firms from closing down and unemployment from worsening to unbearable levels. it is also necessary to make a serious assessment as soon as possible of the consequences of economic and monetary union and the appreciation of the euro in the loss of competitiveness of the european economy and its impact on economic and social cohesion. we must have the courage to suspend the stability pact and replace it with a pact for growth and employment, giving priority to productive investment and social progress. a serious change of policy and direction is needed at european union level.

in writing. the review of the lisbon strategy is based on the triangle of competitiveness, growth and employment. to relaunch its social component, the ec has presented a new social agenda (2006-2010) which, in my view, has fallen short of legitimate expectations. i am not criticizing the underlying philosophy of creating a 'european labour market', nor the list of proposed measures such as the conclusion of transnational collective labour agreements, the promotion of women's employment, the fight against poverty, etc. my criticism is different. i believe that this instrument, which is vague and not binding, is not the most appropriate and proportionate response to the urgent need for modernisation arising from the imperatives of growth and competitiveness. for example, the social agenda gives little importance to local economies and smes as key factors in economic development and employment, which account for over 90% of european business activity. so it feels like a catalogue of good political intentions. in other words, while i agree with the diagnosis, i'm afraid the treatment recommended is not the most appropriate. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the comments made in it on this initiative by the european commission.
madam president, commissioner, under the present market conditions and taking into account the production paradigm in force in most countries of the union, a sustainable european energy policy is only possible if the efficiency of the final use of this resource is significantly increased. the commission proposal underlying this report, although only one part of a wider legislative edifice, is therefore a key element in achieving that objective. the question is all the more relevant now that it is recognised that the level of energy efficiency differs greatly from one member state to another, creating distortions and, above all, waste that is truly unjustifiable in the context of a future internal market. the model proposed by the commission, although based on well-defined rules, is sufficiently flexible and operational to encourage the 25 member states to save energy. the overall and specific approach taken by mrs roth is in turn correct and constructive. by proposing more ambitious targets for energy saving, structured in three distinct levels, it is an active intervention by the european parliament which sends a strong message to the council that the union's energy policy objectives must be met. the setting of even more ambitious targets for the public sector and the creation of an energy efficiency fund to which all service providers have access, from which household consumers and smes can benefit, are also relevant and valuable factors, although the complexity of their implementation must be acknowledged. in the current state of economic development and the actual situation of the internal energy market, it is essential to create new incentives for the promotion of energy efficiency. however, the overall energy policy does not stop at efficiency, since it is increasingly dependent on diversification of sources, increasingly from new energy sources and the secure interconnection of transeuropean networks in a philosophy, as already stated here, similar to the current transport networks. the need for a gradual move towards harmonisation of tariffs and contracts, which would give a real dimension to european energy policy, is also essential.

mr president, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, terrorism is not a new phenomenon, but the tragic events of recent years have demonstrated its destructive power. combating it is one of the greatest challenges we face in the 21st century. i welcome the efforts and work of all the rapporteurs on this dossier. it does not matter how it arises, where it occurs, who its authors are, the justifications presented or the causes they advocate. all terrorist acts, methods and practices are without political or moral justification and must be unequivocally condemned and combated. the tragic events of 11 march in madrid have called into question the effectiveness of the union's instruments and policies and demonstrated the urgency of a new approach that is more dynamic, systematic and effective. the position of european union coordinator for the fight against terrorism, mr de vries, has thus been created, and i welcome his presence in this house. i support a clear strategy to combat terrorism which balances collective security with individual freedoms and which involves, firstly, strengthening the prevention, preparedness and response capacity of the european union and, secondly, the financing of terrorism. there has been a significant increase in funding sources. it is important to improve the alert system for trade in goods and services in order to ensure better control of all suspicious movements, but without compromising normal market dynamics. at the same time, cooperation between public and private institutions, particularly in the banking sector, should be strengthened. thirdly, enhanced information capacity, including the essential improvement of information exchange with europol, prevention and consequence management and protection of critical infrastructure in the fight against terrorism, which implies the development of higher security standards and solidarity with any member state that is the victim of a terrorist attack. finally, a very important point - solidarity with the victims of terrorism. when innocent people are murdered, kidnapped, tortured, extorted, blackmailed or threatened, not only those who lose their lives or suffer the most are the victims, but so are all their family and friends and the whole community.
mr president, commissioner, this debate shows that parliament is aware of the seriousness and gravity of the terrorist threat and is willing to act firmly against it. so i congratulate the rapporteurs i should like to begin by congratulating the authors of the report on their achievement of something that is rare: a document that can be very useful for the washington summit on 20 june. it also made two points. the first to point out that while during the cold war the theatre of strategic operations was europe and the perception of threats on both sides of the atlantic was identical, with the end of the cold war, german reunification, the soviet implosion and 9/11, these figures have changed. on the one hand, the strategic theatres of operations are different, but above all, what is different is the perception of the threat on both sides of the atlantic. if the threat perception is different, the strategies and operational modes of action will have to be different. while in europe we have developed a multilateral concept of 'soft power' through diplomacy, economic sanctions or even political sanctions, in the united states, after 11 september, we have developed above all 'hard power', that is, the thesis of unilateralism, of 'with others if possible, alone if necessary', and in this way the two concepts and the two perceptions of the threat on both sides of the atlantic have become significantly different. what we're trying to do at the moment is to get a convergence, that softpower is less soft, that hardpower is less hard. and above all, the perception of the threat and the ways of combating it must be consistent and complementary. this is the fundamental objective of any transatlantic summit. we can add a second objective to this, which has to do with trade, not only at bilateral level but above all with regard to their joint aggression in the field of globalisation and the world trade organisation. it is absolutely unacceptable that aspects of social dumping and annual meeting beginning on 13 june 2005, that with the adoption by parliament of this proposal from the commission, the european community is well on the road to completing the necessary internal procedures to becoming a full member of this organisation. i am pleased to accept a number of amendments suggested by mr freitas, notably amendments 2, 3, 5 and 6. in particular, these amendments will increase the transparency and simplify the understanding of the content and reasoning behind the need for this council decision, which will enable the community to fulfil its international obligations to become a party to regional fisheries organisations where they exist and to defend community interests in the global fisheries. this will also enable the community to be at the forefront of these organisations and enhance the leading role that it has constantly played in the operation of regional fisheries organisations. i am not, however, in a position to accept the remaining proposed amendments, with the exception of amendment 4, which i can accept provided that the phrase ‘and its certification scheme’ is deleted. i will comment on the certification scheme later with respect to other amendments. i find difficulty in accepting the other amendments for the following reasons. this proposal relates to the approval of aidcp, whereas amendments 1, 9, and 11 focus heavily on a secondary issue of the aidcp, namely, the tuna tracking and verification system, which is already ec law. amendment 10 requires that future changes to the tuna tracking and verification system regulation follow a certain process, in contradiction to the appropriate comitology provisions within the regulation. this regulation is already in force and changes can be made to it as and when necessary. amendments 7, 8, and 12 relate to the issue of aidcp certification and consumer information. again, such amendments are not helpful in this instance since the issue of whether the community accepts aidcp certification is still being considered by the member states and, pending such a consultation, the commission has not adopted any fixed position. the inclusion of any reference to certification is premature and could prejudice the internal debate that still has to be concluded. furthermore, the issue of certification is not one of the objectives of the aidcp, nor is it included in the general measures of the aidcp agreement, nor in the application of the aidcp programme itself. this is a secondary commercial economic interest that is a consequence of the implementation of part of the aidcp, and not a core element.
i have been advocating a balance that i believe is possible between the preservation of ecosystems and the socioeconomic interest of the fisheries sector, which, although difficult, is, as you can see from this commitment, often achievable. as rapporteur for this proposal for a decision on the conclusion by the european community of the agreement on the international dolphin conservation programme, i have had the opportunity to note with particular appreciation that it is possible to agree on strategies which meet the interests of fishermen and the forces involved and at the same time preserve the richness of ecosystems. the programme which forms the basis of this agreement, which the european community intends to conclude, is based on three fundamental priorities: first, to monitor the abundance of dolphins and control their mortality rate associated with tuna catches in the agreement area; secondly, to study the causes of the mortality of these dolphins during fishing operations, while promoting fishing techniques and equipment capable of minimising these effects; and thirdly, to study the consequences of different fishing patterns on the various species of fish and other animals in the pelagic ecosystem. to achieve these objectives, the inter-american tropical tuna commission, which coordinates the programme, proposes a set of measures to be implemented, including the application of sustainable fishing quotas for tuna caught in the agreement area and the inclusion of observers on board each vessel when it goes out to work. ship owners and fishermen, aware of the importance of preserving living resources, have been developing fishing techniques that are less harmful to both the target species and the associated by-catch. the concerted efforts - and this is important to note - have resulted in a decline in bycatch of dolphins in the agreement area using the siege method from about 150,000 catches in 1989 to 1,500 in 2002. in addition to playing an important role in the preservation of dolphin communities in this region, this agreement also has a significant impact on the preservation of the ecosystem as a whole, since it also preserves communities of other species, such as sharks, turtles and other aquatic animals killed using other fishing gear aimed at catching these tuna. all this is evidence of the high level of selectivity of fishing that has been achieved and allows this programme, to which the community wishes to join, to be classified as a good programme. in addition to the technical measures involved, the programme adopts a process of certification of products caught without harming dolphins, and i should stress that only those that do not have associated catches of dolphins can have this labelling, as well as other species for which the offers are not directed. this issue of tuna certification has been widely discussed in the cofi/fao and even in the european commission itself, which, as i understand it, is currently preparing a communication on the subject of eco-labelling. this is an important subject which deserves to be discussed, particularly because, in the specific case of tuna, there are some non-governmental organisations which have influenced, sometimes in a less transparent way, the trade flow of processed tuna products in the european union. i think, commissioner, and it was in this sense that some amendments were tabled, that through the discussion we had in the committee on fisheries, this was an important moment to be able to make the commission and also all the members of the committee on fisheries aware of the need for the european union itself to regulate the issue of eco-labelling. it is my view that a public body must lead this process; while private bodies and ngos can be partners after or before this process, it must be a public body that leads it so that we can have maximum credibility in the whole certification process. for all these reasons, and in accordance with the guidelines of the common fisheries policy, i believe that this programme deserves the positive opinion of this european parliament as regards the conclusion of this agreement by the european community. i should also mention and note that the report was unanimously approved by the committee on fisheries, whose members i thank, the scientists and organisations and, of course, the european commission and the non-governmental organisations such as wwf, which were present at a mini-hearing i organised and which served to explain to everyone the importance of this programme and to prove that it is possible to get fishermen, scientists and politicians to agree on such an important matter as this and which can also give a positive note, as i said, to the role that the european union must play in the future, not only within this agreement, safeguarding what is articulated in it, but also in the whole process of eco-labelling in the european union.
in writing. as the report states, smes represent more than 95% of enterprises in the union. hence the important economic and social role they play, which is fundamental to justifying greater community support. but, like other reports, it insists on covering up measures which, under the pretext of competitiveness, in practice work against micro and smes and benefit mainly large companies, economic and financial groups and multinationals. for example, we disagree with the idea that the 'structural changes' taking place in the european union are beneficial and should be encouraged. thousands of jobs are at stake and the economic and social impacts of such 'changes' are enormous. the rapporteur notes that the analysis of these 'structural changes' is incomplete, but he says that there are no indisputable data on relocations and merely suggests a report to the european council. the fact is that the number of people moving to another country is already high and the consequences are disastrous, which should mean more effective measures to prevent the growing increase in unemployment and the worsening of living conditions.
in writing. european industry is undergoing structural changes for international reasons, but above all for its own reasons. with the exception of the initial phase of coal and steel, the european union has turned its back on its industry, despite the fact that it is a source of jobs, economic growth, service activity, skills and knowledge that a developed economy cannot underestimate. the eu must therefore unhesitatingly adopt a coherent and voluntary policy for its industry, one which is able to anticipate structural changes and develop a solid and competitive industrial base. european industry has no alternative but to distinguish itself from its competitors by relying on its added value, such as its human potential, its capacity for innovation and its sme business fabric. but this support for industrial policy implies a balanced development which preserves social cohesion. the regional impact of recent relocations cannot be overlooked. the structural funds, in particular the esf, could be directed towards supporting the socioeconomic and industrial conversion of the most affected regions. one solution would be to establish industrial activity in a region on a lasting basis by supporting the creation of regional synergies between companies, universities and research centres.
in writing. in march 2005, the council of ministers carried out a review of the stability and growth pact. the aim was to make the jep a more flexible and rational instrument. it was decided to value the 'c' for growth more than the 'e' for stability, given the economic recession the eu is going through. the pec was thus more politicised. however, this review fell short of expectations for a number of reasons, two of which i would like to highlight. firstly, the reform was only necessary because some member states decided, deliberately or not, to flout its rules. more seriously, the eu has set rules which, in addition to not being applied, have given rise to a lax and addictive sanctioning process. the member states are both parties to the same case and are also the judges. they therefore prefer to suspend the application of the jcpoa rather than impose sanctions on one of their peers. the commission, which is responsible for monitoring, should have the power to impose sanctions in the event of non-compliance. secondly, any sanction must be dissuasive and not merely punitive. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the cfp is not disrupted by the introduction of new rules. other sanctions should be given priority, such as the suspension of voting rights in ecofin.
in writing. as was mentioned in the plenary, this reform of the stability pact is very insufficient. what was needed was the suspension of the jep and a major break with the current economic guidelines in order to create the macroeconomic conditions which would allow a relaunch of economic recovery and employment growth. that is why we are advocating a genuine pact for growth, employment and social progress. our vote against was also reinforced by the rapporteur's defence of involving the ecb and the possibility of the commission carrying out financial audit missions in the member states. this is a good example of a report which forgets the fundamental reasons for the 'no' vote in france and the netherlands on the so-called 'european constitution', forgetting that it is necessary to respond to the aspirations of the people.
in writing. because the admission of economic migrants is the cornerstone of any immigration policy, it is necessary to create a common legal framework and strengthen integration policies by defining common basic principles on the integration of legal immigrants. there should be three main pillars: - the promotion of legal immigration, in a global and horizontal approach, adapted to the real possibilities of each member state; - with particular emphasis on partnerships with countries of origin and transit, in particular through information campaigns; - the effective integration of immigrants, with reception and integration policies, which should take account of the specificities and historical and cultural links of each member state. a set of rights common to all migrants in the eu should be defined, but bearing in mind that excessive 'generosity' in granting other rights can lead to greater rejection and be the seed of undesirable xenophobic reactions (such as granting the right to vote). - the firm fight against illegal immigration - by seeking to stem, if possible, illegal immigration and related problems such as the economic exploitation of migrants at their source, while preventing and punishing all forms of trafficking in human beings.
in writing. the bowis report on the development of health care and patient mobility seeks to guarantee the right to seek timely treatment in another member state if it is not available in one's own country or within a reasonable period of time. we therefore consider it to be generally positive, although very insufficient and in some places even contradictory. the rapporteur considers that the organisation, financing and provision of health and medical care is a matter for the member states, although he does not mention the training of health professionals, and is left with a vague statement that the european union is responsible for ensuring public health. the priority of maintaining and providing unrestricted and universal access to public health services in any country of the union should also be stressed, although it is not clear who will pay for it. it is also important to note that health services are services for people who need them and cannot therefore be compared to goods for sale and as such it advocates their exclusion from the general services directive.
in writing. patient mobility is still complex due to differences in national health systems and traditions in medical care. however, patients should have the right to seek timely treatment in another member state if it is not available in their own country or if it is not available within a reasonable period of time. a coherent policy on patient mobility is urgently needed, with guidelines for use by patients, healthcare professionals and funding bodies. i therefore voted in favour of this report so that we can all benefit from this community progress. i would also point out that health services are services for people who need them and cannot therefore be compared to goods for sale, so this subject requires a specific proposal from the commission and should not be included in the general directive on services. finally, following the creation of the european health card, the european commission should monitor its application in the member states in order to ensure that they provide clear and comprehensible information to the public on how to use it.
in writing. the real objectives of this resolution can be better understood by reading the resolution on transatlantic relations, debated in this plenary session, which calls for a us/eu 'partnership' and for its 'active engagement in the reform of the un, in particular the security council, including its composition, ... to authorize the use of force to resolve international conflicts, with a view to increasing its effectiveness and responsibility, as well as the capacity to implement its decisions'. despite its mystifying language, the resolution cannot hide the fact that it is intended that the un should 'legitimize' and 'normalize' the adoption of so-called 'preventive measures' and 'humanitarian intervention' and 'the possibility of using force', in particular by the armies of eu countries 'converted' into forces of external intervention. that is, to turn the united nations into an instrument which, manipulated by the us in partnership with the eu (france, great britain and germany), "whiten" its imperialist policy, its interference and aggressions against the sovereignty of states and peoples. the resolution therefore supports the ongoing militarization of the eu and calls for a seat in the security council, after the adoption of the so-called 'european constitution', for this political-military bloc in the making. peace is also on the nos of the french and dutch referendums!
in writing. the resolution welcomes the current "improvement in the climate of transatlantic relations" and looks forward to the us/eu summit in washington on 20 june and the international conference on iraq co-organised by the us/eu in brussels on 22 june. the resolution tabled by the right wing and the socialists seeks to continue the dangerous objectives enshrined in the so-called "european constitution" and the "european security strategy". they therefore reaffirm the need for "cooperation among the transatlantic partners based on a firm institutionalised framework" to "resolve high-level political issues such as decisions on the use of force and matters related to world order", "clearly recognising that operating together rather than in different or even opposing directions brings more benefits to each partner". the resolution calls for partnership in the so-called 'combat against terrorism', in the 'non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and the use of nuclear energy', in relations with china, india, japan, latin america and russia, in the situation in ukraine, lebanon and kyrgyzstan, in the wto negotiations or in the reform of the un. it reaffirms that nato must become 'a true partnership between equals', recommending 'a closer relationship between nato and the eu', which will strengthen the eu/us relationship. that is, imperialism in its concertation...
in writing. we voted against this report because it is one of the most striking examples of the neoliberal ideology supported by the european parliament. however, the proposals we put forward were generally rejected. for example, they have not taken into account that the years following the creation of the euro area were characterised by slow economic and employment growth, rising unemployment rates and a transfer of productivity gains from workers to employers, as well as by persistently high levels of unemployment, poverty, social exclusion and income inequality in the european union. they also ignored that the european employment strategy, drawn up in november 1997 and included in the lisbon strategy as defined by the european council of march 2000, was the main instrument for promoting the flexibility, adaptability and mobility of labour markets, wage adjustments and changes in wage composition, as well as the opening up to private interests of much of the social security services, including pensions and health, which had a negative impact on the quality and security of the jobs created, workers' rights and income distribution, and the general level of productivity.
in writing. in increasingly global world markets, european companies face problems of lack of competitiveness. at the internal level, european industry itself is going through an intense period of restructuring with job losses and production units being lost. the pattern of employment in certain regions and in certain industrial sectors is changing profoundly. the fact that economic growth in the european union is still below 2% does not help to resolve this gray area either. if the eu is to remain an area of economic, social and environmental progress, member states must firmly pursue reforms both in their labour markets to improve the employability of european workers and in their tax systems to make work financially attractive. the reform of these social and fiscal policies must be articulated in a coherent way as a necessary and indispensable factor for sustainable development and growth. in this context, strengthening the internal market, including in the area of the freedom to provide crossborder services, is boosting the economic growth that the eu lacks by generating more than 70% of wealth and employment at european level.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i and mr joel hasse ferreira, who was absent, believe that it is essential that the promotion of employment and the fight against social exclusion be carried out effectively throughout the european union. the creation of more and better jobs is essential to combating poverty effectively and indeed the quality of these jobs cannot be considered a less important aspect. we stress the need to use incentives to stimulate local organisations that support the effort to integrate more people into the labour market. this line of action is important if, in addition to economic growth, solidarity-based development is to be ensured. in many member states, labour rules and the characteristics of the labour market have changed significantly during the change of regimes and systems. ladies and gentlemen, we must now assume that in a different social and political model, the fight against unemployment and the struggle for social inclusion also involve improving the quality of education and lifelong vocational training. other important aspects of this debate are the consideration of access to housing as a factor of social inclusion, but we would also like to stress the need to effectively support the inclusion of young managers with degrees or other higher education qualifications in the labour market so that they can effectively use the skills they have acquired in the education systems. in addition, the inclusion of these young managers in the productive sphere will contribute to the modernization of the economy. both mr joel hasse ferreira and i myself also stress the proposal of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, which calls for the various member states to devote special attention to eradicating poverty, which affects women, children and ethnic minorities in particular. the lisbon strategy, in addition to the importance it attaches to competitiveness, includes the defence of the european social model. in this context, the promotion of sustained economic development, integrating the creation of more and better jobs in a context of social cohesion, is crucial if the peoples of all the states of the union are to be able to be in one single market, in one developed and united europe.
author. mr president, we are seriously concerned about the situation in bolivia, which is the result of the poverty situation and the enormous social inequalities that persist, but we reject any foreign interference and any attempt at a military coup. we are equally concerned about the attempts of separatism by certain economic circles in santa cruz, which want to monopolize the country's energy resources. we therefore hope that bolivian society will reach a consensus so that the control of the management of the country's natural resources, in particular energy and water resources, will be taken over by the state and contribute to its development and the social well-being of its inhabitants. we also hope that the decision of the constitutional court will be implemented, which declared certain energy agreements signed by the previous government with multinational companies to be illegal because they were not subject to the mandatory consultation of the bolivian parliament. it is also important that the perpetrators of the october 2003 massacres be effectively punished and we call on the oas to take precautionary measures in favour of the leaders of the social movement who are under threat, such as evo morales and abel mamami. finally, we insist that the member states be called upon to take action in the international institutions and at bilateral level with a view to cancelling bolivia's external debt.
madam president, the council lacked the courage to bury the treaty. there is no postponement of what has died, nor is there a resurrection for what cannot be saved. the council still lacked vision. the frankness of your president only illuminates the hidden truth of the europe of governments. with no political ambition of his own, hostage to national egotism, he wants to make omelets without eggs. he's in the grocery business, so he can only fail. there's a before and after french vote. either europe wants to be just a market or it is going to be refounded and move forward by listening to the social reasons for the referendums. the emergence of public opinion is the most important new feature of this crisis, this new protagonist does not want less europe, but more and better europe. the answer is not pause, but the courage of a new constituent process, truly democratic; the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission.
mr president, commissioner, mr president-in-office of the council, i would first of all like to congratulate the commission and the luxembourg presidency on the efforts they have made to avoid the disaster of the european council. to paraphrase mr juncker, the european council was not a failure of the presidency, it was a failure of europe. it was a disappointment. the citizens expected a strong message and received a response without grandeur, without ambition and without a mobilizing idea. the union thus missed a unique opportunity to convey an image of strong leadership and unity. european leaders have fallen short of history, national interests have overridden the values of the union. selfishness has outstripped solidarity. let us now take the opportunity to find answers to citizens' questions: what is europe's role in the world? how can we increase productivity and competitiveness in a globalised world? how to reduce unemployment? how can social cohesion be ensured? what social model? europe is at a crossroads, but history teaches us that it is in times of crisis that the best transformations can take place. i hope we can turn difficulties into opportunities. the world has changed, the desires and needs of citizens have changed. the european union must keep pace with these changes, starting with a change in its relationship with its citizens. but change does not mean changing something so that everything stays the same, as a character from lampedusa recommended - that would be an achievement. europe can live without a constitutional treaty, but it can hardly live without an agreement on the financial perspective. europe must be a political union, an area of cohesion and solidarity, not just a free trade area. this is the challenge for the next presidency, which i hope will surprise us all pleasantly.
mr president, this present time of the european project, marked by uncertainties and anxieties, is also the time that pushes us into the future. it is because europe has become ambitious that it is rethinking and questioning itself. it was to aspire to an inclusive and inclusive justice system, capable of spreading to the world an essential sense of humanity, that europe built a draft constitution. and it was this project that brought europe out of the closet of the offices into our streets and our neighbourhoods. we must admit that the debate on the european constitution marks the greatest moment of democratization in the history of europe. europe is looking for a public space marked by transparency and trust. because there is no middle ground to this odyssey. europe cannot, for the sake of justice, abandon this political sharing. i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the community. without an integrated europe there is no model of europe. without the model of europe, there is no crusade of dignity in the world. political integration is the means necessary for effective decision-making, the consolidation of our system of values and europe with one voice. in the near future, the european parliament's prominence and visibility, networking with national parliaments, the activism of political parties, local authorities and citizens' associations, and the mobilisation of the media are essential. the european institutions have an undeniable responsibility here, because the european debate is not just a sum of national debates. the constitution is this process of seeking consensus in an open and fragmented order. the constitution calls for our responsibility to become aware of a common interest. and so there are inevitable themes: enlargement and governance; the european union's financing model; the decision-making system and subsidiarity; integration and social, economic and political pluralism; the governing constitution or the constitution as a framework order. the way is made by walking.
this was a european council at which the consequences of the double victory of the no vote in the referendums in france and the netherlands on 29 may and 1 june respectively were made clear, and which opened up new possibilities for the fight against the increasingly neoliberal tendencies which have been imposed in recent years in the european union, culminating in their total incorporation in the draft of the european constitution. from the political and legal point of view, the constitutional treaty has been mortally wounded by the positions of the people in these referenda, since only a treaty which has been ratified by all 25 member states can enter into force. the european council of 16 and 17 june 2005 therefore had no choice but to recognise the evidence. yet he refused to do so, admitting only half defeat, and prolonging the agony for a while longer, by deciding to take a year's pause for reflection. it will have to admit later that this proposal, as it stands, cannot enter into force. and even a review will necessarily have to go back to the beginning of the whole ratification process. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment from harmful substances. it is true that this decision has a number of amendments, which we welcome, particularly as regards greater transparency in transport payments, pointing to a real cost base. the members of the european parliament are elected in national circles and are, and must remain, bound to those circles. we reject the federalist conception of the mandate of member of the european parliament, since it forgets the very different social realities of the countries of the european union, in particular the wage reality of workers, exacerbating the distance between the elected and the peoples they represent.
in writing. we have always been opposed to the creation of a monthly 'parliamentary allowance' for all members of the european parliament, regardless of the countries and peoples they represent. meps are elected in national circles and are, and should remain, bound by them. the creation of a single 'parliamentary grant', financed by the eu budget and subject to a community tax, is part of a federalist conception of the mandate of the mep, aimed at transforming the current 'national mep in the ep' into a future 'european mep'. on the other hand, the social realities of the different eu countries are very different, making it inevitable, with the creation of a "parliamentary grant" of about 7,000 euros (about 1,400 contos) per month, the existence of situations of deep inequality and disparity in relation to the wage reality of workers and elected (such as members of the assembly of the republic) and holders of public institutions, especially in portugal, which would be completely incomprehensible. we also reaffirm our commitment to continue to strive for transparency and rigor in the use of the means made available to members of the european parliament for the development of their work.
in writing. the subject under discussion in this report is important and had to be tackled because, especially after the last enlargement, the lack of uniformity in the statute for members was a factor of unjustified inequality. i therefore voted in favour of what i consider to be the most relevant part of this proposal for a statute for members of the european parliament. there are, however, two aspects which i should like to comment on. the fact that this proposal does not cover the current legislature - as well as having a broad transitional period - has allowed me to act with the freedom of those who are not voting on matters of their own interest. finally, the opportunity. the report was approved after the vote, but if the opportunity had been put to the vote, my vote would have been against it. politics is not just symbolism, it is also politics, and the fact that parliament has decided to vote on this matter at this time of deep crisis in the european institutions does not merit my agreement or my applause.
in writing. i welcome the application of the codecision procedure to these proposals and the fact that the court of justice is now taking a position on the border code and, in particular, on the reintroduction of internal border controls. one of the greatest achievements of european integration is the ability to move around without being subject to internal border controls. therefore, they can only be reintroduced exceptionally and temporarily. without prejudice to the police checks that may be carried out throughout the territory. on the other hand, the external borders should be an effective filter to prevent the entry of people who pose a threat to our society, while safeguarding the flow of movement. border control must be effective and efficient, member states must have the necessary human and financial resources for this purpose, and fundamental rights must be fully respected in the application of such controls. i therefore support this report by mr cashman, which essentially supports the commission's proposal for the 'communitisation' of the management of the external borders, so as to ensure that controls are carried out in accordance with the same standards and that the same entry conditions are defined for third country nationals.
in writing. freedom of movement is admittedly one of the virtues most felt and appreciated by the citizens of the european union. at the same time, the question of emigration is one of the political issues to which we must give serious and sober attention. on this note, i consider that the more specific - partly almost technical - issue addressed by the report is nonetheless of no less importance. the practical rules to which both 'internal controls' and 'external controls' at the borders must conform are of significant relevance. first of all, it is important that security and the exercise of authority be properly accompanied by respect for citizens - whether nationals or non-nationals, whether member states or not. on the other hand, the existence of exceptional rules, the possibility for a state, for valid and justified reasons, to suspend the application of the rules, the fact that the possibility of appealing against decisions to refuse entry is advocated without prejudice to the immediate effectiveness of those decisions, and a set of rules on the procedures set out here deserve my agreement.

innovation and the economic competitiveness of europe itself are at stake, as scientists, university professors, the student community, many organisations and small and mediumsized enterprises have rightly pointed out. the common position adopted by the council on 7 march is as unacceptable as the commission proposal for a directive presented on 20 february 2002, on which the european parliament delivered its opinion in plenary on 24 september 2004, and which the european council totally ignored, which is unacceptable. as we said then, we cannot allow patents to be granted on ideas, on knowledge, perhaps even on life itself. we therefore, as we proposed then with regard to the proposal for a directive on the patentability of inventions involving computer programs, call for the council's common position to be rejected. it is the right proposal at the moment, the only one which prevents us from embarking on a very dangerous path for innovation and knowledge. as we know, the copyright system today already provides great protection to software authors by allowing them to have control over the uses given to their work. but it is not acceptable to call into question the possibility for anyone to sit down at a computer and write the software they want, provided they know how to do it, or for a company to develop software specifically for their needs. concentrating the right to create software in the hands of a few would bring very serious limitations. it is well known that software has enabled economies to develop and many tasks to be automated and simplified at relatively low cost. now, in a legal framework where software patents are in force, this would not be possible. before starting to develop software, a company or anyone at home would be required to hire a team of expert lawyers to check whether the idea had the potential to infringe any patents. as you can see, we are in a very dangerous situation where, unlike ordinary patents which protect an invention, a software patent favours the misuse of an idea, i.e. software patents are in fact an attack on intellectual freedom, on the possibility of creating and developing european industry itself. in fact, software patents are merely legal mechanisms to concentrate in the hands of large multinational companies like microsoft and others, the evolution of knowledge and the capacity for innovation, since individuals and micro and small and medium-sized enterprises would not be economically able to compete in court with large companies that have an abstract idea. it is therefore essential to prevent the council's position from being adopted. we do not think that any directive is necessary in this area, but if it is, then at least the possibility of creation and innovation, intellectual freedom should be safeguarded and the amendments we support should be adopted.

the european social fund has a history of more than 40 years. it was initially instrumental in developing vocational training and in relocating more than 2 million workers who were at the same time working in sectors which had been subject to profound restructuring. following the adoption of the first social action programme and the single european act, the european social fund has been active in the fields of employment protection, worker participation, equal treatment for men and women, health and safety at work and the prevention of social dumping. the most important milestones in the development of european social policy and with an impact on the european social fund were the maastricht treaty, which established the promotion of a high level of employment as one of the objectives of the european union, and the treaties of amsterdam and nice. finally, the latest development was the draft constitutional treaty which set as objectives of the union full employment, social progress and the fight against exclusion. in view of these developments, the commission has put forward a proposal for a revision of the european social fund regulation based on the following three points: first, the lisbon strategy; second, the need to simplify texts and procedures; and third, the relationship between the european social fund and the european employment strategy. as regards the first, the lisbon strategy, and the part concerning the modernisation of the european social model, investing in people, combating social exclusion and the set of priority actions, such as the creation of a european research and innovation area and investment in education and training systems, in order to respond to the requirements of the knowledge society and the need to create more and better jobs, i think the proposed regulation is an appropriate instrument. as regards the simplification of texts and procedures, while it is true that the commission's proposals show a clear desire for simplification at different levels, it is also true that there are still many areas where further efforts to simplify and rationalize will be necessary. as regards the link between the european social fund and the european employment strategy, i would like to say that, in general, the proposal for a regulation on the european social fund integrates these two realities in a positive way. i would now like to refer to two amendments i propose to the commission's original proposal: firstly, the question of social inclusion. in this respect, i believe that issues relating to social inclusion cannot be resolved exclusively within the framework of employment policy and the labour market, because there are situations which require more demanding and interdisciplinary intervention upstream. i therefore thought that greater ambition should be emphasized in the european social fund's intervention and, in this sense, i wanted to propose that the fund's action should not be limited to the european employment strategy, since its possibilities for intervention are more extensive and that, therefore, the contribution that the european social fund can make to social inclusion should be clearly expressed. there is also another significant amendment to the commission proposal which is now being submitted to this house and which relates to the distinction which was initially made
