the european union has a long history of being a regional policy, and it is not just a regional policy, but also a regional policy. the structural and cohesion funds are an indispensable instrument, the only one with a redistributive character at the level of the community budget, which enables the european union to undertake actions aimed at reducing regional disparities, promoting real convergence and stimulating the sustainable development of regions, their growth, production and employment, as well as redistributing and compensating for the costs of the internal market, when it comes to less developed regions. one of the central issues is therefore the financial envelope, both in terms of amount and distribution. we believe that 0.41% of the gross national income of the european union is clearly insufficient to achieve the objectives proposed and to meet the cohesion needs of an enlarged european union. however, that is the proposal of the commission and of the european parliament itself in its report on the financial perspective. by limiting themselves to this ceiling, they not only call into question the european union's ability to promote economic and social cohesion effectively, but also fail to address essential issues, such as full compensation for statistical effect regions such as the algarve region in portugal, adequate funding for transitional mechanisms, including for the cohesion fund, or adequate funding for the outermost regions. this is a concession to the interests of the countries that signed the so-called charter of the six, which aim to limit the community budget to 1% of the gross national income of the european union. the failure of the last european council to agree on the financial framework for 2007-13 is, among other things, a victory for the signatories of this letter. it is known that the luxembourg presidency's compromise proposal envisaged a reduction in the structural funds' envelope by more than 30 billion for the period under consideration, i.e. it reduced the community's gross national income to only 0.37%. these reports also do not meet the implementation needs, either in terms of the amounts of prefinancing and co-financing or in terms of the conditionality of the cohesion fund to the stability pact. unfortunately, it accepts a new logic for the structural funds and their adaptation to the financing of the neoliberal lisbon agenda, as is the case with the european social fund, which is subordinated to the european employment strategy. we therefore reject the emphasis on competitiveness, competition, adaptability and entrepreneurship at the expense of cohesion and convergence. we have therefore tabled a number of amendments to these reports to address these key concerns and to strengthen european cohesion policy.
the two 'no' votes to the european constitution, which have recently been delivered, are a warning to citizens that europe should advocate a different social model, one very different from the united states of europe. european citizens have been adamant in saying that they want more citizenship, more social concerns and, above all, more of a european social model. the european social fund, the original principle of europe, has been supported throughout its history by cohesion policy, always aiming to help people and therefore the policy most felt by them. in my view, the european social fund and the other funds cannot stimulate a two-speed europe. the aim is not to place the excluded in a situation of ever-greater exclusion or even to ensure that the most varied discriminations in our society become ever more present. their goal is the exact opposite, to put people first. at this crossroads, we have to show people that we intend to continue to invest in them. we must therefore make the social model work. at this stage we must ensure that the objectives are met and that the statistical effects do not make the righteous pay for the sinner. we must ensure that we do not go from comitology to numerology in a linear way and that the smaller regions do not pay for the whole adjustment. what we want and hope for is that this whole package of regulations under discussion today, despite all the funding that has been put on hold, will really seek to implement the europe of the regions with people as the first priority. let us make this mobile the engine of europe.
several circumstances have made it necessary for this debate on the future of economic and social cohesion policy to take place at a particularly critical time for the european project. the way out of the crisis also depends on the way in which the european institutions, and in particular the council, are able to express the vision and solidarity needed to design a regional development policy that is capable of meeting the enormous challenges facing the european union. the united kingdom, which has just taken over the presidency of the european union, therefore has a huge responsibility. i look forward to this presidency with a mixture of concern and hope. i am concerned that the united kingdom is one of the six countries which want to limit the budget of the european union to 1% of gdp, which seems to me to be in total contradiction with a strong cohesion policy and with the ambitious objectives we want to set for future action by the european union. the european parliament is also concerned that the british government's positions on the renationalisation of the european effort towards economic and social cohesion are known, which would represent a serious lack of solidarity towards the new member states but also towards certain regions still in need in portugal, spain and greece. but alongside these concerns there is great hope, because we know that the united kingdom is willing to make it a priority of its action to strengthen the european union's competitive capacity, without which there will be no vigorous economic growth, no less than that of the united states of america, which will also allow a strong pace of job creation. and we will not achieve this unless we have the courage to implement the lisbon strategy in full. a strong and reinvigorated european cohesion policy with adequate financial resources is one of the crucial instruments for delivering on the lisbon strategy. the most disadvantaged regions of europe have enormous competitive and development potential which must be exploited. this must be one of the main objectives of european cohesion policy.
i should like to begin by, because i am going to speak about the european fisheries fund, to highlight the work that the committee on fisheries has done on this project and also to take this opportunity to congratulate my colleague, mr david casa, on the good work he has done on what will be one of the most important dossiers we are dealing with in this parliament. i think it is essential that the european fisheries fund should be the preferred instrument for reconciling the objective of preserving marine biological resources with the potential of fisheries. it is therefore essential that the budget allocated to this purpose is in line with the real needs of the fisheries sector in an enlarged europe facing new challenges. with a financial envelope for the period 2007-2013 virtually the same as that used in the community framework still in force and in a europe that goes from 15 to 27, it seems logical and necessary to me that the overall financial allocation for this fund be strengthened. the indicative level of funds, as already indicated, does not exceed 0.5% of the community budget on an annual average. in addition to the financial aspect, it seems to me that the intervention strategy proposed by the commission should also be adjusted. i am referring, for example, to the restrictions on the general objectives and rules for the fund's intervention which the commission intends to impose on undertakings. it will be impossible to ask our companies to be competitive and to develop technologies which protect the environment if we only support micro and small enterprises. another point concerns the modernisation of fishing vessels. i think the commission will have to reconsider its position on the replacement of vessels in the community fleet. i think that be protected by the cfp. i therefore believe that the derogations already provided for for the spg in the fifg should remain in the new text of the european fisheries fund, and that the possibility of strengthening some of the measures inherent in these should also be considered.
i also want to congratulate our rapporteur, david casa, who has done an excellent job. i would also like to congratulate the commission, in the person of the commissioners present here, on the good proposal they have put forward, but i would like to mention what i consider to be the biggest shortcoming in your proposal, which relates to the natura 2000 network and its presence in the oceans, to the commitments made by the commission in the context of the ospar convention. these are international commitments which should lead to compulsory expenditure by the commission. unfortunately, the commission's proposal, which is indeed good in many respects, has a serious shortcoming in this respect. i would appeal to the commission and the council not to allow this gap to continue and to resolve it in their final decision on this matter.

in writing. we welcome the adoption of our proposal to reject the council's march 2005 common position on the patentability of computer-implemented inventions. as we have been saying since the european commission presented its proposal for a directive in 2002, we have said that the introduction of software patents would jeopardise intellectual freedom, technological innovation and the development of europe's economy, as scientists, university professors, the student community, many organisations and smes have rightly pointed out. the high patent costs would be harmful to small and medium-sized enterprises, which would not only lack the resources to pay for patents on their inventions, but could even run the risk of having their ideas patented by third parties. software patents could still be used by large companies as a way of blocking new companies from entering the market. we cannot allow patents to be granted on ideas and knowledge. maybe even his own life. we therefore, as we have done in the past, signed the motion rejecting the council's common position, which was adopted today. it is a victory of knowledge, innovation and freedom of creation... in writing. although i co-authored a number of amendments aimed at improving the final version of the common position, in the event of its adoption by the european parliament, i was pleased to vote for and see its rejection, as proposed to the european parliament, adopted, because i felt that this was the best way to avoid the adoption of a document which clearly harmed the interests of small and mediumsized software companies as well as the interests of consumers. the proposal for a common position was also not in line with the most correct principles on creativity and intellectual property and its protection.
in writing. the question underlying this report and its resolution is what the limits of patentability of computer-implemented inventions are. it is well known that the most common form of software protection in europe has been based on the application of the copyright system, the proposed method being a concession to the american model. this import does not seem to me to be beneficial or likely to bring any positive clarification to the market, but rather contributes to increasing the difficulties of small and mediumsized enterprises which nevertheless produce the majority of innovations and account for 70% of employment in the sector. in the parliamentary proceedings it became clear that large european companies have sought to ensure the exclusive use of software which controls inventions by means of computers in breach of the provisions of the munich convention and the case law of the european patent office. the rapporteur rightly points out that 'a computer program is no more likely to be protected by a patent than a musical chord or a combination of words. as a grouping of interconnected mathematical formulas, it is a production of the human mind of the order of ideas. and the free flow of ideas is a founding principle of our civilization". that's my understanding, too. in writing. environmental issues are at the heart of policies for the future of europe. i therefore believe that it is essential to create tools to ensure that everyone is aware of these issues and also to promote better enforcement of environmental legislation. the report by mr blokland aims to incorporate the relevant parts of the unece protocol of 21 may 2003 into community legislation. the outcome of this report will provide improved information to the public and a better understanding of the quantities of pollutants emitted by establishments. i therefore voted in favour of mr blokland's report.
in writing. the major problem with this resolution is that it is conditioned by the european parliament's resolution on the financial perspective for 2007-13, accepting a financial envelope for the structural and cohesion funds of 0.41% of community gni for this period, when the increased needs for cohesion in the face of enlargement and the increase in economic and social disparities would point to more. that is why, among other things, we have once again proposed increasing the amounts for the structural funds, in particular to ensure full compensation for the regions affected by the 'statistical effect' and to ensure phasing-out mechanisms for the cohesion fund. proposals which, against our wishes, were rejected by the majority of the european parliament. we also regret the rejection of our proposals aimed at eliminating mechanisms affecting the implementation of the structural funds, in particular the levels of co-financing and pre-financing, or the linking of the cohesion fund to the stability pact, or mechanisms which call into question the objective of spending the structural funds (the 'n+2' rule). we also believe that the conditioning of public aid to enterprises on long-term commitments, particularly in terms of employment, should have been strengthened, as we proposed.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this interim report on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund, and in particular the adoption of a new paragraph in article 3 providing that the regions affected by the statistical effect, such as the algarve, should receive sufficient financial support to enable them to continue the process of convergence and that there should be no differentiation between them on the basis of population parameters. this population parameter, which was part of the luxembourg presidency's negotiating package for the 2007-2013 financial perspective, lacks any objective support and must therefore no longer serve as the basis for unfair and disproportionate differentiations, which merely mark a 'before' and an 'after' in solidarity between the regions of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i consider that it contains a number of aspects which are of the greatest importance for portugal. i also consider them to be equally positive for the european union in which i believe. the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund are three funds of major strategic importance in pursuing the objectives of economic growth by promoting competitiveness, wealth creation and reducing the enormous regional disparities. i am therefore pleased to note that the rapporteur has defended what i consider to be essential aspects, such as the rejection of any attempt to renationalize regional policies and the rejection of any attempt to reduce the limits of state aid to the most disadvantaged regions, as well as the defence of the commission's proposal to penalize companies receiving european funds which relocate.
in writing. among other things, we consider that one of the central issues in the current proposal for a regulation on the cohesion fund - and which was already in the previous regulation - is the conditionality of the cohesion fund to the stability pact. in other words, the possibility of suspending all or part of the fund's financial assistance to one of the cohesion countries - such as portugal - if the decision provided for in article 104 (8) of the eu treaty is adopted. this conditionality is a double penalty for the target country. the rapporteur's proposal to convert this automatic decision into a political decision by the council does not solve the problem. we also disagree with the application of the so-called 'n+2' rule to the cohesion fund, which will place new constraints on the use of this money by countries which should aim to approach the levels of economic and social development of the community average. we still consider the amounts foreseen for this fund for the period 2007 to 2013 to be insufficient, particularly in view of the enlargement of the european union. in view of the rejection of our proposals to amend these and other aspects which we regard as negative, we voted against this resolution.
in writing. one of the most relevant issues in the debate on the future of the cohesion fund is, of course, that of 'statistical enrichment'. apart from all the other aspects of this fund, which are of the utmost importance, my main concern - as surely also the national authorities' - is to prevent the appearance of enrichment from resulting in real impoverishment as a result of the loss of support, thus interrupting a cycle of growth which has not yet been completed. this is the central problem for portugal in the discussions on the future of this fund, this is my main concern and, appropriately, the report has taken into account the need to find an appropriate political response to this question.
in writing. the accession of 10 new countries has posed one of the greatest challenges to the eu's internal cohesion: the disparities in economic development within the union have increased and regional economic and social disparities have widened. this implies a greater effort on the part of the eu's cohesion policy. it is currently undergoing a major reform to take account of the consequences of enlargement. in an enlarged union of 25, the reformed cohesion policy instruments need to be endowed with adequate financial resources and distributed equitably among the less developed regions of both the new and the 'old' member states, in order to further reduce the disparities in levels of development and backwardness of the various eu regions (now the 'convergence' objective) and to meet the new 'regional competitiveness and employment' objective. the recommendations made in the various reports today, in particular in my colleague claudio fava's report on the erdf, address these concerns. as regards the allocation of these funds, we are still waiting for the european council to agree on the financial perspective for 2007-13. we hope that these will be able to meet the new challenges of eu cohesion policy.
in writing. portugal has benefited substantially from the european regional development fund in recent years. it is true that we can object at national level to some - or even several - of the priorities of the different governments for the use of these funds, just as we can express our regret at the effects produced, since we wanted more and better. that said, we must nevertheless acknowledge the enormous positive effect that this fund has had on portugal. just as we should be concerned about the rules that will apply to it in the coming times. i therefore agree with the concerns expressed in this report, particularly with a view to ensuring a balanced distribution of these funds, bearing in mind the need to deal with enlargement already achieved - and future enlargements - without thereby harming the least favoured countries and regions of the eu, with particular attention to 'statistical enrichment' which is not enrichment and therefore cannot be understood as such.
in writing. among the union's basic objectives is the strengthening of economic, social and territorial cohesion through crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation. these cooperation measures simultaneously promote the integration and balanced and harmonious development of the european territory. the union has therefore been creating internal and external instruments for crossborder cooperation within the eu. action to reduce the difficulties encountered in the management of crossborder, transnational and interregional cooperation actions is therefore essential. i therefore support mr olbricht's report on the introduction of a financial instrument at community level to support the setting up of cooperative groups with legal personality within the eu, known as european groupings for territorial cooperation (egtcs), because i believe that this instrument can be of great importance for the balance of territorial cohesion in europe.
in writing. the resolution adopted by the european parliament on the european social fund closely follows the european commission's proposal, with an emphasis on the european employment strategy and the lisbon strategy, although in one or other respect it has introduced some amendments to include the experience of the equal programme, gender equality, the fight against poverty and greater attention to disability issues. but unfortunately four of our proposals were not adopted, namely: - to promote quality of work in all aspects beyond the question of training and the acquisition of new skills, in particular by promoting the improvement of working conditions (hygiene and safety, health and working rhythms), stable contractual relations, adequate wage levels, working hours compatible with family life; - the need to ensure, taking into account the socioeconomic situation of each member state and the social challenges facing the european union, a broad base of support, focusing in particular on increasing the skills of workers, improving working conditions, the objective of full employment with quality and rights and the fight against poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. the european social fund has always played a decisive role in the development of europe, although its areas of intervention have undergone some reorientation over time. the latest proposal put forward by the european commission can be divided into two parts: one that proposes to modernise the european social model by investing in people and the other that provides for the simplification of texts and procedures. although i consider the commission's proposal a good one, i share the view that esf action should not be confined to the regions covered by the convergence objective. on the contrary, i believe that support for people should be provided in a non-discriminatory way. i therefore support the amendment to article 3 (1) which seeks to extend the scope of this fund, as well as the report by mr silva peneda as a whole.
in writing. the european social fund has been the financial instrument of european social policy for more than forty years and has been, it is acknowledged, a remarkably successful instrument. portugal is a privileged witness to this fact. at a time when our efforts must be concentrated on the effective achievement of the objectives of the lisbon strategy, this fund is of very special importance. portugal has the greatest interest in seeing this strategy defined in lisbon implemented, not by successive declarations of intent, but by concrete action, by a realistic definition of priorities and by consequent action. in this sense, what has been proposed here by both the commission and the rapporteur deserves my substantial support, as i understand that both have clearly in mind these concerns.
in writing. despite the positive aspects, two factors lead us to vote against this resolution: - the commission proposal for a regulation on a european fisheries fund reflects, from a financial point of view, the guidelines of the last revision of the common fisheries policy in 2002, which we opposed; - the proposed financial envelope for the period 2007-2013 of eur 4.9 billion (almost equivalent to that provided for in agenda 2000 for an eu of 15) is clearly insufficient to meet the challenges facing the fisheries sector and the regions dependent on it. the increase in the funds allocated to this fund is important to ensure support for small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing, investments in the renewal and modernisation of the fleet, socioeconomic measures accompanying the reduction of fishing effort, the financing of recovery plans, support for industrial, commercial and aquaculture activities, and to ensure the participation of fishermen and their associations, in connection with the co-management principle. finally, we regret that our proposals concerning the financing of compensation for the loss of income of fishermen affected by a recovery plan and the equalisation of public aid with permanent cessation between owners and workers have been rejected.
in writing. the portuguese authorities, like the portuguese political representatives in the community institutions, must pay particular attention to fisheries. fortunately, the sea has once again been seen as one of the main drivers of national development, including, of course, the question of fisheries. in this connection, it was necessary for us to pay particular attention to the report in question in order to defend our legitimate interests, particularly as regards the replacement of old vessels, the extension of the scope of measures to modernise the fishing fleet, the protection of small-scale fisheries, aquaculture and marketing, and even the geographical scope, since portugal must bear in mind the fact that there are large urban centres in the coastal zone - by the nature of our history and geography - which do not justify their exclusion from community aid. as i said, it was in the light of these main concerns that i voted.
in writing. the resolution adopted, although unsatisfactory in some respects, seeks to update the principle of equal rights and opportunities for men and women in professional activity. these inequalities in treatment can occur not only in the workplace but also in the context of access to employment, training and promotion, and monitoring of practices should therefore cover all these areas. it is true that member states, in collaboration with the social partners, should combat the problem of persistent gender pay gaps and gender segregation in the labour market through regulatory measures that make it easier for both men and women to reconcile family and working life. we know that this means appropriate parental leave regulations for each parent, and the creation of affordable and accessible childcare and care services. we also know that the demand for equality between women and men presupposes changes applicable to both women and men. it is therefore important that member states, in collaboration with the social partners, ensure strategies to make equality between men and women a reality.
in writing. the principle of equal treatment has been enshrined in community law for decades. however, it has not been possible to date to put an end to the inequality of treatment between men and women. the gender pay gap in the european union has remained worryingly high in recent years, even though the employment rate of women has increased. the gender-specific wage gap in the european union remains at an average of 16%. this is often directly linked to the possibility of reconciling family and working life. i therefore support this report on the commission proposal to modernise and simplify community legislation on equal treatment for men and women in employment and occupation. i would stress that the member states must make progress in implementing community law, in particular by promoting information campaigns to change attitudes in working life. on the other hand, the social partners can play a decisive role by promoting flexible labour regulations that allow both women and men to better reconcile work and family life.
in writing. mrs niebler agrees with and supports the fundamental objective set by the commission, namely to simplify and clarify existing law by means of this directive. i agree with the honourable member that this new version of the directive is a development of community law on equal treatment between men and women. i support the report by mrs niebler which draws attention to the need to achieve the objective of modernising and simplifying community legislation on equal treatment for men and women in employment and occupation in order to ensure greater legal clarity and certainty. the rapporteur notes with concern that it has not been possible to put an end to the inequality of treatment between men and women. the legal conditions are there on paper and we are therefore still awaiting the results which are fundamental to the social objectives of our europe.

member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should first like to thank the members of the committee on agriculture, in particular its rapporteur, mr freitas, and the members and rapporteurs of the committees on budgets, commerce and regional development for all the work they have done on this report. on 28 june 2001, the council adopted a reform of the agricultural aid scheme for the outermost regions of the union. the origin of these measures dates back to 1991, 1992 and they have proved their effectiveness in promoting agriculture and supplying these regions with agricultural products. however, their management has posed a number of problems. the two parts of the posei scheme, namely the specific supply and aid scheme for local producers, are characterised by their rigid management. as regards the specific supply arrangements, the commission is required to legislate for sometimes modest variations in the quantities of products to be supplied to the outermost regions. this is not an effective management framework. the aid schemes for local production are spread over 56 micromessages established by council regulations. it is not possible to adapt these measures without interinstitutional legislative procedures, which prevents any rapid action by the community when it comes to adapting support measures to specific situations. the commission therefore proposes a change in philosophy regarding the aid to these regions and the adoption of a participatory method of decision-making. the new system also allows for rapid adaptation of measures, taking into account the specificities of these regions. the draft regulation envisages the presentation of a programme for each of the outermost regions in the member states concerned. these programmes will comprise two chapters: one on the specific arrangements for the supply of agricultural products essential for human consumption - agricultural inputs or products for processing - in the outermost region, and one on aid for local production. as regards financing, the regulation does not alter the sources of financing or the intensity of community aid. the community will finance the programme under the eaggf guarantee section up to 100% within an annual ceiling set by the council regulation. part of this aid will be reserved for support for local agricultural production. the amounts are calculated on the basis of the average of the amounts spent to finance the specific supply arrangements during the reference period 2001-2003 and on the basis of the expenditure ceilings applicable to aid for local production. part of the subsidised amounts will be integrated into the direct payments under regulation (ec) no 1782/2003. they are part of the ceilings in annex 8 to this regulation. i now turn to the sugar reform and the outermost regions. although they are not part of the commission's proposal, i would like to make a number of comments on the reform of the sugar regime and the outermost regions. the commission is well aware that the characteristics of sugar production in the outermost regions of the community are significantly different from those in other regions. therefore, financial support should be provided to this sector by granting subsidies to farmers in the outermost regions. the restructuring scheme will be financed by levying a specific amount on all quotas for sweeteners. sugar undertakings in the outermost regions will not be covered by this scheme. this will put these regions on a par with the acp countries in terms of prices. this is an approach which the commission considers to be reasonable. in addition, the french outermost regions, which were the only beneficiaries of the cash-out aid, will receive an additional amount of eur 15 million corresponding to the current cash-out measures under the reference period. the direct payment for the outermost regions will be included in the single framework of the posei programme which we are discussing and, therefore, excluded from the single payment scheme. the french and portuguese outermost regions benefited from the same increase in their direct payments envelope corresponding to the decrease in additional prices as the other member states. the french outermost regions will receive eur 39 million, while the portuguese outermost regions will receive just over eur 1 million. i now come to the commission's position on the amendments. in view of what i have just said, the commission can accept amendments nos 1, 8, 9, 18, 23, 24, 27, 28 and 32 and it can accept amendment no 35 in part. unfortunately, the commission is not willing and is not in a position to accept the other amendments proposed.
the azores, madeira and the canary islands and the french overseas territories are the so-called outermost regions of the european union and are characterised by their remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult terrain and climate and economic dependence on a small number of products. this concept of the outermost regions was introduced into the primary law of the european union by article 299 (2) of the treaty, and constitutes the legal basis for the council to adopt, on a proposal from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, specific measures applicable to the outermost regions. the outermost regions have been the subject of specific programmes, as the commissioner has already mentioned, to deal with the constraints of the outermost regions, which date back to 1991 and 1992. these programmes in the agricultural sector have included two types of measures: the specific supply scheme (ses) which supports the supply of agricultural products to the ors for food and feed, the processing of local industries and as factors of production, and support for local agricultural production. the impact of these measures was significant and had a positive influence on the revolution of the ors' economies. however, as has already been mentioned, experience gained over the years has shown the need to introduce greater flexibility in the management of these two schemes. the proposal now before us, which we are discussing, maintains the two previous programmes but changes their philosophy profoundly with the aim of, while maintaining the level of support that has been allocated, facilitating the management of the programmes and bringing the decision-making process closer to the people concerned in the ors. the commission's desire to decentralise decision-making and simplify management arrangements through a participatory methodology and the rapid adaptation of measures to take account of the specificities of these regions is to be welcomed. i therefore agree with the commission's proposal in general, but i believe that some specific points need to be improved and to that end i have adopted some amendments which are part of my report. firstly, i believe that the possibility of exporting or re-shipping processed products which have benefited from the oda should not be restricted, provided that there is no export refund, because the size of the production and the market of the ors alone often does not guarantee the sustainability of local processing industries which are essential for the maintenance of some of the agricultural crops and for allowing some degree of diversification. in some cases, these industries therefore need to supplement their supply with raw materials from abroad and to export or dispatch their products in order to ensure their viability. while i welcome the measures announced by the commission for the outermost regions in the proposal for a revision of the common organization of the market in sugar, i must say that this does not solve a specific issue concerning the production of azorean beet, which involves the sinaga company, which, under the regulation currently in force and the commission's proposal, will have no chance of surviving. secondly, in view of the deadlines laid down in the proposal for a regulation for the submission of programmes and their approval, i believe that the date for their application should be made more flexible so that there is no risk of the current regulation being repealed before the programmes resulting from the new legislation are in force. thirdly, i also think it is important to introduce the possibility of derogations for the ors in the field of rural development, in order to safeguard their specificities and vulnerabilities in this area, thus continuing what is already in force. fourthly, with regard to the historical figures for the definition of financial ceilings, i believe that the reference period 2001 to 2003 is not appropriate for the definition of financial amounts, because it ignores the impact of the changes to the system introduced precisely in the 2001 reform, and therefore my report also suggests, in addition to what i have already mentioned, that the historical figures for exemptions granted under the specific supply scheme should be added to the calculations of the financial ceilings. it should be noted that this approach, while being fairer for the ors, does not inflate the amounts involved in the support currently granted to these regions. i would like to thank my colleagues on the committee on agriculture for their support and the members from the outermost regions in particular who have worked very hard on this process. i also thank the political leaders and representatives of the socioeconomic sectors in these regions for their commitment and help in the preparation of my report. this report, commissioner, was unanimously adopted by the committee on agriculture, so i would draw your attention to this fact at the outset and ask you to take account of the final opinion of the european parliament on this matter, which will be expressed in the vote. i hope that the commission will understand the extreme importance of these issues for the outermost regions and i naturally ask my colleagues to vote in favour of this report.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budget is properly managed. other i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and all the colleagues (and there were many) from the outermost regions and beyond who were involved in the process leading to the formulation of this opinion. i would like to tell the commission that over the last few years we have already succeeded in reaching very positive conclusions, in particular by improving the provisions of this regulation on issues such as sparkling wine, specific milk quotas in the azores and the fact that we have succeeded in preventing the portuguese government from transferring this quota to the mainland. we are already beginning to understand one extremely difficult issue, which the rapporteur has raised, namely the refining of sugar from beet and cane in the azores. however, i would like to draw the commission's attention to the problem of article 4: the problem of the prohibition of 'processed products' in some language versions and 'products incorporating products which have been imported under this scheme' in other language versions. this is a subject which is extremely poorly dealt with in the commission proposal; it's highly technical, but it's of enormous importance. i would like to ask the commission to do what it has done in other areas: to pay close attention to this problem, to listen to what we have to say, to see in practice what this can mean for these outermost regions, because if it has this attitude, we too will be able to reach a good conclusion. finally, a very special word of thanks to my colleagues in the committee on budgets who have supported a very important strengthening of this programme, a practice which is not always followed in the committee on budgets, but which shows how much this committee takes the interests of the outermost regions into account.

in writing. the commission proposal responds to the need to recast regulation (eec) no 2075/92, which has become obsolete following the adoption of council regulation (ec) no 1782/2003. this new regulation is the result of the implementation of the second cap reform package agreed in april 2004. for reasons of legal clarity and transparency, several articles and the annex should therefore be deleted due to the abolition of the premium and production control schemes and the transfer of the content of some articles and the annex to the detailed implementing rules to be adopted in the field of raw tobacco. for the sake of legal consistency, the commission proposal is appropriate and the favourable opinion of the committee on agriculture should be supported by the european parliament.

in writing. we reaffirm our position of principle against the militarization of space or its use for military purposes. we therefore reject and criticise the use of the european satellite navigation programme - galileo - for military or security purposes, as is currently planned. on the basis of the principle set out above, we think that this system could be used as an alternative to the gps (global positioning systems) system dominated by the usa. it should be remembered that the united states blocked access to this system in order to use it fully in its military aggressions against yugoslavia and iraq. it should be stressed that the galileo system is of interest to countries such as china and india, which could become partners in this project, helping to end the gps monopoly and creating, as an alternative, a project based on broad international cooperation. this is a project which should be used for peaceful purposes, in the framework of international cooperation, with due respect for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. a project which should be aimed at public service in the field of its multiple applications.
in writing. the galileo programme is far from being a mere research project. it is now of great strategic importance to europe as the world's first radio navigation and satellite positioning system designed specifically for civilian purposes. i voted in favour of the report by mrs etelka barsi-pataky (a6-0212/2005) on the development and operation of the european satellite radio navigation programme. the guidelines in this report seek to manage satisfactorily financial issues, intellectual property issues and also mechanisms of democratic control. it is of the utmost importance that the programme is carried out in a well-defined framework, given the new nature of the programme's implementation through a public-private partnership. finally, i believe that this programme will have profoundly positive consequences and will influence the daily lives of citizens in line with the lisbon strategy, as it will create a considerable number of jobs in europe and strengthen european competitiveness through the technology and knowledge accumulated in this field.

in writing. the european commission's proposal aims to introduce a compulsory electronic system for recording and transmitting data on fishing activities, requiring member states to equip their fisheries monitoring centres with technology compatible with the vessel remote sensing system (vsd) and requiring vessels of more than 15 metres overall length to be equipped with an automatic tracking device to monitor their fishing activities via a satellite vessel tracking system (vms). the aim is to achieve the control and management objectives set out in the 2002 review of the common fisheries policy. we have always had doubts about the introduction of this system, firstly as regards the question of respect for sovereignty, but also as regards the cost and effectiveness of the system itself. the results of the implementation of the impast pilot project at national level confirm our concerns about the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the system, despite the overall assessment of the commission. in any event, it is imperative that the implementation of the system not only respects the specificities of the different fleets and eezs, but also that there is community funding to cover the investment and training costs involved.

in writing. readmission agreements concluded between the european community and third countries are of fundamental importance in the european strategy to combat illegal immigration. the fourth readmission agreement has been negotiated and concluded between the european community and albania, following the readmission agreements already concluded with hong kong, macao and sri lanka, and is due to enter into force by the end of this year. this agreement lays down the obligation for albania to readmit its nationals illegally staying in the territory of the member states and reciprocally imposes on the union the obligation to readmit nationals of member states illegally staying in the territory of albania. i voted in favour of this report recommending the conclusion of this agreement and i am in solidarity with the rapporteur, mrs ewa klamt, whose excellent work i cannot fail to underline, in her concern to draw attention from the outset to the problems that albania is certain to face in implementing this agreement and to the need to support this country in this effort. we will also have to pay special attention to the issues of support for reintegration with a view to a sustainable return.
in writing. immigration issues are now of the greatest importance and deserve the greatest attention from us, both as politicians and as citizens in general. it is clear that the existence of an economic and social model which, despite its difficulties, is a case of obvious relative success, acts - as in the history of migration always has - as a pole of attraction. the pursuit of a better life is human and should be respected. but that does not mean that a successful economic and social system can withstand all migratory pressures. for that reason, there must be rules and there must be a way to enforce them. otherwise we would be promoting organised rape, the formation of illegal economic organisations that offer an illegal service. it is with humanism and realism that we respond to the questions of migration. the report we are debating is a realistic and humane solution, and it should also be a sign. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. the idea of dissociating external aid from the community is defensible and has been advocated by this parliament. it turns out that a good idea should not produce a bad result. whether it is simply because it is illogical to promote competition solely in one's own interests - and even more so when it is conducted unfairly or without respect for rules which we consider to be fundamental - or because the aim of granting aid must be to promote development and not to promote developed economies and our competitors, it is fair to consider that the amendments proposed by this report should merit our agreement. it makes perfect sense to link development aid to the indirect financing of developing regional economies. in that case we shall be promoting the doubling of the effectiveness of the aid granted. but when that only serves to promote developed economies and our competitors, it is clear that we are only financing those who do not need financing. in this context, and in view of the most relevant aspects of the report in question, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. we voted in favour of most of the proposals in this report, which is a second reading of the directive which aims to introduce quality environmental legislation which will, as the rapporteur says, make it possible to improve the sustainability of production, reduce waste production, encourage long-term investment and promote companies which pursue a serious environmental policy. the aim is to improve the community legal situation applicable to the extractive industry, which is of great interest to portugal. the council accepted several of the amendments adopted by parliament at first reading. some of the proposals which were not accepted by the council have now been put back and other proposals have been clarified. i think it is important that there should also be an inventory of the waste that has been left over from the past and that measures should be taken if this waste is an environmental problem. we hope that the council will now be receptive to most of the proposals put forward.
in writing. the lisbon european council set a new strategic objective for the union: to become the most dynamic and competitive knowledge-based economic area in the world, capable of ensuring sustainable economic growth, more and better jobs and greater social cohesion. the social policy agenda constitutes the union's roadmap in the social and employment field as part of the overall lisbon strategy. in this context, the european commission has stressed the importance of simplifying and rationalising the current situation, proposing in particular the creation of an integrated programme for employment and social solidarity (progress). the progress programme is the new community programme which integrates the four programmes currently implementing the social policy agenda and a set of budget lines relating to working conditions. as regards the amendments tabled by the rapporteur, i agree with the increase in the financial framework, the strengthening of the role of the european parliament in monitoring and implementing the programme and the involvement of the social partners and non-governmental organisations.
in writing. the recent developments in the textile and clothing sector in the eu confirm the validity of our criticisms of the way in which the council and the european commission have conducted the negotiations, and the appropriateness of our proposals in defence of this important productive sector, particularly for portugal. the so-called memorandum of understanding of 10 june on restricting textile imports served to avoid the triggering of the safeguard clauses, after the european commission had done everything it could to minimise the impact of this measure. anticipating the agreement and its entry into force, large multinational retailers and importing groups soon tried to challenge it. the commission (durão barroso) immediately backed the proposal, which, by proposing to release the millions of items held by customs, simply breached its earlier commitments. we regret that the important proposals we have put forward to defend this productive sector in the eu have been rejected by the ep. despite the inclusion in the resolution of proposals drawn up by the committee on regional development, such as the creation of a community programme to support the sector, the resolution remains marked by the defence of the liberalisation of the sector. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the liberalization of the textile market since 1 january this year has had a profoundly negative effect on the european textile industry, particularly the portuguese industry. even if we defend the virtues of a capitalist economy and an open market, we must understand that if we do not defend the interests of our industries with competitive potential - and there are several cases of competitive potential in the portuguese textile industry - we will soon be faced with a consumer country that produces nothing. and those who do not produce cannot consume. it is in this context that we must understand the questions raised by the opening up of the textile market. if competition is affected by practices which are considered illegal in our economy - such as the disregard of basic workers' rights - we cannot act as if nothing is happening and open up markets to such competition. if we cannot allow this to happen within our own market, we cannot allow it to happen when competition comes from outside. this is the position i have presented and which, in defence of portuguese interests but also european interests, i will maintain.
in writing. the importance of television in our society is all too evident and well known. in this context, it is worth considering whether the rules of a liberal economy are merely being applied or whether there are factors which justify regulatory intervention to protect the interests of the community. language is undoubtedly one of the defining elements of a community, cultural production, cultural goods, are one of the most visible expressions of a community. for these reasons, some form of regulation - other than state intervention to influence tastes, choices or preferences - can be considered valid if it guarantees the necessary space for the cultural expression of any community. but we cannot fall into the conceptual and analytical error of thinking that it is by imposing a limitation on cultural access that national culture is promoted. the balance between promoting sufficient space for the dissemination of cultural production is not equivalent to imposing cultural consumption or - more seriously - limiting choices. by not crossing this border we guarantee the defence of the interests of a community without limiting individual and creative freedoms.

cooperation between all the entities involved. but we may wonder if that will be enough. for example, whether the functioning of self- and co-regulation mechanisms can be expected to provide a truly are increasingly invading all forms of audiovisual and so-called online services. this is a matter which involves areas as diverse as the protection of human rights, the formation of personality, family and school education, the building of citizenship, and, finally, democracy and freedom itself. the subject matter of this recommendation should therefore involve, at various levels and from various perspectives, european and national authorities, the audiovisual industry, internet providers and users and, in general, those responsible who deal most directly with children, such as parents, educators and teachers. but this also implies technological developments and improvements which make it possible to make the measures covered by the recommendation really effective: from flagging to filtering, from classification to a concrete assessment of the legality or illegality of the practices. it is also a question of getting the children themselves involved, of making available to them the means of defence, of mobilizing the associations for the protection of children and their peers, and of providing training and school learning which takes this problem into account. secondly, it is a question of promoting delicate and complex forms of self-regulation, critical exercise and civic awareness on the part of institutions and industries. this is the most difficult point in my view, because it involves a profound change in attitudes and behaviour in an era of fierce competition and profit-seeking. and finally, it is a question of introducing changes in national laws which will allow all the factors i have just mentioned to be combined and harmoniously applied in order to achieve, at least in part, the desired result. i hope it can become a reality at a not too distant date. for all these reasons, mr president, i think we should congratulate our colleague, marielle de sarnez, and vote in favour of the report in question.

mr president, commissioner verheugen, in a time of economic difficulties it is up to all of us to take the initiative to seek solutions, to find ways, to promote progress and development. it is in this context that our report on the future of sustainable tourism in europe fits. when we talk about tourism in the european union, we are talking about one of our largest and most competitive industries, one that generates more jobs and has the greatest potential for growth, even in the context of an economically stagnant europe. but the fact is that we are also talking about an activity which must be sustainable, so as not to destroy its environmental, landscape and land-use planning resources, among others. at the same time, we must be able to respond to one of the major difficulties which the tourism industry raises in terms of economic efficiency: how to combat the effects of seasonality, particularly on employment and the quality of the services provided? in our report we have repeatedly suggested ways of solving these problems. this is, broadly speaking, the picture of an economic sector with enormous potential, which we must seek to exploit by promoting synergies, developing cooperation and making use of common experience. at the same time, it must be understood that tourism is first and foremost a sector where private initiative predominates and where, by virtue of the principle of subsidiarity, policies emanate mainly from the authorities of the member states. this does not invalidate the commission's role, in particular in improving the coherence of its actions in favour of tourism with the related community policies. we are thinking about transport, employment, the environment, the internal market and so on. in the light of the lisbon strategy, this is an activity increasingly linked to new technologies, making the internet much more than a mere sales channel for travel, making it a real strategic instrument for operating in the tourism sector. in this context, we must know how the community institutions can support the actions of the member states and industry in developing this activity. my answer is: with concrete initiatives. initiatives which can help to improve the management of the actions to be promoted at european level, while at the same time making it possible to take positive action in promoting the tourist destinations of the old continent. the most symbolic of these is undoubtedly the proposal to create a european tourist destination of excellence, inspired by the concept of european capitals of culture. the proposal to draw up a common classification of tourist services on a voluntary basis and with the cooperation of industry is also of importance. it could be used in particular for the classification of hotel and catering facilities, thus increasing the transparency of these services and protecting consumers. we have also proposed a controlled designation of origin for non-food handicraft products. we supported the creation and development of the european tourism portal to which all national portals will be linked, recognising the powerful tool this can be for promoting european destinations. we also advocated the creation of a network of specialised training in tourism, stressing the need to increase employment, training and professional skills in tourism. in the field of security, we proposed the creation of a contact group to coordinate information on crisis management, such as health crises and terrorist acts, for a rapid response in case of need for protection of european tourists and support for tour operators affected. in the field of improving tourist facilities, we propose a set of initiatives to better accommodate people with reduced mobility and the specialised training of tourist service workers for this purpose. we have stressed the need to develop new tourist activities and infrastructure to meet the growing demand for older people, who will constitute over 30% of the population of developed countries in the coming decades. in the field of business competitiveness, we agreed on the need to preserve the competitive position of operators established in the european union in taxation terms vis-à-vis operators from third countries, a matter which was fortunately resolved with the vote this morning on the becsey report, and on the possibility of applying a reduced vat rate system to certain services, similar to others already covered. we support the proposal to create a tourist brand 'europe', which represents the enormous social and cultural diversity, the quality of services and the sustainability of tourist projects in the european union, to be promoted through an appropriate communication campaign to potential visitors from third countries. finally, in the field of transport, we advocated the importance of investing in quality, in particular by adapting capacity and improving accessibility of the various means, by simplifying the tourist offer with the use of integrated ticketing systems and also by its proper interconnection with the main segment of tourist transport, which is air transport. mr president, we must finally address the question of community financing. tourism is an essential sector for regional and local development and must therefore be placed at the heart of the structural funds. this pause in the discussion of the financial perspectives for 2007-13 can and should be an opportunity to bring the subject back by creating a budget line of its own. all this must be done while ensuring that european regulation is flexible and well adapted to the needs, so that operators can take action more easily and continue to offer quality and sustainable services at an affordable cost. in a europe where private enterprise is leading the way in economic growth and development, our role as policy-makers is also to support and complement it on this desirable path of success. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to thank all my colleagues who contributed their amendments and their votes in committee to this report, including, of course, the members of the committees on regional development and culture and education. i hope that the debate which is now about to begin will be commensurate with the quality of their contribution and the effort of all of them.
tourism is the responsibility of the member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. it should remain so. tourism must be developed in a sustainable way, contributing to a balanced spatial planning, respecting the environment, promoting and enhancing cultural diversity and historical heritage, ensuring the participation of regional and local authorities, stakeholders and the general public. it is essential and a matter of priority to combat the growing precariousness and exploitation of workers in this sector. it is urgent and necessary to give value to work, to give wages dignity, to guarantee the security and stability of employment links and to promote vocational training. we disagree with some aspects of this report, and we think that others are not sufficiently emphasized. we have therefore tabled amendments to reaffirm the role of tourism in economic and social cohesion, its link with local realities, the need to ensure quality employment and the importance of preserving cultural heritage. we believe that the absence of a specific legal basis in the treaties has not prevented specific measures and programmes to promote tourism at community level from being implemented in the past. that is why we have proposed the creation of a community programme in this sector, to complement the action of the member states. tourism is an important sector with great potential and can add value to a country which is also developing its productive capacity.

commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, women still suffer all kinds of discrimination in the 21st century: at work, in the family, in politics, in society and also in access to health care. and not just in access to sexual and reproductive health. there is also discrimination in diagnosis and treatment in general and particularly in relation to so-called women's diseases such as fibromyalgia, breast and uterine cancer and osteoporosis. this report is also timely and welcome and i take this opportunity to congratulate mrs svensson. women are discriminated against in care because prejudice overrides common sense and respect for others. because of prejudice and lack of information, more women are now infected with aids. to reduce the number of women suffering and to prevent some deaths, it is urgent that all member states ensure access to sexual and reproductive health and family planning. we cannot allow thousands of women to continue to die from illegal abortions, thousands of young women to suffer the consequences of early pregnancy because of lack of adequate support, and thousands of women to be physically and psychologically abused in maternity hospitals because of neglect and, above all, prejudice. even in european maternity hospitals there are women who are left for hours and hours in labour, in great suffering, without any help or attention. as is well known, domestic violence, female genital mutilation, trafficking in women, prostitution and all forms of sex trade are at the root of serious health problems and female mortality. violence against women between the ages of 15 and 44 kills more women than cancer, malaria, road accidents or war. however, in the european area, women continue to be abused, mutilated, trafficked and prostituted, without the authorities of the member states taking responsibility. and what has the commission done? it is also very little in this field. even obvious and simple measures such as breast screening, which is only adopted in a few countries such as belgium, spain, finland, france, hungary, luxembourg, the netherlands, sweden, the united kingdom and portugal, are slow to be increased. it needs to be extended to other countries. health policy is a matter for the member states, but the commission can and should do more in this area because there are many situations which go beyond national responsibilities.

on behalf of the ppe-de group. - mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, as commissioner frattini has said, this has been a long process: the first proposal was submitted five years ago; in 2001, this parliament, through the watson report, tabled over 100 amendments; the council spent two years negotiating and reached the general approach in april 2004. i regret that the european parliament was not consulted until after the council had reached a political agreement, which means that the council will in practice ignore what we are discussing here. the absence of the council from the chamber is a good indication of the attention it will give to this debate. the fact is that, as commissioner frattini has already said, the directive is important. this first step towards the pursuit of a european asylum system is urgent. this proposal for a directive is the first legally binding instrument on asylum procedures. we need to create a common asylum system and manage migration flows more effectively and fairly, both for immigrants and for host societies. and we must do so in accordance with the 1951 geneva convention, in particular the principle of non-refoulement: states undertake not to force such persons to return to countries or territories where their lives or freedoms are threatened. on the other hand, we must understand that the member states want to combat the abuse of asylum systems by economic migrants. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, wolfgang kreissl-dörfler, on his work. i supported many of his amendments, as i saw most of my proposals integrated with regard to humanitarian issues and the protection of the rights of asylum seekers, the need for swift and effective procedures, conditions of detention, protection of minors and other persons in a vulnerable situation. however, we disagree on two fundamental points, namely the disappearance of the lists of safe countries, which already existed in some member states, and the elimination of the concept of a 'super safe' country. that is why we are calling for a separate vote on a number of amendments. the concept of a 'super safe' country applies to european third countries, such as switzerland, which have particularly high standards of human rights and refugee protection. this concept, when implemented in germany, was a success, limiting abuses and circumscribing the number of asylum seekers. some argued that this solution was contrary to the geneva convention and did not respect the principle of non-refoulement. that is why we have consulted the legal service of the european parliament, which has just issued a report which confirms our position, maintaining that the safe countries solution is fully compatible with the international obligations to which we are bound. we also reintroduced an amendment which was not adopted by the commission and which seeks to ensure that there is an effective remedy whereby the applicant should always have the right to appeal against the decision taken and await the decision in the country where he has applied for asylum. i believe that by approving these amendments we will have a report that is up to our responsibilities, which the council should follow. if we continue with the amendments contained in the initial solution, i am afraid that the epp will not be able to give its consent to the report.

i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations, and that is why i am not going to vote for the report. that is why this first agreement on wine with the united states, after 20 years of bilateral negotiations, is important, but also worrisome, and it seems to have arisen more because of the ongoing negotiations in the world trade organisation than because of the defence of the interests of the european union's wine producers, given the enormous concessions it has made to the united states. we believe it is essential that the negotiations be extended to the international level, but it is also important that the commissioner should make it clear, as regards the united states, how she intends to safeguard the interests of wine-producing farmers in european regions, where this production is essential for economic development. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quality of wine is not compromised, and that consumers are protected. when we look at the details and hear their explanations, we are left with great difficulty and great concern about the guarantees that must be given to our farmers and the regions concerned.
mr president, wine production in europe is not simply the application of laboratory or marketing techniques. as has already been said here today, the cultivation of vines and the production of wine are distinctive cultural features of various european regions and are part of their multi-millennial history. to give just one example, which i am very fond of, as you will understand, port wine, i will mention that it is produced in the oldest demarcated region in the world, created and regulated long before the american colonies ever thought of becoming a sovereign state. in the north of portugal, on the steep slopes of the douro river, successive generations have carved the mountains with their hands over the centuries and worked the miracle of transforming the stones of a desolate landscape into a scene of extreme beauty, now classified as a world heritage site. what i have just said does not exclude my full awareness of the importance of concluding the agreement with the united states. i know how much european exports to this country weigh and i know the extremely difficult trading environment in which this problem has been dragging on for many years. but there can be no negotiating pragmatism that calls into question the establishment of minimum rules for the protection of our designations of origin and geographical indications. the commission cannot under any circumstances neglect the protection of semi-generic indications in the united states internal market. it cannot fail to fix a precise date for the signing of the final undertaking. it cannot fail to resume without delay the planned new phase of negotiations with a view to obtaining recognition of the 17 designations of origin listed in annex ii. i sincerely hope that the disappointing result of this first round of negotiations will be offset by the second round, which we all hope will be concluded quickly. a fair and balanced agreement with the united states could be a positive sign that european wine-growing, faced with various and complex challenges, urgently needs it.

importance it deserves. wine is one of the products which is now subject to increased international competition as a result of globalisation and the liberalisation of markets. it is therefore one of
