in writing. the report by mr florenz on the fees charged by the european medicines agency is an example of how we should take account of the experience and assessments of the work of the community agencies. the report follows a major change in the agency's powers, which have not only been modified but also broadened. it is therefore essential to provide this agency with a sound and up-to-date financial framework. the amendments proposed were aimed at clarifying the principle of setting fees charged by the agency and the application of reduced fees for traditional herbal medicines. the rapporteur's position therefore calls for the application of fees to take account of the workload involved in the evaluation of products. i therefore voted in favour of mr florenz's report on the fees charged by the european medicines agency.
in writing. the new eu-comoros fisheries protocol, which will be in force from 2005 to 2010, is the logical and foreseeable evolution of the previous agreement, with only a few changes compared to the previous one. the new protocol provides for a reduction in the total number of vessels, despite the fact that the total allowable catch is to be increased from 4670 tonnes to 6000 tonnes. as with other fisheries agreements with the indian ocean countries, the eu-comoros agreement is of great importance to the community tuna sector, which is able to meet the needs of the demanding community market. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i should like to point out that the new agreement nevertheless reduces the number of portuguese longliners licensed to fish in the agreement area. i cannot but disagree with the fact that the commission did not consult the portuguese sector in the course of the negotiations for the proposal.
in writing. the new protocol to the fisheries agreement with the comoros will apply from 2005 to 2010. this differs little from the previous protocol (2001 and 2004), which was extended for 10 months. the approval of this agreement thus guarantees fishing opportunities to the fleets of the member states operating in these waters, including portugal. from the eu perspective, it is estimated that each euro invested by the community in the agreement generated an added value of eur 5.07, which represents an impressive return on investment. the number of tuna-fishing vessels remains the same (21 spanish, 18 french and 1 italian vessels), while the number of surface longliners has been reduced from 25 to 17 (12 for spain and 5 for portugal), due to the level of utilisation of the last protocol, which shows that the long-distance fishing fleets are being reduced, as exemplified by the almost residual weight of the portuguese long-distance fishing fleet. this protocol increases the contribution of the shipowners by 40%, from 25 euros per tonne of tuna caught to 35 euros, reducing the community's share, which we do not think is acceptable. the commission has announced its intention to negotiate future protocols with other countries at the same rate for shipowners.
in writing. the new protocol on tuna fisheries concluded between the community and the comoros for the period from 1 january 2005 to 31 december 2010 raised some feasibility issues for community countries with fishing fleets. i have followed the process closely and have noticed that the negotiations did not include consultation of the sector. the commission took note of this criticism and reaffirmed the great importance of continuing and strengthening the dialogue with the fishing industry in the framework of the partnership agreements. the commission also expressed its intention to hold a meeting with the tuna sector in autumn 2005 to discuss all issues relevant to the sector. i would like to stress that the annual financial compensation has increased from eur 350 250 to eur 390 000 per year, and the most important fact is that 60% of it is allocated to measures to support the development of local fisheries. for these reasons i have no objection to the rapporteur's proposals.
in writing. we support the proposal to reject this initiative which, under the pretext of the 'fight against terrorism', is an attack on the fundamental freedoms, rights and guarantees of citizens. the proposal is intended to store indiscriminately data relating to communications (telephone, sms and e-mail) in a systematic way, and apparently without any control. as the rapporteur points out, this is an inappropriate and unnecessary proposal, which is contrary to the provisions of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. it is worth noting that this is not the first time that parliament has rejected such an initiative, but the british presidency and the european commission, despite being widely criticised, have this week again presented new initiatives in this area. the portuguese law provides for a security system which, in conjunction with the judiciary, already includes a whole balanced set of measures, rules and controls which, if used with care and rigor and provided with the necessary human resources, is certainly in a position to combat crime effectively, even in its most organized forms.
in writing. i am in favour of the spirit of the proposal put forward by the four member states, share the concerns expressed in the proposal and consider that there is no excess or disproportion in the proposal, but i voted in favour of the report, which proposed rejecting the proposal put forward by the four member states. i did so precisely because i thought that the substance of the proposal was correct, but since the commission is in a position to present a complete and comprehensive proposal on this subject shortly, this seems to me to be the most correct way of legislating on this matter. in the present times it is necessary not to confuse security with securitarianism. saving traffic and communication data is not even equivalent to phone tapping. it is simply a question of keeping the bare minimum necessary for an effective criminal investigation. and although this measure is not particularly effective in preventing crime - although this dimension is also present - its usefulness in criminal investigations is all too evident. so, in order to justify the confidence that has been placed in it, the commission is now expected to present in good time the necessary proposal to regulate this important matter.
in writing. this proposal for a directive is the first step in the harmonization of the asylum procedure in the various countries of the european union. as our group has pointed out, the ep report, when compared with the agreement reached in the council on this same proposal, covers up some of the most negative aspects of the report, such as the abolition of the concept of 'super safe country' - which the united nations high commissioner for refugees criticises - and the defence of the possibility of appeal against the refusal of an asylum application, as well as the right to remain in the country until the end of the procedure. however, the amendments tabled by our group and our vote in plenary - in addition to other substantive aspects - have also sought to help remove other negative aspects, of which the following stand out: - the rejection of a period of detention for asylum seekers, particularly in the so-called 'detention centres' for illegal immigrants; - the rejection of the concept of a 'safe third country', since the examination of an asylum application should be carried out taking into account the individual case, and the creation of an arbitrary list of countries should be rejected (by what criteria would it be defined?).
in writing. the illusion that legislating on this matter is simple ignores the evidence that different legal systems produce different, sometimes unforeseen or undesirable outcomes - see, for example, the question of the suspensive effect of an appeal against a decision not to grant refugee status. the same illusion also ignores the fact that there are different traditions in the definition of the concept of refugees themselves - for example, the difference in the concept in portugal and the united kingdom. the two aspects mentioned above are inseparable from the vote i have taken on this report. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the internal market. i am sorry that the good intentions which have certainly motivated the parliamentary left will - as so often happens - produce a bad result. the concern for the proper and humane reception of refugees is by no means incompatible with a set of rules which are at least as flexible as possible, so as to make the necessary adjustments to the different national laws. on the contrary, this is the correct sense of a justified concern for the refugee problem and a desire to find really effective solutions.
the commission has already taken a number of important steps in the process of establishing a special status for the outermost regions, in accordance with article 299 (2) of the treaties. this status is based on the very specific situation of these regions. in fact, the combination and permanence of factors such as isolation and distance, insularity and archipelagic nature, small size of the territory, mountainous geography and economic dependence on a single product or activity, create a reality that we call the outermost periphery and which is unique within the european union. it would be a serious breach of the principle of proportionality and equality if the outermost regions were to be given the same treatment as the other european regions. the integration model of these regions must take account of their very specific nature and must therefore be adapted, modelled and even derogated from in some cases. we must treat differently what is different, because the differences that the outermost regions exhibit have a very negative impact on their economic and social development, leaving them in an unacceptable competitive disadvantage and unable to take advantage of the dynamics unleashed by the internal market, recent enlargement, the lisbon strategy and globalisation itself. in fact, how can the outermost regions compete on an equal footing when the economic activities carried out there are burdened by very significant additional costs, such as those derived from transport, the absence of economies of scale and external economies, small and fragmented markets, the shortage of skilled labour, etc. it is therefore crucial to continue efforts to deepen the european union's special treatment of the very specific reality of the outermost regions. this is the main purpose of the european commission's communication 'a stronger partnership for the outermost regions', on which i was particularly grateful and encouraged to draw up the report we are now considering. the european commission proposes an overall strategy centred on three priorities: competitiveness, accessibility and regional integration. it proposes that the new cohesion policy and the other community policies should make a greater contribution to this strategy, and also proposes the creation of innovative instruments such as the specific programme for compensating for over-capacity and a 'grand voisinage' programme to promote the integration of the outermost regions into the neighbouring geographical area, combining transnational and cross-border cooperation with customs and trade policy measures. hence the strength of the european commission's proposal to counter and mitigate the main constraints resulting from the ultraperipheral condition. the main objective is to tackle the main one, namely to break the isolation of the outermost regions, to break the isolation by promoting the use of new information and communication technologies and facilitating access to the european continent in terms of transport, but also by promoting the integration of the outermost regions into the neighbouring area, which they have always turned their backs on. the second key idea is to promote the competitiveness of the outermost regions, not only by reducing the significant additional costs of being in the outermost regions, but also by taking decisive action on the dynamic factors of competitiveness, education, training, innovation, research, the information society and entrepreneurship. in this last respect, the european commission's proposal is clearly inadequate, and this is its major weakness. in fact, the contribution of community policies which could have a major impact on the competitiveness of the outermost regions falls far short of what is needed, such as policies to develop human capital, research and technological development, the environment, services of general economic interest and telecommunications. the european commission does not foresee a special solution for the outermost regions which leave objective 1, because they would have exceeded 75% of the community average in terms of gdp per capita. a special scheme for the phasing-out of objective 1 for objective 2 is fully justified in the light of article 299 (2) of the treaties. the european commission's proposal is, however, quite positive, because it comes at the right time, because it sets the strategy and priorities correctly, because it provides for innovative instruments. we welcome the european commission's initiative, but we urge it to be more ambitious and to take account of the suggestions and comments contained in my report. i should like to conclude without a word of thanks to the colleagues who, through their contributions, have made it possible to draw up a better report.

extra costs of disposing of certain fishery products.
for the gue/ngl group article 299 (2) of the treaty provides that, taking into account the social, economic and structural situation of the azores, madeira, the canary islands and the french overseas departments, specific measures should be adopted for these outermost regions. these regions are characterised by the existence of permanent structural disadvantages which differentiate them from the other regions of the countries of the european union. structural disadvantages aggravated by the remoteness, insularity, small area, difficult terrain and climate and economic dependence on a small number of products, all of which, if persisted and combined, seriously hamper their development. this is stated in the treaties, and therefore, in view of their development needs and the effective achievement of economic and social cohesion, a principle also enshrined in the treaties, it is necessary not only to guarantee the specific nature of the ultraperiphery in a transversal way in all community policies, but also to create a specific community programme of support for these regions, integrating all the dispersed measures and with the appropriate financial means in the financial framework 2007-2013, in order to make a significant contribution to solving their problems. many aspects could and should be addressed concerning the reality and needs of these regions and their populations. i would simply stress the need to ensure the sustainability of fisheries resources and the activity of fishing communities in these regions, for which it is essential that the exclusive competence to access their waters, in accordance with their national jurisdiction, be equivalent to their exclusive economic zone. the need to consider a framework of permanent support measures in the environmental area, taking into account that most of the territory of these regions is occupied by nature reserves and other protected areas, or, finally, support for measures in the area of training, traditional crafts and local production and tourism.
commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate my colleague and friend, mr sérgio marques, on his excellent report and his willingness to incorporate contributions from other members, and mr guellec on the quality of his report. as the pse shadow rapporteur on the committee on regional development, i tabled amendments, which were largely adopted, and i proposed to my group that we support the report and all the amendments tabled in its vote, first in committee and now in plenary. with different perspectives and approaches, we agree to support the strategy proposed by the commission for the sustainable development of the outermost regions of the european union as regards priorities, instruments and, in particular, the creation of a specific programme to compensate for over-cost, designed to compensate for the specific and permanent constraints of the outermost regions, such as their remoteness, insularity, small size, difficult terrain and climate, economic dependence on a small number of products and activities, small size of local markets, and the establishment of an action plan for the outermost regions. although we agree with the strategy, we have some criticisms or reservations concerning: first, the lack of action and of financial means for its implementation in the wake of the commission's statements and proposals; the second concerns the exclusive use of the gdp per capita criterion for the eligibility of these regions under the new convergence objective of the reformed cohesion policy. the third is the use of the population criterion in the allocation of the budgetary allocation for the specific programme for compensating for over-cost; and the fourth concerns the uncertainty about the greater neighbourhood action plan, as it is not clear how it should be framed in the future european territorial cooperation objective of the reformed cohesion policy and its 'new neighbourhood instrument'. for all these reasons, and in agreement with the rapporteur, i suggest, as a justified claim of the outermost regions, that the outermost regions should be given differential treatment in accordance with article 299 (2) in view of their specific conditions of access to the structural funds, and that priority financial support should be granted to them regardless of their income level. secondly, an increase in the budgetary allocation for the specific programme to be distributed equitably according to the constraints affecting them; thirdly, a clarification of the action plan for the wider neighbourhood in the context of the future objective of 'european territorial cooperation' and the new 'neighbourhood policy' of the union, with a view to a neighbourhood which covers not only the regions and neighbouring countries such as morocco, cape verde, brazil and others, but also the host countries of the large communities of migrants from the ors with whom they have traditional ties. i therefore suggest that this report be adopted, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as a further important step after the positive proposal from the commission, so that, by approving the financial perspective, the conditions for the sustainable development of the outermost regions can be created, and economic, social and territorial cohesion can be successfully promoted.

in writing. for a country, territorial cohesion means combating interregional economic and social disparities and agglomeration effects, i.e. promoting the harmonious and homogeneous development of its entire territory. in this context, territorial cohesion is an integral part of economic geography and is implicit in the objectives of any structural policy. their inclusion at community level, alongside the objective of economic and social cohesion, is only meaningful because for some the idea of a federal eu 'state' with a territory is underlying it. we therefore believe that the report should focus on regional disparities within each member state, which show a tendency to persist or increase, and on the need for new policies which, instead of promoting them, combat these disparities. this means promoting public services, developing the productive system, providing basic infrastructure (transport, communications, energy), establishing a wide network of small and medium-sized agricultural holdings and a strategy to support the development of small and medium-sized urban centres in inland, rural and peripheral regions. all this requires increased resources and a real cohesion policy. we therefore regret the rejection of our proposals.

the european commission was expected to do something new. it was hoped that concrete measures would be put forward, with adequate and urgent means, to give effect to the important proposals contained in the european parliament's resolution of 6 september. however, what we heard was more of the same. it was an attempt to justify the unjustifiable. let us remember: on 1 january, with the liberalisation of the textile and clothing sector, there was an exponential increase in imports into the european union. alert to the serious economic and social consequences, for example for portugal, that this would entail, and to the need for the rapid activation of the safeguard clauses provided for in trade agreements, the european commission, chaired by durão barroso, only regulated the application of these clauses on 6 april, but minimising the impact of their implementation. it was not until 17 may that it began consultations, and only on two categories of textile products, before presenting an agreement on 10 june which, in addition to abandoning the use of safeguard clauses, was a trap. once again, the absence of regulations for its implementation, which only came into force on 20 july, was used by the large european import and distribution multinationals to call into question the import limits agreed in june. in september the commission, echoing the interests of the large multinationals, quickly called into question what it had previously agreed itself, forcing millions of textiles and clothing articles into the country. the moral of the story is that the real beneficiaries of the liberalisation of the textile and clothing trade are the large importers and distributors who are increasing their profit margins to ever more exorbitant levels. the losers in european textile production are the workers and thousands of micro, small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. we support this resolution which is critical of the bilateral agreement on trade in wine signed on 14 september 2005 between the eu and the us, calling it 'insufficient' and 'inadequate'. the resolution reaffirms:- the defence of traditional production, family winemaking and the quality of our wines, the international recognition of the eu's protected traditional terms;- the establishment of a register of internationally recognised geographical indications and the inclusion of this objective among its main priorities in multilateral agricultural negotiations, including in the wto;- the recognition of the 17 appellations of origin included in annex ii, so that all european appellations of origin for wine are duly protected, as soon as possible, by the american authorities within their own market;- the need to strengthen community support measures to improve and promote the quality of community products in the context of the forthcoming reform of the common market organisation; it stressed that the agreement considerably weakens the eu's position in the wto negotiations on agriculture, as it calls into question the production zone-centred approach and the quality prevailing in much of the wine sector.
in writing. i would just like to stress that there was no point in the motion calling for urgent measures to support sectors which are being seriously harmed by the increase in fuel prices, but instead it stressed the 'importance of avoiding political intervention'. it should be recalled that, following the fishermen's statements on the consequences of the increase in fuel prices for the fisheries sector, the council of agriculture and fisheries ministers of 19 and 20 september, inexplicably, only once again 'took note' of the situation and did not decide on any measures to deal with the problem. as fishermen have warned, the increase in fuel prices is causing great difficulties for the sector, with the viability of many vessels at stake if immediate measures are not taken, such as financial support to minimise the increase in fuel costs. it should be noted that the increase in fuel prices is aggravating the already difficult situation of many small-scale fishermen who use petrol in their fishing activities, without any support to help mitigate the consequences of successive increases in this fuel. so, apart from other long-term measures, because they are urgent, immediate action is required.
in writing. in 1945, the world was emerging from the war and europe was in ruins. the un was founded on goodwill and hope, a sign of an effort to emancipate men, from a kind of tribal relationship of alienation and exclusion to a greater civilization that identifies us all with equal dignity and deals with difference through dialogue. the united nations, without a force that matched the size of its foundation, tried to sublimate the tensions of the cold war, in the forms of decolonization, in regional conflicts. an ever-permanent attempt to surpass itself, in its fabric of states, for peace. the european union too is rooted in the same moral design as the united nations: the values of peace, solidarity between peoples, democracy and the rule of law. the european union too is continuing to pursue its aims. in search of governance, of integrated coexistence, of transposing their humanitarian ideal to the world. in this crusade, reform of the european union is needed, reform of the un. multipolarity is achieved by deepening the political and legal dimension of the european union. i mean, the united nations needs a european constitution. it's the middle of great politics.
in writing. the resolution omits or implicitly supports the ambitions and efforts to transform the un into an instrument dominated by the big capitalist powers, led by the usa, whitewashing the aggressions and interferences of imperialism, if possible, concerted multilaterally. the eu has also been involved in the negotiations on the future of the european union, and has been involved in the negotiations on the future of the european union. the 'millennium development goals' are being recalled, but no progress is being made in achieving them, whether in reducing hunger, poverty, child mortality, or in ensuring access to water, health, education and the promotion of equality. there is no measure - blocked by the united states, with the complicity of its allies - for the disarmament and elimination of weapons of mass destruction. the resolution also stresses the federalist drift - defeated in the nos to the proposal for a new treaty for the eu - but which the resolution gives rise to when it refers to 'the prospect of obtaining a common european seat in the security council' and the 'merger' of the offices and delegations of the different countries in a 'common external delegation of the eu'.
in writing. the report seeks to take stock of the state of play of the policies and concrete actions developed by the different countries of the european union with regard to renewable energies. it considers that, although progress has begun, the policies and measures in place will not allow the previously set targets for the use of energy from renewable energy sources to be met. in this context, measures are proposed which - although with limits to real progress - seek to contribute to the reversal of the present situation. the main features are:- strengthening of qualified training and research and development in the subjects concerned;- greater autonomy for each member state as regards the objectives, options, sectors and technical solutions to be implemented;- greater decision-making autonomy and availability of means for local and regional authorities;- support for energy agencies at the various levels of intervention;- substantial strengthening of structural and cohesion funds and even of the cap (rural development) for this purpose; however, the report does not go into the fundamental question, namely the clear and explicit recognition of the reality of peak oil and the reduction in oil consumption and the need to exploit other sources of energy.
in writing. welcomes the timely report by mr claude turmes on the european commission's communication on the share of renewable energy in the european union, and agrees with the position on the extreme importance of renewable energy for the future of humanity, which highlights its environmental and health benefits. it also specifically agrees that the consolidation of the use of renewable energy as an alternative depends on a correct combination of political will and instruments applied at global levels, including the european union itself, national, regional and local levels.
in writing. road traffic has tripled in the last three decades, while the number of deaths has halved. however, road accidents remain the leading cause of death for people under 50. strong measures to promote road safety should therefore be taken. the report by mr vatanen, which i wholeheartedly support, welcomes the implementation of the third action programme on road safety, which aims to halve the number of deaths on european roads by 2010. the key role that the european road safety agency and an eu road safety framework (with performance indicators) could play in achieving the objectives of the 3rd road safety action programme is also highlighted. in the short term, therefore, drivers' behaviour must be improved through enforcement of legislation, enforcement campaigns, training and user education. in the long term, initiatives in the technological field (electronic security) and the increasing integration of electronic devices in 'smart vehicles' will contribute to achieving the objectives. finally, road infrastructure must be improved and adapted to current traffic levels.

education have now led to the text being voted for in the plenary with a strong vote in favour. another preliminary point: education policies are the exclusive responsibility of the member states. simple idea: equal educational rights are due to the number and the number of people living in our cities, regardless of their colour, sex, language, religious beliefs or legal status. the first consequence of this choice is recognised by the acquis communautaire itself. school systems must ensure that immigrants and their descendants learn not only the language of the country of destination stops. mr president, allow me to speak now about good practice. some members of this house have their children in the european schools which the union has set up to facilitate the integration of its officials. in these schools, language and content learning is integrated. one thinks and studies not only in the language of the country of destination but also in one's mother tongue. i think everyone is proud of the quality of this multilingual education. it prepares our children to face their future without fear. that's how it's right. but it needs to be added that what we want for our children cannot be the luxury of luxurious immigrants. it should be a horizon for european education systems. in the city of hamburg i was able to see how this system is successfully applied to public schools. nine primary schools have classes where german children mix with children of a second mother tongue. the teaching is carried out in both languages with two teachers per class. after five years, immigrant parents try to put their children in these classes anyway, even if they live on the other side of town. portuguese, italian, spanish, polish and turkish citizens are benefiting from this pilot project. it's worth it! this pedagogical project is not universally applicable and does not exhaust the map of multilingual educational proposals, but anticipates the future. and it is anticipation of the future that this report is talking about. the creation of a european network of schools to which projects for integrated language and content learning can be submitted is the third relevant proposal in this report. the truth is that bilateral agreements between states are subject to severe constraints of a budgetary nature and even of political will. the allocation of a budgetary appropriation in the lifelong learning programme specifically for the promotion of this network unlocks the will and gives new impetus to education policies based on multilingualism. it's the least we can do!
on behalf of the pse group. because of poverty 1,200 children die every hour. because of poverty, the world loses about 900,000 children every month. according to a 2005 un report, the number of children dying each month from poverty is equivalent to three times the number of victims of the tsunami that struck southwest asia in december 2004. every day, thousands and thousands of people die because of poverty, mostly children and women. despite the 2000 millennium development goals to reduce child mortality, the target will not be met by a difference of 4.4 million. yet, the world's 500 richest individuals have a combined income greater than that of the 416 million poorest people. the 2.5 billion people who live on less than two dollars a day, and represent 40 percent of the world's population, represent only five percent of the world's income. the millennium declaration contains the promise to halve poverty within 15 years. yet, the gap between rich and poor continues to widen. there is much to be done to lift so many women and children out of poverty. just one example: microfinance instruments, including microcredit, have proved effective in combating poverty, and it has been women who have made the most and best use of microcredit, succeeding in improving the economic situation of their families. women who are unemployed or on low incomes and therefore do not have access to conventional financial institutions. in europe too, according to eurostat data, 16% of the population were at risk of poverty in 2003. there are about 70 million poor citizens in europe at 25. we have therefore tabled a proposal on behalf of the socialist group to amend this report to introduce a guaranteed minimum income, similar to the one already in place in my country, portugal, as a means of effectively combating poverty, and especially poverty among women. poverty leads to trafficking in women and children, sexual slavery, violence, school dropouts, child labour, children at risk, fundamentalism and even terrorism. preventing poverty is about building a more just and secure society, also for the rich.
it is not enough to lament the dire poverty of many tens of millions of women in the 25 member states of the european union. it is not enough to say that the poverty, social exclusion and misery in which more than 72 million people in the european union live is a violation of human rights and has a female face. we need to demand a radical change in the economic and social policies that are aggravating unemployment, poverty and social exclusion and increasing inequalities in the distribution of income. a radical break with neoliberal policies and the guidelines of the european central bank is urgently needed. the stability pact must be replaced by a growth and employment pact and a genuine strategy for economic and social development must be promoted, by putting an end to the privatisation of public services and social security, by ensuring incomes that provide social welfare and access to public health systems that naturally include health care and all the care that women need. only then will it be possible to guarantee quality employment with rights, with wages that give dignity to those who work, and to guarantee the realization of all the human rights to which women are entitled.
in writing. the euro is one of the most widely used currencies in international transactions and as such is one of the most at risk of being counterfeited. the union has been taking the necessary measures to ensure that the circulation of the euro is protected by effective and uniform mechanisms against criminal counterfeiting activities. although counterfeiting rates remain high, the anti-counterfeiting measures are having a very significant effect, with the total number of operations in which counterfeit euro banknotes were seized increasing by 20% between 2003 and 2004, while counterfeiting of banknotes, e.g. 100 euro banknotes, was reduced by 38%. it is therefore clear that the surveillance, training and technical assistance measures which are indispensable for the adequate, uniform and effective protection of the euro against counterfeiting must be continued. i therefore support the proposal to extend this programme, as well as all the excellent amendments proposed by the rapporteur, because only a stable financial framework will make it possible to pursue the objectives set out in the programme, especially in view of the needs resulting from the integration of the new member states into monetary union.
in writing. relations between the european union and switzerland are, of course, governed by special rules. in all likelihood, switzerland would very easily become a member of the european union, since it fulfils all the criteria for membership. it turns out that this has not been the will of the swiss. it also happens that for geographical reasons switzerland is effectively at the centre of europe and the european union. there are therefore all the advantages of concluding agreements with our neighbour such as the ones in question, which make the relationship between the 25 member states and switzerland simpler and more fluid, in that they make life easier for the citizens of both sides. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. the fisheries issue is fundamental to my country and even though i am not directly involved in this case, i have followed this report closely, as i consider the protection of species and the preservation of this important sector of activity for several countries in the union to be of the utmost importance. i welcome the participation of the new member states of the baltic sea in the amendments to this legislation. the added information is crucial. consultation with representatives of the fisheries and processing sectors is also essential to anticipate possible shortcomings in the provisions on conservation of resources. the baltic sea is a sea with very particular characteristics. this report has sought to combine with care and attention not only the question of the preservation of ecosystems but also the social question linked to this activity. it is also worth noting the importance of this proposal for the development of fisheries in the baltic - in particular with regard to the maintenance of fish stocks - which lacks a full knowledge of the situation and its problems for a final decision. for these reasons i voted in favour of mr chimielewski's report.
in writing. although the european parliament's report is better than the european commission's text, the truth is that it is based on some conceptions, which we consider negative, about the development of higher education. one example is the creation of networks of national and european evaluation and accreditation agencies - public and private - whose evaluations and their results may have consequences for the licensing, funding, student support and 'reputation' of institutions, although this is not explicitly stated. the opening up of valuation to private individuals indicated the creation of a new business, opening the door to greater influence of capital on the institutions, their programmes, objectives and social strategy. a web of interests could be created between agencies, states, institutions and economic powers in each country, with the aim of ensuring evaluation criteria that favour the best possible evaluation of their institutions and harm poorly ranked institutions and education systems. they can thus favour the predominance of economic criteria, enhancing certain 'qualities' and helping to create even more difficulties for those who already have them - in addition to disregarding the national and public dimension of higher education - accentuating the trend towards the elitisation and commodification of higher education in europe.

in writing. the quality of higher education in europe is a key factor in our strategies for growth and development worldwide. the much-desired mutual recognition of university qualifications and degrees in europe requires optimal conditions to ensure the quality and continuous improvement of university establishments. this is why this proposal is so interesting, because it adopts concrete measures for a more efficient, more transparent and more attractive european higher education system for students and scientists. i therefore voted in favour of mrs novak's report.
in writing. much could be written about the relations, particularly trade, between the various countries in the european union and china, a country with a population of about 1.3 billion. despite the balanced aspects of the report - for example, the establishment of 'trade relations in a spirit of cooperation and complementarity, while ensuring that both sides can preserve and develop their industries, agriculture and respective services in harmony, in order to ensure the best possible living conditions for all their people' - the report is characterized by the apology of capitalism, capitalist competition and the liberalization of trade relations, particularly in the context of the wto. hence the demands for 'opening up markets', in particular the liberalisation of 'financial markets', the reform of the 'economic system' and the 'embrace' of the 'market economy' - i.e. the implementation of capitalism - the 'acceptance of the legal and economic system' of the european union by china. hence the acceptance of all the european union's cheating - with the agreement of the ps government - in the textile and clothing sector, to the taste of the interests of the big importers and distributors. which is unacceptable.
in writing. the trade relations between china and the european union are a reality that must first of all be faced head on. the idea that the flow of goods from china can be reduced is an illusion. it is just as illusory to think that we can compete with this huge producer on the basis of a similar economic model based on low wages or unskilled labour. without abandoning our industries, without giving up production, without abandoning our citizens, we must act with a clear view of the future development of this trade relationship and its consequences for the european economy. and we must also seek to achieve a fundamental objective by increasing trade: the democratization of china, where respect for human rights is anything but commendable and where foreign policy is designed in obedience to a logic of expansionism of its influence, ignoring the objectives - ours and those of our allies - of the expansion of democracy and respect for human rights. let us therefore make trade a platform for development. that must be our challenge.
in writing. i would like to leave two recommendations to the european commission. first, the home front. globalisation is a new reality, the effects of which cannot be contained by protectionist measures. globalization has its positive aspects, but there is one side to it that we should not ignore. we must act swiftly and vigorously in the sectors and regions most affected at social level. i recommend that the commission prepare specific programmes for these regions. now the outside front. since joining the wto, china has never played by the rules. the goc continues to pursue export aid policies; they artificially devalue the currency; they violate environmental standards; they do not respect workers' rights; fail to ensure that health and safety standards are in place; they use child labor and forced labor. in textiles, they have repeatedly and flagrantly violated the commitments they have accepted with the eu's approval. i therefore recommend that the european commission press for the introduction of minimum social and environmental standards in trade agreements with the respective system for verifying their application. globalization has its winners and losers. defeat is bitter, but to lose because the opponent has not respected the most elementary rules of the game is revolting and unacceptable.
in writing. the internal situation in iran has been a matter of sincere concern for many years. whether at purely domestic level, whether at regional level, whether even at the global level, iran and its policy of disregard for human rights, disregard for the values of freedom and democracy and, most basic of all, its disregard for human life, has been a strong factor of instability of enormous gravity. against this background, iran's nuclear activities are a further cause for concern. the european union has recently pursued an active diplomatic policy and has openly cooperated with the iranian authorities in the hope of achieving results. you can hardly say that you have succeeded. the resolution adopted today is another effort in the same direction, but it is beginning to raise the question whether this is the only way forward, whether it is not necessary to extend the international alliance in such a way that, by means of diplomacy, iran is forced to comply with its international obligations and to respect minimum standards at national level. we will keep our eyes open.
in writing. in its relations with the various countries of the international community, and particularly with the african countries, europe must accept once and for all that without democratization - and all that goes with it - all efforts at cooperation and aid are at least unproductive and may even be counterproductive. in the case of ethiopia, where the legitimate expectations of a people who have suffered for decades have recently been betrayed, it is our duty to do everything possible to make the road to democracy a reality. africa cannot be a territory where lawless governments are accepted as if nothing could be done to prevent it. in this sense, the message that this resolution sends to ethiopia must be clearly understood. finally, let us act first and foremost in the name of our principles and in the name of the people. but let us be clear, let us do it also in the name of our own interest. africa cannot be a continent from which its disenfranchised understandably want to flee.
in writing. i voted in favour of the bono report on education as a cornerstone of the lisbon process because, ' (1) in order to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy, in order to establish a knowledge society, the member states must make a clear commitment to lifelong learning and training, thus contributing to job creation in europe. 2.this report stresses the need to place greater emphasis on education in european policies, promoting de-bureaucratization and mobility through mutual recognition of qualifications and universal and non-discriminatory access to european educational institutions.
in writing. this report confirms a number of the criticisms we have made, namely:- the failure of the european project to converge towards higher standards in education as well as the education system itself in several countries;- the crisis of the current productive activity of the current economic and social fabric which is reflected in employment and is reflected in unreasonable pressures on performance in the education system. the commission is proposing some positive measures, in particular 'to ensure a 15% increase in the number of graduates in scientific sectors by 2010', which should be taken into account in portugal. it also stresses the need for member states to 'increase the number of teachers and to create quality initial and continuing teacher training', which is positive. it also points to the financial bottleneck felt in most countries, which is important, especially in view of the situation in portugal. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. however, it advocates the neoliberal approach envisaged in the lisbon strategy, with all the negative consequences already known, particularly in education and vocational training. that is why we abstained.
in writing. what will make us more competitive, more efficient, more productive will be our special ability to research, to innovate, to create. what will bring europe back to economic growth and development is, as is widely recognised, the commitment to the development of human resources. in this sense, investment in training is the most productive investment, even if only in the medium/long term. it is becoming increasingly late to believe, realistically, that the objectives of the lisbon agenda will be achieved in time. it is not just time that is running against us, it is above all we who have been running against reality, and if we insist on doing so, the result risks being serious. correcting this process requires measures with short-term, but also medium- and long-term objectives. as i said, investing in training is a medium- to long-term measure with enormous potential for effectiveness. we must therefore focus on the qualification of our human resources, because that is our model of development.
in writing. an integration policy is more than a policy of tolerance. integration is active and inclusive, provides communication, values difference and is part of the a priori of equality in dignity. tolerance is merely the recognition and acceptance of the other as a stranger. kant already rejected this idea of tolerance which, truly, does not allow the point of view of conceiving ourselves in the place of the other, which is the point of view of justice. europe, perceived as a "virtuous attraction", is this homeland of values, this intersection of an identity based on cosmopolitan law and national identities with strong traditions that recognise it. plurality is its defining element, not its potential for dissolution. that is why europe provides the ideal political framework for cultural diversity. immigration must have a human response to its causes. but let us now consider this subject of language. language teaching is the most basic prerequisite for human communication, for a civic majority, for awareness and the exercise of rights. without such communication, europe will fall short of its civilizational project, that is, it will be nothing more than a system of open doors into which one never really enters.
in writing. in immigration matters the key word is integration. the willingness, the mutual, the integration, the capacity, the mutual, the integration. the rapporteur is talking about something of the greatest interest, but it is worth setting priorities. i understand and share the concerns of the rapporteur, but i cannot help but focus my attention on this idea of integration capacity, which presupposes strict rules on entry and stay controls, for two reasons: firstly, because the existence of bounties for breaking the law is above all an incentive to illegal immigration and the networks that benefit from it; secondly, because illegal immigration is itself an unsustainable challenge to our capacity for integration. that said, in the field of education, the active integration of immigrants and their children is the most urgent concern. the arrival of new and different cultures is a positive factor, but this cannot mean that we no longer want those who arrive to integrate first and foremost, and to integrate means to accept the culture of the host country. obviously, school is an excellent place to do so. and, as is also obvious, the more bi-univocal that movement is, the better. but we still don't know where he should start.
in writing. i voted in favour of the pack report on the new challenges facing the circus as an integral part of european culture because: the commission should therefore contribute to the recognition of this activity as part of european culture by drawing up rules to ensure that it is preserved.
in writing. the circus, with all the imagination associated with it, deserves my utmost respect and i would even say, if the term is allowed, even affection. in addition, some of the questions raised by our colleague, the rapporteur, particularly those relating to employment, are certainly relevant. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question.
in writing. the urban dimension should be present in a regional development policy. the existence of small and medium-sized towns in inland, peripheral and rural regions is a factor in the development of these regions and helps to combat interregional disparities and the agglomeration effects of large urban centres within each country. as cities are the enablers of development, they too, because of the economic, social and spatial planning policies currently being pursued, concentrate complex problems ranging from congestion to housing needs, from pollution to social exclusion. a policy of urban renewal and rehabilitation is therefore essential. in this field, cohesion policy could contribute with a community initiative, such as the 'urban' concept, with adequate financial means. for example, it is possible to evaluate possible additional community support for the construction of social housing. unfortunately, that is not the case. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs is a good one. despite this consideration and our rejection of the 'role of cities' or the so-called 'urban dimension' being placed at the service of the neoliberal lisbon agenda, we support the report in general terms.
in writing. the question of cities is not a matter for the union. however, like so many other issues, tourism, for example, has been directly or indirectly affected by multiple community policy interventions. in particular, the urban question is treated with caution in regional policy, in the framework of the structural and cohesion funds. i believe that the union's action must be complementary, helping to ensure that the actions of the member states can be fully developed for the benefit of the people. we must therefore invest in programmes which have contributed to a balanced relationship between the different levels of decision-making. given that the gap between rural and urban areas is very wide in the 10 new member states, it is essential that the urban networks of the 10 new member states be integrated into the urban system of the entire community territory, in particular by improving the transport networks of cities with their regions and between cities themselves, for the development and progress of the european union itself. i therefore voted in favour of mr beaupuy's report.
in writing. we voted in favour of the report because it incorporated some of our proposals and because the text presented was improved in the vote in plenary. i would like to stress the following from our approved proposals: defence of access to high quality jobs, and in particular to fair and reasonable pay, which is a way of preventing and combating poverty; the committee also notes that parttime work and low-quality employment, which mainly affect women, contribute to increasing the number of women among the working poor, and points out that this is a source of social exclusion. on the other hand, some of its most negative aspects have been excluded, so that the final resolution, even if partial, does not deal in depth with the causes of poverty or the basic measures needed to combat it, but draws attention to serious social problems which particularly affect women.
in writing. the problem of combating poverty and social exclusion in the european union is a subject which has been the subject of much discussion and which is included not only in the millennium development goals but also in the objectives inherent in european ideals. this report is the first in the new europe to focus more specifically on women's poverty. why women? the truth is that we are confronted with impressive data of greater vulnerability in female populations to extreme poverty and various types of exclusion. for these reasons, this parliament has considered it important to look at this phenomenon and to propose the development of indicators and a methodology which can help to combat this problem effectively, not only through partnerships with the poorest women, but above all through measures to ensure that our societies contribute to the reconciliation of family life and working life in disadvantaged environments. we can thus help to combat poverty, which we must now regard as a violation of human rights and a reality that must be abolished immediately. i therefore voted in favour of mrs zaborska's report.

the next item is the report by mr vasco graça moura, on behalf of the committee on culture and education, on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision establishing the 'culture 2007' programme (2007-2013) (com (2004) 0469 - c6-0094/2004 - 2004/0150 (cod)) (a6-0269/2005).
the rapporteur. we recognize ourselves as europeans, despite all our differences, thanks to european culture. it represents a common and dynamic heritage in which identity and linguistic diversity are linked by a complex matrix in which the greek-latin, the judeo-christian and the mediterranean-muslim traditions are combined, without, however, these three vectors exhausting the picture of the elements that make it up. in order to promote the construction of europe, special attention must be paid to culture, the restoration of the common heritage and the promotion of diversity in order to strike a balance between centrifugal and centrifugal forces. this is by giving full weight to the common heritage and allowing the union's more than 400 million citizens to get to know each other better in their specific cultural and linguistic identities. it would be manifestly wrong to talk about cultural integration in europe. one of the most fascinating aspects of our civilization is precisely that europe must assume itself as a common unity and a unity realized in and by the diversity of its openings to man and the world. culture 2007-13 must first and foremost be the framework programme not for integration but for intensive cultural communication between the citizens of europe and at the level of europe and its values. all this means that european cultural policies must be pursued with a systematic view of european added value, otherwise they will lose all meaning and end up being indistinguishable from national cultural policies. but it also means that cooperation between the european institutions, the member states, the cultural agents and cooperators of each of them and their transnational networks is essential in the pursuit of common cultural policies. the culture programme 2007-2013 is a third generation programme. it takes account of the experience of previous ones and seeks more appropriate solutions in the face of that experience. i should like to say that i personally would have preferred a form corresponding to that of the first generation - raphael, ariane and kaleidoscope - which was clearly defined in its areas of art, literature, the performing arts and cultural heritage. resources are scarce, the number of applications for grant support is increasing and policies, to be truly effective, should be focused on a few very clear and very well defined objectives, even at the expense of other possibilities. but hopefully the new device will work and bring a more rigorous and positive contribution to this area. we are trying to improve the commission's proposal and make some corrections to it, to make it more appropriate to the purpose in view, to enshrine more clearly the dimension and importance of the common cultural heritage, without prejudice to contemporary creation. with all due respect to commissioner figel, i must say that it is not in the european commission's interest to refuse to make an explicit reference to an aspect which has to do with cultural heritage, the gigantic living heritage, both tangible and intangible, which has accumulated over the centuries and which has contributed so much to defining us as europeans. this is not a purely sectoral issue. we are talking about a matrix, a dimension common to all sectors, and that is fundamental. we also believe that provisions for the preservation of european memory sites linked to the sinister memory of totalitarian violence, both nazi and stalinist, would be better placed in the 'education for citizenship' programme. both this understanding and the acceptance of it by the european commission were formally expressed in the minutes of the parliamentary committee. finally, mr president, i should like to mention a very worrying point: the budget. the figures in the böge report are merely indicative. they were still taken into account. whereas in that report the figure for this programme was eur 566 million, we have put it at eur 600 million, because the böge report itself provided for a reserve to enable this to be done. this is a very modest sum! all the european leaders, those of the european commission including its president and commissioner for culture, those of parliament including the chairmen of the parliamentary groups and a great many colleagues, and those of the council including practically all the ministers for culture, have long been in favour of the need to increase the budget substantially in this area. the union has grown from 15 to 25 member states. european unity implies more and more intensive action in the field of culture. the lisbon strategy itself will be a dead letter if european cultural policies are left to languish without achieving their objectives, which are linked both to the common cultural heritage and to cultural and linguistic diversity in the member states. there can be no lisbon strategy if we do not know each other better. without knowing each other better, in the variety of our historical, cultural and linguistic identities, we cannot really cooperate with each other in a common design. this can only be achieved by cultural policies which aim at european added value and are equipped with the necessary means to achieve this. i therefore propose that we vote on the report which i have had the honour to endorse and which also contains a whole series of useful contributions from my colleagues from the various political quarters in the parliamentary committee on culture.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, for the commission and the council, culture is a problem of visibility for the european union. this has been and remains the real aim of the culture programme. the first merit of the graça moura report is that it departs from this view which exploits cultural creation for political purposes. but this is not the only merit, because the commission and the council want maximum visibility with minimum resources, so they concentrate support on a few actions, bodies and initiatives. it's a bad call. in the name of visibility, europe has been missing from so many projects that need it. secondly, this is what the report also proposes to correct in its own way. it promotes projects for up to two years, simplifies procedures for financial support, focuses on the transparency of calls for proposals and introduces the promotion of heritage and linguistic diversity into the programme's objectives. that's more than enough reason to vote for it. the financial perspective is still blocked by the british presidency. the priorities of tony blair, as we know, are different, but i think everyone here agrees on one point: the proposed €600 million for this programme is the bare minimum if the union is to present itself to creators and producers of culture as an institution which still puts some value on the words it speaks. i hope that the members of the committee on culture will be able to assess the final proposal in the light of this value and that the council will understand the message.
, in writing. since july this year azerbaijan has started air flights between its capital and the turkish-occupied northern part of cyprus. as the cypriot members of this parliament, and in particular our group, have pointed out, these flights are being carried out in violation of the principles of civil aviation and international law. it should be noted that this is not the only example of an attempt to impose in practice recognition of the turkish military occupation of part of cyprus and the so-called 'turkish republic of northern cyprus', which is not recognised by the united nations. the european parliament itself recently decided to set up a 'contact group for relations with the northern part of cyprus', an initiative which our group has criticised. the european union has also taken steps to ensure that the cyprus problem is not simply a question of the political situation in the country, but also of the political situation in the region. that is why we are voting against this report.

in writing. it is important that the rapporteur acknowledges, as can be seen in the pisa 2003 report, that there are still huge disparities in the performance of education systems in the different member states, despite all the community initiatives which claimed to be making progress towards greater equality. we also agree that full attention should be paid to promoting language teaching and learning and cultural diversity in education and training. but we still have a number of criticisms of the content of the european commission's proposal which the report, while seeking to mitigate, does not respond effectively, by maintaining some underlying orientation of the neoliberal policies which are increasingly having an impact on education and training. starting from an integrated programme for the period 2007-13, which is subdivided into six distinct sub-programmes (comenius, erasmus, leonardo da vinci, grundtvig, transversal and jean monnet), the overall amount proposed is low in view of the scope and diversity of situations covered. hence, even small increases in grants remain insufficient to ensure participation by young people and other people of low economic means.

in writing. the importance of education and training in creating a competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in europe is widely recognised. the report by mrs pack focuses mainly on the necessary simplification measures in the context of the community's education and vocational training programmes. community action in this area has contributed to the definition of quality indicators in education and encouraged the dissemination of good practice. the existing community instruments are of course complementary to the action of the member states and in this context the commission proposal aims to rationalise the existing instruments. we are faced with a well-conceived proposal which rationalizes the community's instruments, increases their coherence and synergies and makes them more effective. the commission is therefore proposing more ambitious targets, requiring a substantial increase in funds. i voted in favour of this report, believing that these programmes also contribute to the improvement of education and training systems throughout the eu.
in writing. this report significantly improves the youth in action programme for the period 2007-13 and seeks to take account of some of the criticisms made of the previous youth programme in the context of its mid-term review and the consultation process, in particular as regards the structure, which is now more flexible and with less red tape in the submission of requests for financial resources. however, the financial framework proposed by the european commission is very limited, so we supported the report's proposal to increase the available budget substantially, just as we considered it positive that it had been made clear that the promotion of the fundamental values we want to promote among young people are, in particular, respect for human dignity, equality, respect for human rights, tolerance and non-discrimination. we also welcome the amendments which seek to give greater attention to the following aspects: equality between women and men and the fight against discrimination; the fight against all forms of exclusion and discrimination, including on grounds of sex, race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation, in accordance with the provisions of article 13 of the treaty. that is why we are voting in favour of the report, despite some of the shortcomings in the programme.
in writing. i give my full support to this report on the community programme 'youth in action'. the rapporteur generally agrees with the european commission's proposal, but suggests some amendments, in particular the insufficient financial framework for the implementation of the 'youth in action' programme in the period in question; support for interactive and innovative seminars for young people; the regular organisation of the european youth week; and the aim of ensuring equal participation of disadvantaged young people in the programme, avoiding discrimination. it is recalled that the 'youth in action' programme will succeed the current 'youth' programme and will be more simplified. the formulation of the proposal was preceded by a broad consultation process, as provided for in the white paper on youth policy, and reflects to some extent the initiative of the heads of state or government to create a 'european pact for youth'. the 'youth in action' programme, which covers five actions with a total budget of €915 million, will come into force in january 2007 and will be managed in a decentralised manner, with centralised projects managed by an executive agency.

member of the commission. the commission believes that the degree of concentration in the energy market of many member states is considerable. at the same time, energy markets have seen some new entrants in many member states, either in the form of start-ups or through companies established in other member states setting up subsidiaries. therefore, consumer choice has increased in many parts of the community. a high degree of concentration may negatively affect the level of competition in these markets. the price level of energy may be one indicator for this; however, it has to be borne in mind that the price of energy is also influenced by many other factors: oil, gas and coal import prices, prices of co2 emission allowances on the carbon market, additional expenditure for the support of renewable energies, and increasing internationalisation of the external cost of energy. that is why the commission is monitoring the competitive dynamics of the markets at issue very carefully and why it recently launched an inquiry concerning the european energy sector. we await the findings of this inquiry. as far as energy mergers are concerned, their possible impact on the level of competition has to be evaluated on the merits of each case. the commission is strongly committed to carrying out this assessment with great attention in order to protect european consumers against the risk of reduced competition and unjustified price increases. the commission would like to draw the attention of the honourable member to the fact that it is currently carrying out phase ii in-depth investigations into the e.on/mol merger in hungary and the dong/e2 merger in denmark.
i am grateful to you, commissioner, especially for the principles you have reaffirmed, which are fundamental principles. the legal assessment that the european commission is carrying out on the gas natural/endesa merger could show (which i do not believe) that this merger does not have a community dimension and that, as a consequence, it should be assessed by a national competition authority, which is not independent of the respective government. in this context, and in the light of its decision of 9 december to prohibit the edp/eni/gdp merger, i ask the commission how it can prevent a merger with significant cross-border impact and competitive implications at a time when an integrated iberian energy market and a more perfect internal market in the energy sector in europe are desired.
mr president, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, the free movement of persons, goods, services and capital does not benefit the justice system, since the powers of intervention are restricted to the territory under the jurisdiction of each member state. we also know that several member states recognise the existence of a lack of trust between different police forces by refusing to share information. we cannot be surprised that this lack of confidence is even more felt at union level. it is therefore urgent to establish the widest possible cooperation on the basis of common procedures and minimum harmonisation of legal rules. only in this way can we combat transnational crime more effectively and prevent criminal networks from taking advantage of the differences and gaps in the laws of the member states. the lack of a common judicial area has led to the emergence of several community initiatives to approximate legislation, strengthen police and judicial cooperation, set up joint investigation teams, create a european arrest warrant and through the exchange of information and mutual assistance. this proposal for a framework decision is an important step in strengthening cooperation between member states, in seeking to find a common approach, in particular through a minimum framework of harmonisation, in particular as regards the definition of criminal organisation, offences and criminal frameworks and the establishment of common principles for determining jurisdiction. i would like to congratulate mr newton dunn on his work in the commission and the european union is the most important source of immigration for the people of europe. the right of men and women to seek a better life in a country other than their own is unquestionable. just as they have legitimate expectations of entering a new country safely, legally and with full respect for their fundamental rights. for this to happen, europe must have the capacity to receive, the conditions for acceptance, employability and integration, and be able to conduct a policy of development cooperation which reduces the disparities in wealth between the countries of origin and those of destination. and for this common european policy on migration to be clear, coherent and able to manage migratory flows effectively, it is necessary, firstly, to open up new legal routes of entry into the european union, taking into account the real possibilities of each member state and taking into account the lisbon strategy and the european employment strategy;
