the european parliament's proposal, while improving the council's in terms of the volume of payments, fails to respond to the economic, social and environmental needs and challenges of an enlarged european union. it is worth noting that this proposal falls short of the target of 1.08% of gni in the 2006 financial framework. given that the final commitment will be between 1.04% and 1.01%, we hope that the european parliament is not calling into question the already insufficient proposal it had put forward for the financial perspective for 2007-13. despite our criticism of the substance, we call for the amendments we support to be adopted, namely the creation of a pilot project for actions in the textile and clothing sector, with a view to the future establishment of a community programme for the sector, as proposed by the european parliament, the creation of plans for the recovery of fishery resources, taking into account the socioeconomic consequences of the periods of protection, and the defence of multilingualism, particularly in the eu-acp parliamentary assemblies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the avril doyle recommendation for second reading on 'emissions from air-conditioning systems in motor vehicles' because: (1) it translates the commitment made in the kyoto protocol to reduce greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere; (2) environmentally friendly technologies are needed to avoid climate change and, consequently, to prevent the increasing frequency of natural disasters.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. these measures are certainly not enough, but they are a contribution, in particular the new directive and regulation which are now being negotiated. the old models will be phased out and member states will be able to encourage the installation of air conditioning systems containing an efficient gas with a low global warming potential, such as co2, as advocated in one of the proposals adopted in the european parliament and which we supported. we hope that the commission and the council will accept it.
in writing. the report by mr florenz will enable the commission proposal on noise emissions into the environment from equipment for use outdoors to be adopted as soon as possible. it was found that the technical knowledge available five years ago and the progress made in the meantime have brought new data which will allow a further modification of the limit values. it is essential to take into account the consequences that a delay in the amendment of the legislation may have on the internal market for such equipment. we cannot therefore allow equipment to be withdrawn from the european market. therefore, the limit values for the phase starting on 3 january 2006 for these equipment should be of a purely indicative nature. the publication of the directive in the official journal before the end of the year will give the manufacturers concerned legal certainty as regards their products. i have voted in favour of the florenz report.
in writing. the report deals with community co-financing of transport and energy network projects, and is in line with the objectives of the so-called 'lisbon strategy', namely: the completion of the internal market - giving priority to its enlargement to the east, to the new member states - encouraging privatisation and competition in both the transport and energy sectors. for example, the report advocates encouraging so-called public-private partnerships - a tool that has served to hand over control of numerous public services to private capital - 'through legal guarantees compatible with competition law and the internal market', i.e. the primacy of capitalist competition at the level of the european union, and the secondary status of so-called 'economic and social cohesion'. the proposal in the report to increase the level of community co-financing for these projects is welcome, but it does not raise the need to increase the overall financial package for this purpose, which is contradictory, since it will reduce the number of projects that can be financed.
in writing. i congratulate mr mario mauro on his important and timely report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down general rules for the granting of community financial aid in the field of the transeuropean transport and energy networks and amending council regulation (ec) no 2236/95, which i support, particularly as regards the introduction of provisions to promote the investments needed to meet the lisbon objectives. europe needs to invest in transport and energy infrastructure. however, the 2007-2013 financial perspectives will need to be taken into account in setting the maximum funding rates for this proposal.
in writing. the transeuropean networks are a very important instrument in the creation and development of the transport, telecommunications and energy infrastructure sectors in europe. the european commission's proposal aims to review the general rules for the granting of community financial support in the field of the trans-european transport and energy networks for the period 2007-13. i believe that, in view of the list of 30 priority projects in the field of transport, we must clearly lay down the rules for granting financial support so that these projects can be developed in a manner consistent with the other community policies, with criteria of effectiveness and rules of transparency in the field of project financing. finally, it is clear to everyone that this report contains some measures to implement the provisions for promoting the investments needed to meet the lisbon objectives. i therefore voted in favour of mr mauro's report.
in writing. we consider it a priority to combat organized crime, its numerous networks and trafficking, money laundering and tax havens. however, we follow the concerns expressed by members of our group who criticise aspects of this report, including: - the extension of the definition of criminal organisation, in the context of the fight against organised crime, to associations of persons not seeking material or financial benefits, going beyond what is defined in the united nations convention on transnational organised crime, which considers organisations which have as their objective material or financial gain - thus excluding political or social motives - as organised crime; - i know . the possibility of incriminating persons is broadened in a way that may create ambiguity, i.e. persons who are not actually involved in criminal acts may be incriminated; - i know . the report also stresses the need to ensure that the european union is able to take action to combat organised crime, and calls for the creation of a european union police force. we also note and regret the rejection of our group's amendments, in particular the one which sought to ensure parliamentary control of europol's activities.
in writing. international organized crime is assuming high proportions and is growing. what is the measure of this growth? what are the actual figures? no one has a clear picture of the true extent of organized crime. this is absolutely unsustainable in this day and age. how can we, as responsible politicians, tolerate this situation? no, i'm not going. it is more than necessary to strengthen the fight against international crime on european soil. it is essential for the near future of our societies. the new text proposed seeks to make the fight against organised crime more effective. we are dealing with a more precise text, and it should be noted that it defines more clearly the relations between europol and interpol. i voted in favour of mr dunn's report, in the hope that these measures will contribute to a ruthless fight against organised crime.
in writing. the resolution we have just adopted is a positive element in the fight against this disease, especially because it focuses on prevention, as we have been advocating, since that is how a possible pandemic can be avoided. as the text says, the emphasis on information is essential to avoid alarmism by acting rationally and in concert with national and international authorities. hence our proposals for the european commission to provide financial support for a system of disease surveillance/monitoring, laboratory diagnostics, research into the appropriate vaccine, the burden of vaccination in the member states, and financial and technical support to third countries, particularly in asia, to ensure prevention and screening at source. however, in view of the possible emergence of an outbreak of the disease and the loss of income for poultry farmers during the period of launching a new farm, it is essential that there should also be community support, as we advocate. if this happens, it will also affect, directly and indirectly, a significant number of farmers and other workers involved in poultry farming and will have a strong economic and social impact in the member states. it is therefore important, beyond the human health problems, to take into account that the high costs may be unaffordable for some countries, both in the european union and at the origin of the disease - south-west asia.
in writing. it is true that biotechnology is one of the most important technologies for the future and must be supported by an appropriate policy framework, taking into account ethical, environmental and health aspects. one of the most important problems in this area is that of patents. we believe that human life, including human dna, should not be patented under any circumstances. that is why we voted against all the proposals which opened the way to the patentability of genes, of life, and we regret that in the final resolution there is some confusion which may indicate that opening, even if it was to avoid another more serious proposal. our position is clearly opposed to patents which include life and knowledge which we consider to be a universal good. another area of discussion concerns ethical principles, and it is true that stem cell research should not be prevented, even though we are against human cloning as stated in the resolution. our abstention at the end of the resolution is due to the contradictory aspects of the resolution, taking into account our positions of principle.
in writing. the report contains points which we value, in particular when it calls for the full implementation of the provisions of the 'international convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families', adopted by the united nations general assembly in 1990, and for its ratification by all member states. or when it denounces the fact that the current policies of the european union have concentrated on the repressive aspect, among other aspects which we consider to be positive. however, the report contains contradictory points and is part of a migration policy which is aimed above all at exploiting the human resources of third countries, particularly their most highly qualified workers. insisting on the inclusion of clauses on migration flows and compulsory readmission - expulsion - in cases of illegal immigration. we also regret the rejection of our group's proposals, which aimed, among other things, at rejecting 'temporary detention centres' and measures depriving immigrants of their liberty, rejecting the creation of 'temporary detention centres' in third countries, or denouncing the failure of the 'quota' policy, which has resulted in an increase in illegal immigration and the precarious employment of these workers.
instead of proposals that are needed to respond effectively to the serious social problems of the european union - more than 22 million unemployed and 72 million people living in poverty - the president of the council insisted on measures to support competitiveness and competition. thus, the emphasis on research, development and innovation is always presented as a way of creating a business-friendly environment and not as the answer that is needed for better health for all, higher levels of public education and creating quality and entitled employment. the president of the council, tony blair, therefore insisted on the need for greater labour flexibility, mobility and support for restructuring which reduces jobs, contributing to more unemployment and greater job insecurity. that is why it also insisted on the proposals for directives on the creation of the internal market in services and on working time, which makes it clear that what is being prepared is the insistence on neoliberalism, aggravating all the existing economic and social problems, in order to serve only the interests of the economic and financial groups of the european union, in response to the unice agenda.

in writing. the barcelona process was intended to be a turning point in relations between the european union and its southern neighbours and to provide a framework for the concerted development and mutual assistance of the mediterranean countries. the ten years of this process therefore require adjustment and reinforcement of its implementation in order to provide the conditions for meeting the current challenges and adapting to a new regional and international context. by combining levels of political, economic and social, bilateral and regional dialogue with opportunities for interaction, this process enhances the possibilities for rapprochement and the establishment of trusting relations between peoples. i think the most relevant point is the planned creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area from 2010 which should cover some 40 states and approximately 700 million consumers. it seems to me that a model of relations based on an enlarged free trade area will certainly be more effective and can, by promoting the economies of the south, contribute to the development of this region in order to avoid, for example, migratory tensions such as those we have seen in recent times. i voted in favour of the jäätteenmäki report.
in writing. although this report refers to the work of the previous ombudsman in his now-defunct mandate, we welcome the way in which he has carried out his work, seeking to draw the attention of the european institutions to citizens' complaints and even, in one case or another, achieving a resolution. it also put forward proposals which, if accepted, could improve the capacity to intervene and solve citizens' problems, in particular by making the european institutions respond more quickly. we also follow the rapporteur's position that there should be greater cooperation between the european ombudsman and the european parliament's committee on petitions and that efforts should be made to give greater visibility to the rights of individuals. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. europe faces a crisis of dialogue with its citizens the european ombudsman continues to receive complaints that fall outside his mandate. it seems to me therefore essential that a dialogue with the citizens should be re-established in which the powers of the institutions are explained in a clear and simple manner. the european ombudsman has taken initiatives in this regard and should continue to do so. the current ombudsman has also shown us that he is well aware of his role, and has even proposed intensified cooperation with his national or regional counterparts and measures to promote the highest levels of quality in european public administration. finally, i would stress that it is vital to maintain the impartiality of this influential body, which acts as a mediator between the public administration and the european citizens and offers extrajudicial solutions. i therefore voted in favour of mr mavrommattis' report.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, we know that this process of neo-liberal globalisation is contributing to the worsening of economic and social inequalities and to the widening of the gap between rich and poor and to environmental imbalances, both between and within different countries, as statistics and un reports demonstrate. it is high unemployment, inequalities in income distribution, poverty and social exclusion that are also generating increasing social tensions, including here in the european union. it is therefore not enough to recognise the existing situation; what is needed is a break with the economic, monetary and international trade policies that generate this situation, both at the global level and at the level of the european union, if the strategic objectives of sustainable development and the raising of living standards on a global scale are to be achieved. the amendments we are tabled are intended to underline the importance of changing some of these policies urgently so that the social dimension is properly safeguarded. for example, it is urgent to take concrete measures against financial speculation in global capital markets, including the introduction of a capital movements and capital gains tax, in order not only to reduce the volatility of capital markets and the risk of financial crisis, but also to promote investment and wealth creation in the real economy, to promote social inclusion and to guarantee human rights. it is also necessary to replace the lisbon strategy and the stability pact with a genuine european strategy of solidarity and sustainable development to promote equal rights, social protection for all, the eradication of poverty and social exclusion, the resolution of problems linked to precarious employment and the strengthening of the social rights of workers, the unemployed, the elderly and children. it is essential to ensure that all have access to high quality public services in areas such as water supply, health, education and housing, and it is therefore necessary that the european union should not insist on liberalising services in the context of the world trade organisation and gatt.

in writing. the 2004 athens olympic and paralympic games were the first to be held in a schengen member state without internal border controls. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the schengen visa system for members of the olympic family who are to participate in the olympic games in athens. in practical terms, it would allow them to enter the territory of the state where the games are held without having to undergo any further procedures or formalities other than the possession of this authorization card together with their passport or other official travel document. following the evaluation of its application in greece, it was concluded that this derogation scheme was a success and that it constituted a flexible and effective instrument and did not compromise the level of security required within the schengen area. i therefore support this proposal which adopts a nearly identical system (this time, in co-decision), with some adjustments to the regulation so that it can be applied to the new olympic and paralympic winter games in turin in 2006.
in writing. we voted in favour of this report, which improves the commission's proposal, which proposes an amendment to regulations 1408/71 and 574/72, taking account of the changes in national legislation in the field of social security, particularly in the new member states, since the accession negotiations. it also aims to update the list of provisions of social security conventions which continue to apply and are not replaced by regulation 1408/71, by proposing technical improvements. overall, the proposals now adopted improve existing legislation and provide legal certainty until the new regulation enters into force, thus helping to improve the protection of workers who opt for mobility in the member states of the european union.
in writing. as the recital to this report states, 'this regulation plays an important role in that it implements one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu, namely the free movement of european citizens. indeed, the possibility to live, work and move freely within the eu - with as few financial or administrative barriers as possible - is a tangible advantage that eu citizenship confers on citizens.' that's right. the social protection possibilities available to the citizens of the member states have been a factor of enormous importance in promoting genuine freedom of movement. in the present case, where no social security models or rules for the operation of the various systems are discussed, but only the necessary adaptations and updates of the present regulation are made, the vote in favour is justified as an adaptation in accordance with the interests and principles of the regulation in question.
in writing. the eel population in the european union has been declining in a worrying way in recent decades. due to the complex reproduction process of the european eel, it is essential that measures are taken to reverse the increasingly evident trend towards the extinction of this species. in addition to some emergency measures which need to be implemented immediately, there is a set of medium and long-term measures which should also be adopted in order to ensure, firstly, the recovery of the stocks of this species and, consequently, their proper management. this report presents a set of proposals in this direction which deserve my unconditional support.
in writing. we welcome the existence of a community action plan to support the recovery of the eel in the way it is proposed, particularly because it takes account of the need to implement socioeconomic measures for fishermen, the community financing of measures (emphasis should be placed on a separate budget line), the need for reliable data on the state of the resources, and the investigation of other causes of the reduction of the stocks, such as pollution. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. however, with regard to the national management plans of each member state, we emphasise three aspects:- that these plans should emphasise their precautionary nature, given the lack of scientific knowledge about the numbers of eel stocks and the spatial distribution of successive generations of eels;- that they should incorporate concrete measures to avoid the existence of physical obstacles that hinder or limit the migration of eels in waterways;- and that they should provide for the intensification of scientific research and the collection of data on fisheries, aquaculture and exports.
in writing. the matter under consideration is of significant importance for portugal and for portuguese fishing communities, and the concerns expressed by the rapporteur should be noted. i believe that there are good reasons to support, among other equally important aspects, the presentation of proposals for socioeconomic compensation for those who are harmed by the limitation of fishing and the limitation of the export of european eel. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

in writing. there are two ways of looking at globalization. one is to think that reality is avoidable (and undesirable), to think that if 19th century workers had protested more effectively there would have been no industrialization (and that this would have been a positive), to think that technological innovations are an evil in themselves. the other, realistic, history-conscious and aware of the responsibilities of each generation, is to seize the opportunities that globalization brings us. globalization is neither good nor bad in itself, it is a reality that can be used for good or for bad. the european union is a major player in the world economy, and it is the world's largest exporter of goods and services. and not only do you have that opportunity, you have that duty. that is the spirit in which we should approach globalisation.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the use of financial resources for the decommissioning of nuclear power stations. i agree with the principles set out in these reports, not only because i believe that nuclear energy must be surrounded by all safety measures, but also because i believe that we must take effective account of the financial resources that manage its life cycle. i think that the conditions for the use of financial resources for decommissioning set out in this report are responsible and effective, and i am particularly referring to the creation of a decommissioning fund which will take account of the management of funds generated by energy production. i would remind you that whenever we look at nuclear, it is a matter of priority to take account of the necessary safety and environmental protection measures for the life of a nuclear power station and it is in this framework that the proposed measures for its decommissioning in a safe, efficient and environmentally friendly way should be included.
in writing. in the run-up to the 11th conference of the parties to the unfccc, to be held in montreal from 28 november to 9 december, parliament stressed the need to give top priority to negotiations on the post-2012 emission reduction commitments under the kyoto protocol to the unfccc, which entered into force on 16 february 2005 after being ratified by 152 countries and regional organisations. there seems to be some overreach in setting greenhouse gas targets, given that little is known about the actual consequences of human interference in climate change, which is even more problematic with the us outside the kyoto protocol. but we welcome all measures aimed at reducing energy intensity and waste, improving energy efficiency, developing a new policy for less polluting transport, and promoting rail transport and public transport in general. we already have a very strong opinion on emissions trading, because as we know it does not solve any problems and only serves to aggravate environmental inequalities and imbalances. the richest countries will always be able to continue to pollute by buying emission rights from others, which is not acceptable. that is why we abstained.
in writing. the excellent report by mr wijkman sets out some measures to help solve the problem of climate change at world level. the eleventh conference of the parties will shortly be held in montreal. at this meeting, european leaders are expected to put forward proposals for a future climate change regime. such a regime should be based on common but differentiated responsibilities, aiming at continued emission reductions and the participation of more countries in these efforts. on the other hand, more ambitious targets should also be proposed. the european council of march 2005 insisted on a reduction of emissions by developed countries of between 15% and 30% by 2020. the rapporteur proposes to set long-term targets, suggesting a 60 to 80% reduction by 2050. finally, a strategy needs to be developed to make europe the most energy-efficient economy in the world. incentives should be created to increase the use of 'clean' technologies, and research and innovation should be promoted at european level to support sustainable energy and sustainable land use management.
in writing. the importance of the environment, and in particular of climate change, as one of our concerns, is, i think, obvious. i share a lot of the basic lines of environmental policy that europe has been advocating - and which are echoed in both the commission's report and the communication. but i think we should bear in mind two aspects. on the one hand, it is clear that the first concerns of the developing countries are not environmental, in that they are not original. on the other hand, developed societies are also not willing to give up their quality of life, and that should not be our purpose or our model. that is exactly why i believe that the main investment should be in research and development, since the objective, the model, should be to manage resources better, always ensuring a better and more sustainable quality of life.

the value of arms contracts signed by the four main european exporters in 2004 for developing countries was almost five billion dollars, according to a recent report by the us congress. an increase that represents a value five times higher than in 2003, which will harm development by proliferating conflicts in africa and other continents, no one knows. this is the reality which calls, more than ever, for the application of strict and effective rules on arms exports. europe cannot promote construction through development aid while at the same time promoting destruction through the unregulated export of conventional arms. we therefore support - as mr romeva's excellent report does - the urgency of making this code of conduct legally binding for all member states. and that is why we welcome - as the commissioner, whom i welcome, has - the council's decision to push for a genuine universal treaty at the un that would establish common rules for the global arms trade. the arms embargo on china, which has repeatedly threatened taiwan, must not be lifted until china pays for the tiananmen prisoners and missing persons and improves human rights in general. as for the wuermeling report, it contains a fundamental aspect for the future of the european defence project and the common foreign policy, which is reflected in amendment no 6 by my group. no world power has fully open markets for defense equipment. the united states protects its defense industries with a buy american act. we have much to learn from our american friends here. it is essential to introduce european preference in the procurement of defence equipment by member states. this is to ensure the survival of one of the sectors which contributes significantly to the success of the lisbon strategy, to technological innovation and to the union's strategic autonomy. let us not be delusional, let us not be naive: planes are not bananas, tanks are not refrigerators. let us not treat this matter as if it were a mere question of markets. parliament must take the lead in this debate, which is above all political and strategic, and what we are proposing is a first step in that direction. finally, as regards mr kristovskis' report - which i also welcome - i believe that it is not possible to have a coherent and effective non-proliferation strategy if the five nuclear-authorized states, including two member states, continue to fail to fulfil their commitments to progressively disarm in accordance with article 6 of the npt and to ignore or react against powers which have become nuclear outside the npt, such as israel, india and pakistan. and this is all the more serious as, in addition to more states, non-state actors and terrorists are also seeking to get their hands on these illegal weapons.

industries of the union states ever support in practice the outbreak or maintenance of illegitimate wars or dictatorial regimes. that is not the vocation of europe, that cannot be the practice of the in writing. this vote was the culmination of a long negotiation process marked by enormous pressure, especially from the powerful chemical industry, dramatically increasing the economic costs that could result from the entry into force of the standards contained in the first version of reach. the british presidency itself accepted germany's request to postpone the decision on reach, scheduled for the next ministerial meeting, on the pretext of the delay in the new government taking office. in any case, we are in a first reading of the legislative procedure and we are faced with a text which is rather backward, although there are very positive aspects in which progress has been made and which it is now important to defend until the end of the negotiations with the council. it is recalled that reach creates a single integrated system for the registration, evaluation and authorisation of chemicals in the european union, which aims to control and replace the most dangerous chemical agents (causing diseases such as cancer, affecting dna and the reproductive system, among other serious health problems); provide safety information on all chemicals at the registration stage and transmit information to consumers, workers and distributors. if we continue to yield to the pressure of the european chemical industry, we may weaken and distort the objectives of the programme, turning it into something even more burdensome than the current legislation, if it does not protect public health and safety.
in writing. the new regulation for chemicals on the market - reach - fills in obvious gaps in legislation and in our knowledge of the products we are exposed to every day. the registration of substances gives the european chemicals agency (also established by this regulation) the necessary authority to require more tests than those provided for each category, if there are grounds for doing so. a strong and efficient agency ensures that products are not marketed without the necessary precautions. data sharing is strongly encouraged and animal testing is thereby reduced to the strictly necessary. the imposition of a time limit on all authorizations and the obligation to submit a substitution plan for substances considered dangerous are also very positive aspects of this regulation. although i am pleased with the final result of the vote, i cannot help saying that i disagree with the inclusion of substances in tobacco, since they are already subject to their own legislation.
in writing. in this, as in all discussions, our duty is to defend the interests of the citizens, whether they are the most immediate or those that are more distant in time, little visible at present but of enormous relevance in the medium and long term. i voted in accordance with the criteria which i consider decisive when there is a - at least apparent - conflict between the interests of industry and the interests of environmental protection and public health. firstly, i believe that the protection of public health and the environment should be a priority, but i do not believe in fundamentalisms which make everything equal, which ignore the economic impact of the measures and, above all, which are unaware of the global dimension of these issues in the face of economies that do not shy away from environmental dumping. i am also convinced that european industry itself and the interests of competitiveness and technological innovation benefit from our demand. finally, i am convinced that the need to revive the european economy is urgent and worth our effort and commitment. i therefore believe that, in view of the amendments tabled, the vote in favour was the most justified, especially because i believe that there will still be an opportunity to make the necessary corrections, for example in the chapter on authorization.
in writing. although it is part of the wider discussion of the reach regulation, this proposal for a directive deals with a subject on which a broad agreement is easier to obtain. good consumer information is an essential element for a true market where freedom of choice can be effectively exercised. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. we supported the rejection of the commission proposal because, as the rapporteur says, it is not based on the latest scientific knowledge and on the possibility of using technical means to avoid situations considered cruel to animals. the commission proposal follows the international agreement on non-cruel trapping between the european union, the usa, canada and russia. however, this agreement has already been rejected by the european parliament twice, and it only came into force because the commission and the council argued that they did not want to create a conflict situation with the usa and canada. what is at stake is the very concept of "not cruel". the european parliament's committee on the environment argues that traps which cause animals to suffer agony for five minutes or more cannot be considered 'non-cruel' when there are possibilities to avoid it today. in any event, it is unacceptable that the european commission has accepted the international agreement without first hearing the european parliament.
in writing. once again, in addition to all the issues raised by the report on the code of conduct on arms exports, i believe that the issue of banning arms exports to china is crucial and fully justifies my vote in favour of this report. it has been and remains my view that the european union should persist in its decision to ban, because this is above all a signal that the 25 member states are giving in their defence of human rights and also of international order and peace. china is and will remain a major player on the international stage and a very important economic partner of the eu. in my view, the development of the chinese market will be one of the ways of developing democracy and respect for human rights. but that path cannot be taken without demand. it is in this context that the prohibition is rightly placed. we will be economic partners, but we will be demanding partners committed to building a better world.
in writing. first of all, we would like to point out that parliament took the initiative in drawing up a report on non-proliferation and not on disarmament. we consider that the resolution, although it contains positive points, contains very serious ones. the consideration of the possibility of 'recourse to military force' in the context of non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction is very serious and unacceptable. the 'support' that this policy has given to the monumental operation of manipulation, aggression and occupation of iraq by the us and its allies - on the unacceptable and false grounds that that country had weapons of mass destruction - betrays its real aims and intentions. the association between the so-called 'war on terror' in partnership with the united states and the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction is dangerous - and not innocent. we also regret the rejection of our group's proposals for the creation of a european disarmament agency, for denouncing the us use of the united nations, for making europe a nuclear-weapon-free zone, for the withdrawal of us nuclear weapons from europe, or for urging germany to eliminate its uranium enrichment potential at the garching research reactor.
in writing. in matters of international policy, and when world security is at stake, the commitment in the declarations needs to be reflected in the ability to act accordingly. it is not possible to be exacting in words and indeterminate in actions. the questions raised by the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction risk being one of those cases where the vehemence of statements is not accompanied by the same determination on the concrete political level, and very especially, and very significantly, on the diplomatic level. i think that the european union must first of all make some changes to the clarity of its speech. the widespread perception that the eu will not be consistent weakens our diplomatic position. i therefore vote in favour of this report, in the hope that its adoption will strengthen the eu's resolve in this matter. without preferring or even encouraging military solutions, but revealing determination and decision.
in writing. this report is part of the process of militarization of the european union - which the rejected 'european constitution' was intended to enshrine - by destroying one of its fundamental pillars: the development of the military industry in the different eu countries. the aim is to help strengthen the 'european' arms industry and what it considers to be its 'inevitable' process of concentration. the report is also clear on what is at stake, stating that six of the 25 eu countries purchase more than 90% of their military equipment - how much will they produce? the ep report is clear: it is intended to remove the competence for arms policy from the states, or rather the so-called 'small' states, by progressively creating a 'european defence market' 'in accordance with interoperability standards agreed in nato'. it called on the 'large' states and the big arms companies to overcome their contradictions, arguing that 'public contracts in the defence sector are governed more by european community legislation than by national legislation' and that 'a restrictive interpretation of national security interests is appropriate'. all under the "leadership" of the so-called "european defence agency". the arms race at its best... that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the aim, as advocated by the rapporteur, of promoting the creation of a european defence market and of making this market free and competitive, with clear respect for the specificities of the sector, is a purpose which i share and which i support. in that sense, my vote is understandably in favour. there is, however, one aspect - among many others - which deserves special attention. the defence market is one of those where investment in r & d is most relevant. all these objectives must therefore be accompanied by a european determination to modernise, to become more competitive and to rely on technological development as an important lever for economic development. the fact that a defence market is only possible if such investment is a clear option, therefore, gives me more reason to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. we are clearly critical of the serious and irresponsible statements by the president of iran regarding israel. the resolution, however, is illuminating on the policy of 'two weights and two measures' which characterises the european union. the resolution is characterised by a partial view of the situation in the middle east, incorporating aspects that are part of a logic of escalation of the confrontation. the resolution, while taking the blame for iran's support for terrorism, ignores the very serious responsibility of the us, israel and the eu itself for the worsening of the situation in the region. the consequences of the aggression and military occupation of iraq by the united states and its allies are not denounced. the situation in palestine is referred to as a 'conflict', whitewashing the occupation of palestine and the most brutal violation of the fundamental rights of the palestinian people by israel. iran is required to comply with its international obligations in the development of its nuclear programme, without questioning what is required of other countries in the region which have developed programmes and possess nuclear weapons. the statements made by the president of iran only serve to make the situation more difficult in a region completely destabilized by the policy of interference, war and domination carried out by the united states, with the support of its regional and european allies.
president-in-office of the council. madam president, this has been an extremely interesting and informative debate with a typically wide range of views expressed. i am pleased to see that members of the european parliament are so engaged in these important issues. i certainly look forward to discussing them further with the delegation that will be going to hong kong. the key message i take from this debate is that we should maintain our level of ambition for the round as a whole. we should be supporting the package of measures for developing countries outlined by commissioner mandelson and this must be seen as a down-payment with more to come, not a final deal. we should not underestimate the benefits of trade to the developing world. just look at where south korea was in the 1950s – a country with a similar level of income to the average in the continent of africa – and compare that with where it is today as a result of trade. look at china, which over the last 20 years has taken one third of a billion people out of extreme poverty as a result of trade. the results are enormously impressive. our objective should be to kick open the door to the developed world’s economies for the least-developed countries. that is what the eu package is about. however, we should not underestimate the benefits of an ambitious trade round to the european union either. as commissioner mandelson said, the benefits in terms of services and nama if we achieve a balanced outcome to the round will be of benefit to the eu economy and indeed the world economy as a whole. there are difficult issues in this trade round. we have heard about sugar, bananas, cotton: all these require discussion internally and will be part of the negotiations. as the uk presidency we fully support the commission and its negotiating tactics in the round. commissioner mandelson has made a serious offer that requires serious consideration by other countries. we now need to see progress on nama, on services, on the part of brazil, india and other countries. i would like to say to you, the members of this parliament, that we recognise that we all have to take any final deal home and justify it to our electorates. i was asked about the specific arrangements for hong kong as regards the european parliament delegation. the uk presidency is making plans to meet with members of the delegation near the launch of the conference and hopefully again towards the end. the commission will be holding daily briefings that will be given to meps. we are also planning a reception co-hosted with the commission for meps to meet with eu ministers. once again, i thank you for your time today and for your support in our preparations for hong kong.
member of the commission. madam president, the remark with which i agree most came from the honourable member who said that the commissioner certainly does not have an easy job in knitting together the interests, views and policies of 25 member states and then fitting those 25 views into the 149 wto members – minus of course we 25. one thing i am sure about in my approach to hong kong and in the approach to the round as a whole, is that i have an obligation to do what is right in the long term, rather than what will get me cheers in the short term. i have found in my time in this job that it is very easy to play to a gallery. it is very easy to mouth the slogans; to say the things that will please the people you are talking to; to get them to champion you and give you all the cheers in the world. but when i say what is right in the long term, rather than what will get me praise in the short term, i mean: what is right for the global economy as a whole? what is right for multilateralism and multilateral processes and institutions? what is right not just for us in europe, but for developing countries? there are very many different sorts, sizes and states of development in developing countries, as i am finding out. there is also considerable public interest in this round. i am grateful to bob geldof for giving out my email address, which has now clocked up something approaching 100 000 messages from members of the public wishing me well at hong kong. i am sure that he did so in the best possible spirit. i know that those who have been speaking this afternoon speak for and reflect that public opinion. i greatly welcome and value the joint parliamentary resolution on the doha round which has been put together. i take it as a strong signal of support for the commission and my approach in the round. i have always welcomed the guidance and wisdom of the european parliament and will continue to do so at hong kong and beyond. i am sorry that my fellow countryman, mr farage, has not remained in the chamber. well, he has a very pressing diary with many engagements. unfortunately, in his hatred of all things european, he got slightly carried away with his description and praise of the us agricultural offer that has been tabled. at first sight, the us market access offer is indeed ambitious. but it also tactical and highly unrealistic, as i suspect they know. on domestic support, the us offer – which i strongly welcomed at the time and continue to do so – is far from being as ambitious as it seemed. it presents no real cuts in actual levels of spending. it brings down the ceilings of spending, but that is not, of course, quite the same thing. when it comes to its main domestic support programme, its counter cyclical payments, those remain untouched by the proposals that the united states has tabled. on export competition the united states is very ambitious: very ambitious with our export subsidies, not quite so ambitious when it comes to its own export credits and its own food aid. however, i am sure it is only a matter of time before the us offer is improved and i look forward to that negotiation. agriculture, however, is very important to get right in this round. the uruguay round made limited inroads into agricultural protection. inevitably, therefore, agriculture is a focus of the doha round. but let us not overlook the fact that the biggest welfare gains for all developing countries will come from liberalisation, not of agriculture, but in industrial goods, which account for 75% of developing countries’ trade and most of the tariffs that they pay. that is why this must not be an agriculture-only round. it must be balanced. mr désir was right about agricultural liberalisation. of course agricultural liberalisation will benefit some developing countries. the highly competitive agricultural exporters in the developing world, like brazil and argentina, are the developing countries that will be the chief beneficiaries. but the biggest winners in most agricultural liberalisation scenarios would be in the developed world, not the developing world, including large agricultural exporters such as australia and new zealand. that is not me speaking, that is the world bank speaking in its recent publication. let me just make two last points about non-agricultural market access and services. in nama i want to give an assurance to honourable members that we are certainly not asking from developing countries what we are prepared to do for and give ourselves. the principle of less than full reciprocity is important; it means commitments according to capacity and we shall certainly uphold that. on services, the eu does not impose trade liberalisation on developing countries. we offer a free choice of sectors for developing countries. there is no pressure to open sectors such as education, health or water, although, in the case of water, i think many would benefit from such an advance. it is simply not the case that we are imposing overnight liberalisation; transition periods for developing countries would be of their own choice. we will not be proposing liberalisation of audiovisual services. lastly, on the subject of sugar, i think that mrs kinnock was right in her description of the anger amongst acp countries. there is indeed a virtual eur 40 million offer on the table and i was not right in saying, as i had been advised this morning, that this figure had been agreed with acp countries. there is certainly a marked imbalance between what is on offer in the sugar action programme to acp countries and what we are offering to our domestic sugar producers. before we reach final conclusions on this, we need to think through the implications of what we are offering. but clearly, on the question of budgetary allocation, we look to the council and parliament, as there are conflicting views and voices in this matter in both the council and parliament. in conclusion, as far as our transparency with the european parliament in hong kong is concerned, we will keep in close touch with the european parliament members who are there. they will participate at meetings at the interparliamentary conference that will take place in hong kong. i look forward to regular daily contact with parliamentarians, so that together we get this meeting right.
the commissioner, who is leading the negotiations on behalf of the council and the commission for the so-called doha round of the wto, said that the ambitions for international trade liberalization remained intact, despite the reduced expectations for the outcome of the hong kong summit. the commissioner's ambitions - which are also part of the negotiating mandate - are the same as those expressed by the confederations of large employers for the ninth time in their declaration of 21 november: greater liberalisation in agriculture, access to the market for industrial products and services, and the guarantee that the round of negotiations will be concluded by the end of 2006. liberalisation which, as the latest undp report points out, has increased inequalities. what they want is control of international trade within the framework of capitalist competition, where the large economic and financial groups would control the economies of the states, their agriculture, industrial production, services and natural resources. the reality, resulting from the offensive of capitalism, is dramatic and unacceptable. it calls for a new international order based on cooperation, solidarity and development, respect for the sovereignty of each state, its right to respond to the needs of its people and to manage its resources.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the new outbreaks of avian influenza in asian countries and some european countries, following the situation in italy and the netherlands where many millions of birds were killed, justify the need to take more effective measures in the field of prevention and to establish appropriate mechanisms to support member states where outbreaks of the disease may occur so that there is rapid intervention, isolation and prevention of their spread. so, without being alarmist, and in view of the public health consequences of possible epidemics, it is necessary to act with the greatest effectiveness and readiness in prevention, both in the european union and in third countries, especially in asia. although avian influenza has a worldwide distribution and affects most poultry, its distribution is influenced by the relationship between poultry and wild birds, the location of poultry production units, the routes of migratory birds and the seasons. it is now known that surveillance and prevention are very important, even for low pathogenic viruses, given the possibility of mutation to a high pathogenic virus after spreading for short periods in a poultry population. and although this type of infection is not common in humans, it is known that in recent years outbreaks of infection caused by certain viruses (bird flu) have been documented causing the death of dozens of people in asia. the committee on agriculture, fisheries and rural development has therefore, in the light of the opinions of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety and the committee on budgets, whose rapporteurs, mr robert sturdy and mr jan mulder, i thank for their work, insisted on the need to strengthen the commission's proposal in five key areas. first, the focus on prevention and monitoring, starting with the identification of risk areas in each country, to avoid the possible consequences for public health of an avian influenza epidemic. secondly, greater community support for the development of oral vaccine research for the various cases and its application, if necessary, and 100% sharing of the burden of vaccination. thirdly, community support to member states for the development of a disease surveillance/monitoring system, including laboratory diagnostics and research (especially of appropriate vaccines). fourthly, the development of cooperation and technical assistance measures for third countries, especially asian countries, to ensure the prevention and control of avian influenza in the countries of origin. fifthly, greater support for farmers who face loss of income if they have to slaughter birds, destroy eggs, clean and disinfect farms and equipment, and contaminate food, with the european union sharing part of these costs with the member states. the level of community financial assistance, which according to the committee on agriculture should be 50% of the expenditure borne by the member states, should be the same for both cases of highly pathogenic and low pathogenic influenza, because if there is intervention and slaughter of animals the losses are the same. it seems to me, however, that this is a case where it is worthwhile to increase the community contribution to 60%, as i propose, since if a state is faced with such a situation after having taken the necessary preventive measures, it should be the target of community solidarity, even to prevent the spread of the disease. i also have another proposal for which i would ask the house to support. it seems to me that it is more socially just to support any poultry farmers whose farms are affected by the disease, not only for the costs and losses caused, but also by 50% of the income lost during the period of launching a new farm, without prejudice, of course, to market mechanisms. finally, i would like to thank you for your cooperation in the preparation of this report and i hope that the commission and the council will take due account of the european parliament's proposals so that all the necessary efforts can be made to prevent and combat possible outbreaks of disease, trying to prevent their spread in the defence of public health.

the debate on the report by mr andrew duff, drawn up on behalf of the committee on constitutional affairs, on the guidelines for the adoption of the european commission (2005/2024 (ini)) (a6-0179/2005) will continue.
the duff report opens a ritual of parliamentary approval by the european commission, followed by almost silence on the subject in the rules of procedure. this ritual qualifies the importance of the political fact of the commission's approval. first, because it shows a higher degree of demand and gives it another basis of legitimacy. secondly, because parliament is thus increasingly taking up a role in the process of forming the commission that is far from being merely symbolic. thirdly, because this creates a new relationship of influence between the european political institutions, which anticipates the mechanisms of control and accountability inherent in constitutional semantics. the commission's parliamentary approval procedure now has a framework of rules which establish greater fairness in the hearing of candidates by parliamentary committees and greater consistency in the final evaluation, which is now agreed in the conference of presidents and the conference of committee chairs. it is good for us all to be aware that procedures in a democratic order do not have a merely formal or symbolic meaning. the procedures synthesise the values of public morality in the machinery of the institutions, and transfer to that machinery the claims of the community which judges it and justifies it. the european political process has become more demanding as it has become more ambitious. it must therefore be a process of intense scrutiny, generating strong institutions and leaderships capable of opening the doors to the future. europe can no longer recognize itself without this growing visibility and legitimacy of its institutions, without this demand for probity and responsibility which is imposed on everyone, but which is especially imposed on political leaders, since they are the ones who have responsibility for the world.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow at 11 a.m.

in writing. although the european parliament's proposals make improvements to the european commission's proposed regulation, they do not call into question the central issue, namely the monopoly and control of pharmaceutical companies over medicines through patenting. the proposals put forward by the european parliament continue to 'legalize' and impose a 'compulsory' model of dispensing essential medicines to huge populations in the face of profound regulatory cynicism, without giving priority to the creation of mechanisms to promote research and the development of research capacity, manufacture and supply by these and those peoples of the medicines that are essential to them and to which they have a right. the aim is to 'regulate' access to medicines by so-called underdeveloped countries, so that multinationals can charge cheaper prices and thus expand their market without losing the privileges they retain. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial' in the definition of the term 'commercial'. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. although i think that we are still far from ideal solutions, i think it is worth applauding the effort made in the proposal for a regulation - in particular with some of the amendments voted by the european parliament to make it possible for the poorest countries to fight diseases of enormous gravity, and which cause enormous mortality, more effectively and less costly. the protection of property rights, in particular intellectual property rights, is not and cannot be considered incompatible with the defence and commitment we must make to the objective of making the medicines that the poorest countries need most accessible to them.
in writing. as the rapporteur has pointed out, the best way to avoid a possible human pandemic of avian influenza is to eradicate the disease from birds effectively and completely. it is therefore in this direction that the community's research and financial efforts should be directed, in particular in the development and production of oral vaccines against multiple strains which are effective in all relevant bird species. we also thought it appropriate to amend the directive currently in force by adopting control measures which also cover low pathogenicity viruses in poultry, in order to avoid the risk of evolving into highly pathogenic viruses. the report, together with a whole series of measures to prevent human infection, could only have been voted for.
in writing. i welcome the approval of my report. it is important that there be greater community support for the development of oral vaccine research for the various cases and its application where necessary, as well as 100% burden sharing with vaccination. community support to member states for the development of a disease surveillance/monitoring system, including laboratory diagnostics and research into appropriate vaccines, and the development of cooperation and technical assistance actions for third countries, in particular asian countries, in order to ensure the prevention and screening of avian influenza in the countries of origin is also important; as for the level of community financial assistance, it has only gone up to 50% of the expenditure borne by the member states, and it should be the same for both high and low pathogenic influenza cases, and my proposal to increase it to 60 has been rejected, which i regret. the proposal for 50% support for loss of income during the period of setting up a new farm was also rejected, without prejudice, of course, to market mechanisms. in any event, i hope that the commission and the council will take due account of the proposals adopted in the interests of public health.
in writing. public health measures cost money. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. not only is there the possibility of a worldwide pandemic, but it must be borne in mind that certain member states may be more easily affected because of their location as a transit point for migratory wild birds. if we add to this the need for prevention, in particular in the development of disease monitoring and surveillance systems, laboratory costs and research into new vaccines, we realise the scale of the financial effort required. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to amend regulation 974/98, which was the legal framework during the transitional period for the adoption of the euro by the current members of the euro area. the aim is now to use this legal framework for the countries that joined the european union on 1 may 2004 and which have a legal obligation to join the euro area. one of the key issues is to shorten the transitional period and provide for an optional solution known as the 'big bang', with the introduction of euro banknotes and coins at the same time as the adoption of the euro as a monetary unit. the report by parliament goes the same way and even tries to impose the idea that no member state can leave the euro zone, which is unacceptable. we believe that a member state has every right to leave the euro zone. it is discriminatory to try to impose such a situation on new member states when it is known that two countries have an opt-out clause (denmark and england) and another has decided not to join (sweden). that is why we are voting against, and we are certain that we will maintain our position of principle against the euro. moreover, the consequences of monetary policy are already clear, with economic stagnation and unemployment, which still ...... in writing. the idea of voluntary crossborder cooperation deserves my support and i advocate its encouragement. as a general rule, forms of cooperation between the administrations of the different member states, especially when they result from a voluntary initiative of those administrations (although it can be encouraged) and do not result in a new administrative and bureaucratic entity, seem to me to be of great use. and in this case, the fact that it includes crossborder neighbourhoods outside the eu also seems to me to be commendable. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report. there is, however, one aspect which i cannot overlook. these initiatives cannot be encouraged, encouraged and, above all, conceived in an alternative logic to the central powers. that is to say, the european union cannot, by means of these incentives, seek to achieve results of internal disintegration of the states, which can only be detrimental to each of the member states in particular, but above all because that is not, should not and cannot be the function or purpose of the union.
in writing. the euro introduction regulation has proved to be a good legal framework during the transition period to the adoption of the euro in the current euro area countries. it therefore seems to be a suitable basis for future member states to join the european currency. certain technical adaptations will be necessary. but more importantly, after the experience of the changeover to the euro, there is a need to fine-tune communication strategies in order to provide, in particular, for the dual indication of prices for the information of citizens and also the modification of the time limits for the circulation of the two currencies, as well as to extend the time limits for the exchange of the old currency with the banks. i therefore voted in favour of mr rosati's report.
in writing. since october 1992, and after three extensions (until the end of 2005), the council has decided to maintain the minimum standard rate of vat in the european union at 15%. the commission's present proposal now aims to extend this rate once again until 31 december 2010, which deserves our agreement. the initial intention of establishing a minimum rate was to create a band with a maximum rate which would be harmonised to a single vat rate for the whole community. although no member state has a rate below 15% or above 25%, the establishment of this band for this purpose would undermine the fiscal sovereignty of the member states and their options for financing the community budget. however, the report reintroduces the question, which leads us to vote against. it also intends, in a subtle way, to accelerate the debate on vat harmonization, which calls into question other elements of the flexibility of the present system, in particular the reduced vat rates in accordance with the different social and cultural choices of the various member states. which reinforces, once again, our vote against.
in writing. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's security forces are able to take part in the fight against terrorism. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. liberalisation means attacking the achievements of workers and the sovereignty of peoples, the appropriation by the big multinationals of natural resources and biodiversity, environmental destruction, the increase in unemployment, the ruin of millions of small farmers and the undermining of food sovereignty and food security. the european parliament has been a key player in the development of the community's relations with the countries of central and eastern europe, and it has been a key player in the development of the community's relations with the countries of central and eastern europe. that's all that's at stake.
in writing. the conviction that the development of international trade contributes to economic growth, development, employment and - also - to a better environment in international relations is fortunately now widely held. nevertheless, there are still groups today with conflicting agendas and programmes, but who are engaged in a common struggle against a freer and more open world for trade. it is good that we do not follow these voices, but it is also necessary to understand the origin of these discontents, because politics is not done by ignoring reality. in this context, this joint resolution addresses the most important concerns and the most defensible positions. i believe that the european union must at the same time take a clear and strong negotiating position but also a sincere desire to support economic development and the growth of world trade. i therefore welcome the statement in this resolution that the objective of supporting economic growth in developing countries is to be upheld. the emphasis on social, environmental, labour, cultural and, needless to say, economic concerns is also positive. more international trade, and more fair trade, without ever forgetting the responsibilities we also have towards our own citizens.
in writing. regardless of the assessment of the principles, criteria and standards to be submitted to the commission as a collegiate body, it is not permissible for the european parliament to approve reports stating that the entry into force of the constitution is foreseen on 1 november 2006. "only a huge obsession with federalism and neoliberalism leads the majority of parliament to insist on this thesis, even after the defeat in the referendums in france and the netherlands that prevent the adoption of the european constitution. there are positive aspects to the evaluation criteria and principles, but we must not forget that more than competence, commitment and suitability are the policies they advocate, either individually or collectively. that is a fundamental basis of our appreciation and evaluation.
in writing. maritime transport is vital to portugal, given our important coastline. they are also important for the whole union, which has a large stretch of sea borders. i therefore believe that it is essential to provide the union with a viable and competitive european navy within the framework of the lisbon strategy. community action on competition in maritime transport must take account of the emergence of new maritime nations such as china, korea or taiwan. it is therefore essential to have instruments to protect the new frameworks for commercial cooperation between liner operators on traffic to or from the union. i therefore voted in favour of mrs kratsa's report.
in writing. without entering into a debate on tax harmonization and the common vat system, the main purpose of this resolution is to extend for another year (end of 2006) the experimental period for member states that have opted to introduce reduced vat rates for labour-intensive services. we thought that this one-off measure could help to promote job creation while reducing the shadow economy, and there is still a long way to go to assess the socioeconomic impact of this measure, which also allows greater flexibility in indirect taxation. it should be borne in mind that the abrupt termination of this measure could result in higher prices. this system should apply to all the present member states and discrimination against the new member states is not acceptable.
on 30 november, the european commission published its proposals for fishing quotas and associated measures for 2006 under the common fisheries policy, to be adopted by the council by the end of the year. the commission states that its objective is to reconcile, as far as possible, a gradual approach to the restoration of fish stocks with the continuation of fishing activities. however, the proposals which the commission is putting forward for reducing fishing effort are not accompanied by an assessment of the economic and social costs, particularly for fishermen. the fisheries sector, particularly in portugal, is already being hit hard, among other things by the increase in fuel prices, and i therefore call for measures at community level, especially since it is a matter of a common policy to support the income of fishermen, especially in small-scale coastal fishing, in order to safeguard the future of the sector.
portugal has been plagued by the relocation of businesses, which is aggravating unemployment to alarming levels, particularly affecting women. this time it is the american multinational delphi which has just announced the closure of one of its units, the linho cable factory, which once had some 1 200 workers and is now pressing the remaining 300 to lay off when it is known that the multinational delphi has made profits in the various factories it owns in portugal, with a total profit of millions of euros. i therefore, mr president, expressing my full solidarity with these workers, once again call on the council and the commission to take urgent measures to prevent the worsening of unemployment and to put a stop to these wild relocations of multinationals in the various countries of the european union and, in particular, in portugal.
