regardless of party considerations, it is always possible to compare the ceiling and priorities of the community budget for 2006, about 1.01% of community gni, with that of 2005, or with the proposals of the luxembourg and british presidencies for the financial framework 2007-2013. but let us not forget that the 2000-06 financial framework foresees 1.08% of community gni for next year, or that the european parliament's proposal for the 2007-13 financial framework provides for 1.0% and that of the commission for about 1.14%. in fact, in recent years there has been a real reduction in the community budget, aiming to fix it at around 1%, with the structural funds representing only 0.36 to 0.37% of community gni, which meets the requirements of the economically more developed countries of the european union. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. the amsterdam treaty has made enormous progress in combating discrimination by extending the concept to other dimensions beyond equality between men and women. the principle of equality and non-discrimination is an integral part of the core of fundamental rights that underpin the eu. this proposal designates 2007 as the european year of equal opportunities for all, with a view to promoting equality and eliminating all forms of discrimination. the idea of organising this initiative arose from the evaluation of the results in the green paper on equality and combating discrimination in the enlarged eu. it will help to promote three priorities: information and awareness-raising; analysis and monitoring of the impact of anti-discrimination legislation; and networking between stakeholder groups. promoting equal opportunities is key to achieving a more cohesive, competitive and dynamic society and economy, reaping the benefits of diversity. we should therefore increase awareness-raising initiatives of this kind to combat discriminatory attitudes and behaviour and to inform citizens of their rights and obligations. it should also act as a kind of awareness-raising campaign to put pressure on member states which are still lacking to transpose the directives quickly.
in writing. at a time when discrimination, inequalities and social injustices are on the increase, it is worth reaffirming that non-discrimination is a fundamental principle which must be respected in all policies - economic, social and cultural, we add - but it falls short of what is required in view of the seriousness of the social situation in the various eu countries. although it mentions the need to respect rights and equal opportunities, the need for participation and the right to information - increasing knowledge and awareness of rights (added, acquired, lost or to be acquired) - the report does not identify the determining causes of their violation or non-fulfilment. when workers are confronted with a generalized offensive against their rights and social gains, an offensive that is promoted at eu level, by more awareness campaigns and propaganda that are carried out or by more containment measures that are promoted, the reality and the consequences of the capitalist offensive will prevail, that is, the most unbridled exploitation, the destruction of public services and their appropriation by private capital, poverty and social injustice. equal opportunities first require the fight against the policies that attack them.
in writing. equal treatment, enshrined in the treaty of amsterdam, is a fundamental right of all citizens. in order to take stock of the progress made in the fight against discrimination and at the same time to gather views on how the union could strengthen its action in this area, the european commission launched in may 2004 a wide consultation in the form of a green paper entitled 'equality and combating discrimination in the enlarged eu'. it was from the evaluation of the results of this publication that the idea of organising a 'european year of equal opportunities for all' in 2007 was born. the initiative has four objectives: to raise public awareness, stimulate debate, promote the concept of diversity and promote respect and tolerance. despite the abundance of european legislation in the field of combating discrimination, many citizens are either unaware of it or are not familiar with it. the promotion of a media event such as a 'european year' should therefore be supported as it represents an excellent instrument for raising awareness and informing european public opinion. the european year will also put pressure on member states which are lagging behind in transposing the equality directives.
in writing. while it is true that discrimination, for whatever reason, is widely combated from a legal point of view, it is not possible to state categorically that all discrimination is prevented and combated in practice. the commission argues that it is in this context that a european year of equal opportunities for all will make sense. i've never been a big fan of celebrating as a way of solving problems. on the contrary, i have always feared that the promotion of international years or days on this or that subject might have a pernicious effect, only succeeding in concealing ignorance of the problem in the remaining days or years. there is, however, a recent tradition of promoting these initiatives, with a widespread belief that there is - and indeed there is - a side to the cause of increased visibility that is advantageous. i therefore consider that the theme of celebration dealt with in this report justifies my vote in favour.
in writing. as the epp shadow rapporteur i supported this excellent report by mrs roure. denmark cannot use an option of inclusion under the protocol, as neither the eurodac regulation nor the dublin ii regulation are part of the development of schengen. this is why an international agreement between the community and denmark and a protocol to the agreement between the community, iceland and norway are needed. the proposals are aimed at extending to denmark the provisions of the eurodac system and the determination of the member state responsible for examining an asylum application. it is a positive step, although the conclusion of such agreements should be exceptional and transitional. these situations raise serious doubts as to the different guarantees that asylum seekers will enjoy if their asylum application is dealt with in denmark or in one of the member states participating in the european asylum policy, as denmark will apply these two regulations but will remain outside all other measures taken under this policy. i agree with the rapporteur that the legal basis to be applied will be the second paragraph of article 300 (3) tec, i.e. that parliament should have been consulted in the process of giving a favourable opinion.
in writing. this proposal deserves our agreement. the activity of the different fleets of the member states operating under fisheries agreements and protocols between the european union and third countries should not be interrupted for administrative reasons, in particular because of the long negotiation periods and legal ratification procedures to which these agreements are subject. these disruptions often last for several months, with vessels being immobilized and fishermen unemployed, creating difficulties in supplying fish to the national and community markets. the proposal thus allows the third country to issue fishing licences on the date provided for in the exchange of letters between the two parties, even before the final adoption of the text of the agreement by the council. we hope that this proposal will enter into force as soon as possible and we shall see whether its implementation will ensure that fleets are not brought to a standstill or, at the very least, that the current periods are significantly reduced. in any event, the costs of long negotiation periods and renewal of agreements should not be borne by fishermen and the necessary economic and social compensation mechanisms should be established to ensure the survival of fishermen.
in writing. the report under consideration deserves my approval for two reasons. firstly, because it is clearly necessary, so that administrative and bureaucratic difficulties do not cause further difficulties for the fishing industry. but there is another reason why i agree with this report. as the rapporteur says, this whole process is excessively bureaucratic, inefficient and unjustified. i would even say that it is almost kafkaesque nonsense, this whole succession of agreements and provisional licences imposed by a highly inconvenient mechanism. i therefore support the rapporteur in her wish that this situation be reviewed. the competitiveness of a european industry - in the case of fisheries - cannot be constrained by bureaucratic inefficiency in the community institutions.
in writing. the goodwill and good intentions which underlie the assumptions of the programme in question deserve my agreement. as for the actual effectiveness of its execution, i have some doubts. however, since we are discussing a provisional programming, i think our concern should be to approve this programme in good time, with the new framework that has now been given to it, concentrating our efforts on the revision and, above all, the evaluation of past programmes, in the design of the future eia regulation. the eu's foreign policy - because that is what it is about - must be effective. and efficiency is only proven by evaluating the results. this must therefore be one of our main concerns in the next legislative moment in this matter.
in writing. of all the aspects which are mentioned in this report, and which justify my vote in favour because they fall within a balanced perspective of environmental protection, consumer protection and the promotion of energy efficiency, there is one which i think should be highlighted. my attitude in favour of a free and open economy is always based on the assumption that full access to information is possible, or at least encouraged, because without information the consumer is not truly free to choose. it is therefore the rapporteur's concern with the information to be provided to consumers that i would like to highlight in my vote in favour.
in writing. a compromise has been reached which is further back than the initial proposals, but it is good to try to achieve greater efficiency in the final use of energy, and we therefore support measures which actually aim at this objective. ♪ however, while the final proposal maintains the recognition of the important role that the public sector can play in this area, notably in launching energy efficiency pilot projects, in the context of public procurement, by establishing energy efficiency criteria, or also by encouraging the integration of energy efficiency improvement requirements into their investments, it insists on free competition. so our final abstention vote is based on this disagreement with amendment no 60, which is, moreover, completely inappropriate. we cannot agree that, on the subject of energy efficiency, one should insist on market liberalization as the rapporteur did, or insist on 'safeguarding a level playing field for all energy suppliers'. we think this is a strategic sector where the state must maintain a dominant position.
in writing. the european union must be more consistent in its approach to energy efficiency, whether it is in terms of consistency with its discourse - and its attitude - to major environmental agreements such as kyoto, or in terms of rationality, particularly economic and environmental rationality. the emphasis in these matters should, in my view, be on efficiency and rationality. these should be the standards which guide our environmental and energy policies.
in writing. the proposal for amending budget no 8/2005, as amended by the letter of amendment of 16 november 2005, is worrying because it cancels the request for additional payment needs of the original €650 million for the structural funds (taking into account that some €380 million had already been obtained through transfers from other headings), in addition to cutting the same amount in expenditure on agricultural markets. the committee is concerned that the payments made and the few applications received from the new member states do not even guarantee the full implementation of the appropriations available under the structural funds, especially as we are nearing the end of the current financial framework and there is the so-called 'n+2' rule, which automatically cancels commitment expenditure when it is not implemented within two years. the return of own resources to the member states will amount to some €3.9 billion, obviously benefiting the main net contributors. while not creating the conditions for the effective and full implementation of the structural funds, as would be desirable, these returns will once again help to meet the constraints imposed by the stability pact, contributing to the reduction of deficits in some of these countries.
in writing. the economic value of simplified and speedy proceedings is enormous, as countries benefiting from both secure and speedy judicial systems well know. a european order for payment procedure, as is proved by similar instruments at national level, is precisely in this direction, promoting greater legal certainty in commercial transactions and better justice. however, as several member states have mentioned, they must ensure that its scope does not exceed what is reasonable and necessary in the field of cooperation between sovereign states. with these considerations, my vote was in favour.
in writing. the taxation of companies was already one of the topics covered by the so-called monti package for tax harmonization. after the adoption of the lisbon strategy, the creation of an internal market without tax obstacles gained new impetus. the proposal, under article 94 of the treaty on the approximation of laws, advances the creation of a common consolidated corporate tax base. the objectives are clear: to remove tax barriers for companies carrying out crossborder operations and to create the conditions for large multinational companies to operate under a single system of dividend distribution and crossborder profit and loss compensation, facilitating restructuring, merger and acquisition operations. it thus contributes to the effective implementation of the european company statute by increasing the possibilities of 'legal' tax evasion for these companies and not by preventing tax evasion, contrary to what it claims. the european parliament, in its maximalist spirit, even proposes the possibility of moving forward with enhanced cooperation in this field if some member states do not want to go down this road. we have always rejected this approach, not only because it is contrary to the fiscal sovereignty of the member states, but also because it does not solve the fundamental problem of the burden of taxation falling on labour. that is why we voted against this report.
madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, mr president-in-office, ladies and gentlemen, the european council in march and the jha council in april 2004 defended the need for data retention rules, considering that modern telecommunications, with all the benefits inherent in them, can be exploited by international crime and, in particular, by terrorism. as a result of these decisions, we have received a framework decision which was rejected by the european parliament, and we have received the present proposal for a directive which, as president cavada said, is positive in that it takes account of the prerogatives of this parliament through a new legal basis which is being proposed to us. i cannot, however, but regret that we have been forced to work in an extremely short space of time. but we tried our best. it was a very difficult negotiation and the compromise reached is far from ideal, but it was possible if we want to reach an agreement at first reading. unlike other colleagues, i think the decision to set a retention period between a minimum of six months and a maximum of 24 months is a positive one. we cannot risk our joint crime-fighting effort failing because data has been deleted too soon or not even retained. but i think it is essential to ensure that the data retained are stored securely and that there can be no abuse of any kind by strengthening the rules on data protection, security and access. member states should lay down appropriate penalties in accordance with their national law. if we fail to make these rules effective, we put the fundamental rights of the human person at risk. it is good to have a clause calling for us to come back in three years' time to assess the system which we have now approved, and it is good to have the requirement for transparency and the public nature of the assessment which the european commission is to present. i hope that this evaluation, which will be provided by commissioner frattini, will help us to make a rigorous assessment of the effectiveness of the adoption of these instruments.
madam president, in the committee on transport and tourism it was possible to reach a compromise on the subject under discussion, which was well expressed in the text of amendment no 49. disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility have the same rights as other citizens to free movement, freedom of choice and non-discrimination. these rights apply to air transport as well as to other areas of human life. all the following is a consequence of this generous principle and we welcome it. it has been extended from the initial concept to include not only persons with reduced mobility but also other persons with physical or mental disabilities, which is worth noting. this broad concept may be more demanding for operators or may involve higher costs, but the truth is that the problem is not, and cannot be, with people, but rather with the need to ensure accessibility of infrastructure, modes of transport and services, for which fair and equitable solutions must be found. the problem is that, ladies and gentlemen, you cannot remove one barrier by creating another. that is why we congratulate the rapporteur on the commitment shown in adopting the amendments, particularly those relating to the division of responsibilities between airports and airlines, recognising the cases where airlines already offer this service with a high quality, often differentiating it from competitors and without additional burdens. madam president, just two final notes. one to highlight the detail used in drafting the proposal the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of workers from discrimination. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams was signed on the same day as the airport services agreement signed with ryanair on the same day. in short, it is a good report, and i congratulate mr evans and all those who have contributed to the excellent compromise reached.
we welcome the compromise reached and hope that it will not be altered to ensure that the regions affected by the statistical effect retain the same treatment as regards state aid as that applied to the regions in the convergence objective, the same being proposed for the outermost regions. as stated in the report, cohesion policies and state aid policies are complementary. state aid is a fundamental instrument of the states to promote their regional development and real convergence between the different countries of the european union. state aid is an important lever for promoting public investment, sustainable economic development, in particular by ensuring public services in the less-favoured regions. in addition, the existence of public services of a high quality is essential to achieve the objective of social, economic and territorial cohesion. each state should define its public sectors and services, their appropriate financing and organisation, and in no case should they fall within the scope of the application of state aid rules. states, even in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, should be able to use this instrument to respond appropriately to the specific development needs of their less-favoured regions. competition in international trade is putting increasing pressure on the less favoured regions. this competition causes the closure and relocation of businesses and the increase in unemployment with a serious impact on the development of many regions, particularly in countries like portugal, and we therefore reaffirm once again that the states, through state aid, among other fundamental measures, have a duty to intervene in these situations, in particular with the support of the european union. we also believe that the obligation to maintain investment in the regions for a minimum period of five years is grossly inadequate and should be increased. it is necessary to ensure that state aid does not promote the relocation of undertakings, in whole or in part, within or outside the european union. we believe that state aid to enterprises should be subject to a long-term commitment to the duration of the investment, the number of jobs created and the guarantee of workers' rights, requiring its reimbursement in the event of non-compliance. we also believe that the relative prosperity of regions and, consequently, their eligibility for aid should be based on gdp per head. if new indicators are to be integrated, we consider the level of qualifications of the population to be relevant. here are some of the proposals we put forward.
state aid is generally seen as a negative element from the point of view of competition. however, the treaty on european union recognises that such aid is acceptable when it is intended to contribute, for example, to the economic development of regions where the standard of living is well below the european average. the principle that active public policies are justified when the pursuit of greater social cohesion is at stake is thus enshrined. the free functioning of the market contains many positive elements for the growth of the economy, but it does not in itself ensure development. in terms of regional policy, this type of state aid therefore emerges as an instrument which can be important for supporting the most disadvantaged regions. in this case, state aid is complementary to regional policy and must be linked to it, and in this context i support the rapporteur in that the regions which have suffered from the statistical effect should be subject to the same system as the regions in the convergence objective. another problem is that of globalisation, which has brought a new issue to the european union and to which i have not tired of drawing attention, and which concerns the possible disappearance of the industrial map of regions and sectors whose economic basis is manufacturing production. to stem this tide, the european union has put forward the idea of the globalisation adjustment fund. i support the initiative, but this fund should be used only in regions which, in view of foreseeable developments, present a high social risk. the fund must therefore be very selective, exceptional in its application, and focus on regions with three fundamental and simultaneous characteristics: high incidence of population concentration, high unemployment rate and high sectoral specialisation.
the preparations for this council demonstrate the seriousness of the situation in the european union and the crisis to which the increasingly neoliberal policies, serving the interests of the economic and financial groups of the most powerful countries, have led. the solidarity of the richer countries is getting weaker. the very principles of the treaty on economic and social cohesion are being completely trampled underfoot. the latest enlargements of the european union have been achieved without new financial means and are preparing to make the situation worse with further cuts proposed by the british presidency for the new member states and for cohesion countries such as portugal. the budgetary crisis is merely an expression of the serious malaise in the european union, which has been aggravated by the fundamentalism of the monetary guidelines of the ecb and the stability pact, and which is being deepened by the restrictions they impose on the community budget. in the meantime, new priorities contained in the european constitution, which has now been rejected - the militarisation of the eu, so-called internal security and immigration control, competition policies - are being reinforced, which will tend to channel financial resources to the priorities of the economically more developed countries and their economic and financial groups, at the expense of social, environmental, cohesion and development aid needs.
the financial framework for 2007-13 is the european council's 'hot plate'. but it's not the only one on the menu: the liberalization of services and the so-called "fight against terrorism" are also there. the british presidency has been the champion of the interests of the eu's most economically developed countries, presenting a proposal that seeks to lower the bar once again and overcome contradictions between them, and this has increased the pressure for an agreement as soon as possible. unice (the big employers' association in europe) comes to tell you that they understand each other. while warning of the danger of losing the eu's 'credibility', it presents its specifications: an agreement on the financial perspective, reaffirming that it 'must be an instrument at the service of the lisbon strategy'; the rapid establishment of the internal market for services (it is also eloquent that, in order to justify the liberalisation of services, unice argues that this is an 'essential element of the lisbon strategy', a 'requirement of the treaties', supported by the decisions of the european court of justice - later they 'sell' that the so-called 'european constitution' has nothing to do with it...); and the liberalisation of international trade within the framework of the wto. that is, the eu without a mask!
in writing. we regret that the proposal to reject this directive on the retention of electronic communications data, which we support, was rejected by the majority of the european parliament. it is recalled that a similar proposal was previously rejected by the european parliament and did not obtain the necessary majority in the council for its approval, when it required a unanimous decision. however, the current proposal for a directive (presented by the european commission on the initiative of the united kingdom) took only three months to be adopted by a majority of meps and a qualified majority in the council. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. we consider this to be an unacceptable proposal - one more - which is part of the current security offensive which is attacking the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens under the pretext of the so-called 'fight against terrorism'. what is intended is to "legalize" the illegality. the aim is to extend the collection and storage of information (telephone communications, e-mail, internet, etc.) for a period of up to two years, which can be extended, in order, among other things, to 'prevent' infringements. a flexibility clause is included which will allow for the almost indiscriminate collection of electronic information. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. before we discuss the report, it should be noted that the fact that the subject in question is the subject of a wide-ranging debate is a first positive sign which should be highlighted. it is a sign, in my view, that europe is aware, is awake, to the risks that an overly security-oriented attitude can bring with it in the matter of individual freedoms. in the report we adopted, i did not see any security issues or any abandonment of the fundamental principles of respect for and defence of the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. the report we have adopted recognizes the need to strengthen the means available to combat crime, particularly in view of the seriousness of certain types of crime - terrorism being the most prominent of these, of course - and the use of new technological means for the practice of these criminal activities. there is, however, one concern which was expressed in the debate and in the document adopted, and which should be highlighted here. the admission of the possibilities provided for in this report is compatible only with a reinforced monitoring of their use. parliament cannot ignore the follow-up to the directive in question. what we passed today was to protect citizens from criminals and cannot be used for any other purpose.

detainees without judicial protection. i therefore commend commissioner frattini for the clarity of his position. the european union, which has created and is consolidating the area of freedom, on behalf of the gue/ngl group, i would like to reiterate what has already been stressed in the debate in the committee, namely the insufficiency of the amount of funds included in the european commission's proposal, in view of the objectives set out in this regulation - the financing of control and enforcement measures, conservation measures, data collection and improvement of scientific advice, so-called governance, international relations and the law of the sea. when it is necessary to significantly increase the financial resources of this important instrument of the common fisheries policy, in view of the enlargement of the european union and the greater ambition of the objectives set, this is not the case. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european parliament's budget for 2007-2013 is a step in the right direction. we have therefore tabled an amendment which states that the overall financial envelope for fisheries, in particular for this proposal for a regulation, is clearly insufficient to meet the economic and social crisis facing the sector and the needs arising from the 2002 revision of the common fisheries policy, and we are calling for the fisheries sector to be provided with the appropriate financial means. furthermore, because we consider it essential that fishermen participate in the definition and implementation of the common fisheries policy at its various levels, we have also put forward a proposal to support the creation or promotion of associations representing small-scale coastal fishing, by far the most important sector in the sector, and to support their participation in decision-making processes, in particular in regional advisory councils. finally, it should be noted that the regulation is still imbued with the idea that the conservation of fisheries resources is achieved solely by reducing fishing activity at the level of the european union, while other determining factors are ignored. we believe that the main objective should be to promote the modernization and sustainable development of the sector, while respecting the balance of fisheries resources, in order to guarantee the public supply of fish, to maintain jobs and to improve the living and working conditions of fishermen.

to the way it manages and distributes its budget in this way. however, in order to move forward with a sound, conscious and sustained strategy, we need to have tools at our disposal that allow us to policy and complements the proposal for a council regulation on the european fisheries fund, which we had the opportunity to discuss here a few months ago. as i said at the time of the eff, it seems appropriations earmarked. in view of the more ambitious and far-reaching tasks which have been created by the enlargement of the union, i think it is inappropriate to apply reductions of 6.3% to this member of the commission. mr president, first of all i would like to say that funding has in fact been increased under this instrument. this is due to a number of reasons: enlargement, new technologies, broader scope of data, the new control agencies and the establishment of the regional advisory councils. on the latter point, i wish to say, as i said before, that the commission is willing to consider the funding of the regional advisory councils during the review to be undertaken after the third year of their operation. with regard to the extent of the funds, were more funds to be made available the commission would surely not complain. however, in reality we will hopefully have a 150% increase in control and enforcement, a 160% increase in data collection and scientific advice, a 110% increase in governance and a 120% increase in international relations. if all goes well, there will be an overall increase of 130% if one compares the 2000-2006 financial period and the 2007-2013 financial period. if there is a reduction, we have a cushion to some extent, so we do not have to deduct from any one specific heading. if there is going to be a drastic cut, all headings will be affected linearly. we will know hopefully before the end of the week what the situation is going to be. so far, from the indications we have, the cuts envisaged under the financial perspective as regards fisheries are relatively small, especially in the second instrument, and hopefully it will stay that way. on the international agreements, the commission believes that the proposal strikes the balance between internal and external policies, between international agreements and conservation, control and governance. at this juncture i wish to highlight that the allocations to the various areas are only indicative and based on current forecasts. adjustments for each programme will in any case be submitted and adopted every year in the annual budgetary procedure. i would like to pick up on the point made by mrs attwooll with regard to amendment 16. since these are commercial relationships, the monies often go directly to the treasury budget as part of the budget of the state. however, we intend to strengthen our dialogue with the commission’s development services, to enhance the effectiveness of these monies in these countries’ general development objectives, in particular in the fisheries sector. with particular reference to the fisheries partnership agreements, i need to underline that each fisheries partnership agreement contains provisions on the payment of funds under the agreement, as well as on the use of the financial share foreseen for the fisheries policy of the third country. on the basis of indicators and benchmarks, as i have said before, both parties will jointly evaluate the results of this policy and where appropriate will make the necessary adjustments. with regard to the remarks made by mr clark, i cannot agree with his assertions. the lower stocks of fish are the result of year upon year of uncontrolled over-fishing and not of the common fisheries policy. that policy, through its measures, seeks to address the need for balance between the availability of stocks and the fleets that target them. finally, the point on coastal fisheries and small-scale fisheries is better addressed under the european fisheries fund, which will hopefully be adopted early in 2006.
the commission's proposal for a regulation on the conservation of fishery resources in the north sea is based on the principle of the conservation of fishery resources in the north sea. in an excellent thesis on the workings of the confraria de cangas in galicia, dora jesus noted that the assumption of exclusive fishing rights in a given area for a given fishing community, i.e. the assumption of rights and duties relating to the ownership of natural resources, coupled with primary control and penalty systems managed by the brotherhood itself, allowed the recovery of the hornet and its ecologically and economically sustainable exploitation in the area under the control of that brotherhood. unfortunately, the european union has opted for a different policy, namely a maximum of dissociation between fishing rights, the allocation of which is considered to be an exclusive european competence and which for some species are determined for virtually the whole of the european marine area, and the control and penalty systems left almost entirely to the discretion of each individual. the amount and the share rates proposed by the european commission to support investment in fisheries control by member states, reduced to €32 million in 2006, are a small amount compared to the responsibilities assigned to some regions and some member states. in addition, there is no community contribution to the implementation of the controls and monitoring of the cfp. let me remind you in this context that, for example, portugal, despite having just over 2% of the european population, has more than 50% of the area of the european exclusive economic zones and that the autonomous region of the azores alone has an eez larger than that of any member state, despite having only 250 000 inhabitants. as a result of this situation, and since access to azorean waters was liberalised on 1 august 2004, and although the presence of many dozens of foreign vessels in this eez has already been recorded by vms, sometimes reaching more than two dozen at a time, only one inspection has been carried out between them, in stark contrast to the numerous inspections carried out on land, or at short distances, on the azorean small-scale fleet by regional, national and community authorities. in the absence of any vms control system and with the vms system operating extremely poorly, owing to some exceptions to fundamental aspects of its operation, with the classical high seas control system acting only weakly and ineffectively, it continues, particularly in the poorest and most peripheral areas of europe such as those just mentioned, without effective protection, either against fishing by unregistered vessels or even against vessels legally registered. at a conference on european maritime policy and strategy held last week by the european socialist party in ponta delgada, we learned that about 150 different species of coral have recently been recorded in the azores sea, several of them endemic and some with life spans of up to thousands of years. among them are dense forests of black coral, some more than six feet [2 m] high. the heritage value of these corals and other deep-sea organisms, as well as their biotechnological potential, is admittedly enormous. it is true that trawling and bottom trawling have finally been banned in this area, but the question is whether these bans are effective when the community's efforts and guarantee to monitor, control and protect these european treasures are practically nil. the announcement of the european commission's proposal for a marine strategy gave us all hope that we would see this situation changed, but it was with great disappointment that we found that this proposal envisages no community funding, that is to say, it will insist on the same logic as the present one, whereby in europe, only the use of marine resources is for everyone, the responsibilities for protection are exclusively for the people who live there. in the field of maritime safety and nature protection, we are now unfortunately faced with a major tragedy in the azores, with the shipwreck of a large container ship with a flag of convenience on a quay classified as a site of community interest integrated into the natura 2000 network, carrying some containers with a dangerous chemical load. despite the various legislative packages, the erika, the prestige, and the creation of the european maritime safety agency, the truth is that there is still no european response capacity, both to these disasters and to those resulting from unsustainable fishing. for these reasons we believe that it is urgent to set up a genuine european coastguard, where fisheries control activities are linked to other control operations at sea and where fishing is open to the whole of the european fleet - an effective, modern and harmonised system of controls and sanctions. the liberalisation of access to waters without these requirements being met is absolutely unacceptable and can only result in the rapid deterioration of europe's marine natural heritage.
member of the commission. mr president, i wish to thank the rapporteur and the committee on fisheries for its report on this proposal from the commission. i am pleased to note that the committee has given a favourable assessment to this scheme, which is aimed at improving the member states’ control capabilities, and that it fully supports the extension of its validity for a further year. i also note that the committee is favourable to financing, under the community budget, administrative arrangements with the joint research centre with a view to developing new technologies in the area of control, and to the financing of studies on control-related areas, to be carried out at the commission’s initiative. the committee has, however, tabled seven amendments to the proposal. i regret that it is very difficult to accept any of the amendments, mainly for formal reasons, which i would like to explain. amendment 2 proposes a change to the time limit for the presentation of national programmes. we would like to keep the existing date of 31 january, as the submission of requests early on in the year will allow the commission to adopt a decision granting the financial contribution in the first semester. this will, in turn, ease the planning requirements for national administrations. it should also be noted that the national administrations are already fully aware of this time limit. on amendment 3 and the related amendments 1 and 6, the commission shares the committee’s view that these expenses should be financed under a different heading. this can be done through a budgetary arrangement. however, it is not possible to finance these two new actions if they were not foreseen in the legal text. the commission deems that this proposal is the appropriate legal text to introduce them and cannot, therefore, accept these amendments. in amendment 4, the committee asks the commission to establish criteria in order to allocate grants when the amount of request exceeds the available appropriations. the commission’s policy is to allocate grants only when the need for investment has been proven, namely through the national report on control activities, irrespective of the overall amount requested. establishing criteria will introduce some rigidity to the selection of projects and could entail a risk that grants will be given for projects that are not of general interest. this amendment cannot, therefore, be accepted. amendment 5 refers to the contribution rate for the most expensive items, i.e. patrol vessels and aircraft. increasing the rate to up to 75% of the eligible expenditure will reduce appropriations for other actions. the commission considers a rate not exceeding 50% to be appropriate, as a general rule, for all kinds of investment. it cannot, therefore, accept this amendment. finally, the commission cannot accept 7, since at the end of 2006 most of the projects will not yet have been completed, meaning a report on the decision will be of little use. i should like to recall that the commission will present a report on this decision to the european parliament by 30 june 2008 at the latest. concerning mr morillon’s oral question to the commission, may i say that i fully share the view that sanctions, including in the fisheries sector, must be proportionate to the seriousness of the offences committed. they must also effectively discourage any further infringement of the same nature. moreover, sanctions should be non-discriminatory between nationals and non-nationals of member states. we cannot achieve compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy without creating a level playing field across the european union for all fishermen.with a view to promoting transparency and to encouraging the application of adequate and dissuasive sanctions against those who commit serious infringements, the commission publishes an annual communication on serious infringements to the rules of the community fisheries policy. the commission has published four of these communications so far. in its comments on the tables annexed to the communications, the commission stressed the need to reduce existing disparities regarding the level of sanctions imposed across the community. on the same communications, the commission has also declared its preference for the use of administrative procedures and sanctions when dealing with breaches of the common fisheries policy rules, since they are imposed in a swifter manner and are more effective. the commission believes that a sanction, such as the suspension of an authorisation to fish, decided by the administrative authority and entering into force immediately, subject to the possibility of a judicial review, is a stronger deterrent. the choice, however, between a penal or administrative procedure lies with the member state. in conformity with article 25(4) of council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002, the basic regulation on the cfp, the commission intends to present in due time a proposal aimed at harmonising at community level sanctions for serious infringements.
the control of fishing activities is an important pillar for the sustainability of the fisheries sector and, in view of the need to recover certain endangered fish stocks, it is urgent to continue to support member states in order to enable them to exercise their obligation to control, monitor and inspect fishing activities in their areas of jurisdiction. the result of strategic reflection dates back to 2001, when control strategies were already one of the main focuses of the green paper of that year. the creation of a community fisheries control agency in april 2005 could, i believe, herald the beginning of a new era. although it organizes and coordinates the control and inspection activities of the various member states, the institution does not eliminate the powers and obligations of those states. at a time when a decision on the financial perspective and the new community framework for the period 2007-2013 is still pending, these amounts are still unknown and it is therefore appropriate to consider the extension of decision 465/2004 at this stage. i would like to congratulate my compatriot paulo casaca on his good work as rapporteur for this document. despite what the commissioner has said, i believe that the adjustments made to the original text are appropriate and make the document more balanced and more in line with its real purpose. however, and although the adoption of the document deserves my full and unequivocal support, i would like to draw attention once again to the fact that the member states are still struggling with immense financial difficulties to be able to implement all the desired measures. the recent 2003 european commission communication and the reports of non-compliance with the cfp are proof that there is still much to be done. in order to ensure that member states comply with their obligations under the rules of the common fisheries policy, it is therefore absolutely necessary that the european commission continue to support their investments in the field of control and surveillance.

in writing. according to the ngos, this is the first specific regulatory instrument at community level concerning disabled people, who number approximately 50 million in the european union. the aim is to ensure that transport for disabled people (as proposed by the european parliament) and for people with reduced mobility due to any other factor have access to air transport. this regulation lays down rules for the protection and assistance of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility travelling by air, both to protect them from discrimination and to ensure that they receive assistance at airports of embarkation, transit and arrival, which should be provided at no additional cost to the passenger. among other examples, a set of measures is also provided to adequately inform disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility about their rights. the need for training of ground and flight personnel, as well as the preparation of infrastructure and aircraft to provide this service is pointed out. the initiative we voted for.

in writing. we voted in favour of this fisheries protocol because it guarantees fishing opportunities off the seychelles to the various fleets of the member states operating in these waters until 17 january 2011, in particular to five portuguese surface longliners. the renewal of this fisheries protocol is important to ensure the survival of the member states' long-distance fishing fleets, a segment of the fleet which has been particularly affected by the crisis in the fisheries sector in recent years. the portuguese case is an example of this, where the number of vessels has been reduced from year to year. however, even taking into account that this new protocol is for six years, as well as the levels of utilization of the fishing opportunities offered, we cannot fail to note the reduction in the number of surface longliners used and an increase in the cost of licences - which we do not consider justified - which implies higher costs for armaments, with the corresponding loss of profitability. it should be noted that the proposed increase in the cost of licences is € 1,000 for surface longliners with more than 150 grt and € 750 for surface longliners with less than 150 grt.

in writing. i would like to start by welcoming the initiative taken by the ep to implement this report, as i consider the role of women in this and other sectors to be fundamental to the sustained development of the economic and social fabric of the eu. in the specific case of this report, the proposals to the european commission on gender equality and equal rights at work seem to me to be correct. support for the creation of networks of women in the fisheries sector within the eu, as well as their inclusion in coastal action groups and the new regional advisory councils, should be taken into account. i also welcome the approach to the ec to ensure specific support to support the set of initiatives proposed in mrs attwooll's report.
in writing. women in the fishing industry and in fishing communities play a role very similar to that of women in farming communities, i.e. supporting the back-up activities related to catching - often unpaid work - in addition to domestic activities, with health risks and no guarantee of social protection. women in the catching industry represent less than 3% of the workforce. on the contrary, in the processing or aquaculture sector they take the largest weight in the workforce, showing the progressive feminization of the workforce. gender issues remain a backdrop in the sector and the participation of women in fisheries organisations and associations is very low. in this regard, we supported the creation of networks and associations of women in the fisheries sector at local and national level, with community support, in order to: give greater visibility to the role of women in this sector; increase women's participation in the decision-making processes of the common fisheries policy; and draw attention to the need to preserve fisheries as an economic, social and cultural activity fundamental to the development of fishing communities in different countries.
author. – mr president, as head of the european union election observation mission in ethiopia, i helped to persuade ethiopian opposition leaders not to boycott the may elections, assuring them that the world and the european union in particular were watching. they felt that the electoral process had been set up by the regime not to achieve democracy but to fool the international community. despite being elected by the ethiopian people, they are now in jail. they have been on hunger strike since 28 november, face a possible death penalty, and yet are neglected by european leaders. this is in spite of the fact that, in early september, i warned european governments, the commission, the us government and the un secretary-general that the regime might be planning the selective repression of ethiopian opposition leaders. how could european governments fail so miserably those who trusted the european union, those who fought and continue to fight for democracy in ethiopia? how could european and american leaders fail so miserably the ethiopian people and such an important country: the second most populous in africa and the headquarters of the african union? what message are they sending to all africans? how can the un secretary-general and the security council continue to turn a blind eye to massive human rights violations inside ethiopia, forgetting how this could lead to another devastating war with neighbouring eritrea? how can mr blair, the british prime minister and president-in-office of the european council, continue to allow in his commission for africa mr meles zenawi, who is keeping imprisoned and threatening with the death penalty the elected opposition leaders, journalists, human rights and development campaigners and even the ethiopian representatives of the global call to action against poverty? this is the third resolution since july in which the european parliament, across all political groups, has expressed its deep concern about the situation in ethiopia. how can european leaders fail to act upon repeated appeals from this parliament when the lives of ethiopian prisoners are at stake? (applause)
